attributes.name: cost_currency_code
attributes.description: ISO 4217 three-letter currency code for the pairing cost (e.g., USD, EUR, GBP).

attributes.name: created_timestamp
attributes.description: Date and time when this pairing record was first created in the system. Audit field for record creation tracking.
attributes.references: AIMS Crew Management System - Audit Standards

attributes.name: crew_position
attributes.description: The crew position or role this pairing is designed for (captain, first officer, flight attendant, purser, relief pilot). Determines qualification and legality requirements.

attributes.name: deadhead_segments
attributes.description: Count of deadhead (non-revenue positioning) segments in this pairing where crew travel as passengers to reposition for operational duty.
attributes.references: AIMS Crew Management System - Pairing Module

attributes.name: effective_end_date
attributes.description: The last date this pairing is valid for crew assignment. End of the pairing's operational window. Nullable for open-ended pairings.
attributes.references: AIMS Crew Management System - Pairing Module

attributes.name: effective_start_date
attributes.description: The first date this pairing is valid and available for crew assignment. Start of the pairing's operational window.
attributes.references: AIMS Crew Management System - Pairing Module

attributes.name: end_datetime
attributes.description: The scheduled date and time when the pairing ends (crew release time at base). Represents the end of the last duty period.
attributes.references: AIMS Crew Management System - Pairing Module

attributes.name: fatigue_risk_score
attributes.description: Calculated fatigue risk score for this pairing based on duty patterns, circadian disruption, and rest opportunities. Used in Fatigue Risk Management System (FRMS). Higher scores indicate higher fatigue risk.

attributes.name: hotel_cost
attributes.description: Estimated total hotel accommodation cost for all layovers in this pairing. Used for pairing cost calculation.
attributes.references: AIMS Crew Management System - Pairing Optimizer

attributes.name: international_flag
attributes.description: Indicates whether this pairing includes any international (cross-border) flight legs. True if any leg crosses international boundaries, false if all legs are domestic.

attributes.name: last_modified_timestamp
attributes.description: Date and time when this pairing record was last updated. Audit field for change tracking.
attributes.references: AIMS Crew Management System - Audit Standards

attributes.name: legality_status
attributes.description: Indicates whether this pairing meets all regulatory crew duty and rest requirements (legal), violates regulations (illegal), is under review (pending_review), or has an approved waiver (waiver_approved).

attributes.name: max_duty_period_hours
attributes.description: The longest single duty period (in hours) within this pairing. Used to verify compliance with FAR Part 117 and EASA FTL maximum duty limits.

attributes.name: min_rest_period_hours
attributes.description: The shortest rest period (in hours) within this pairing. Must meet or exceed minimum rest requirements per FAR Part 117 and EASA FTL.

attributes.name: notes
attributes.description: Free-text field for operational notes, special instructions, or comments about this pairing (e.g., special qualifications required, known issues, crew preferences).
attributes.references: AIMS Crew Management System - Pairing Module

attributes.name: number_of_duty_periods
attributes.description: Total count of duty periods in this pairing. A duty period is a continuous block of work time from crew report to crew release, separated by rest periods.

attributes.name: number_of_layovers
attributes.description: Total count of overnight layovers (rest periods away from base) in this pairing. Each layover occurs at an overnight station.
attributes.references: AIMS Crew Management System - Pairing Module

attributes.name: number_of_legs
attributes.description: Total count of flight legs (segments) included in this pairing. Each leg is a single takeoff-to-landing flight.
attributes.references: AIMS Crew Management System - Pairing Module

attributes.name: optimization_run_code
attributes.description: Identifier of the specific optimization run that produced this pairing. Links pairing to the batch optimization process.
attributes.references: AIMS Crew Management System - Pairing Optimizer

attributes.name: optimizer_version
attributes.description: Version identifier of the crew pairing optimizer software that generated this pairing. Used for audit and reproducibility.
attributes.references: AIMS Crew Management System - Pairing Optimizer

attributes.name: overnight_stations
attributes.description: Comma-separated list of IATA airport codes where crew have overnight layovers during this pairing (e.g., 'JFK,LAX,ORD'). Sequence reflects pairing order.

attributes.name: pairing_code
attributes.description: Business identifier for the pairing, externally known code used in crew scheduling and operations. Typically alphanumeric format assigned by the pairing optimizer.
attributes.references: AIMS Crew Management System - Pairing Module

attributes.name: pairing_status
attributes.description: Current lifecycle status of the pairing: draft (under construction), published (available for assignment), assigned (crew assigned), in_progress (currently being flown), completed (finished), cancelled (no longer valid).
attributes.references: AIMS Crew Management System - Pairing Module

attributes.name: pairing_type
attributes.description: Classification of the pairing based on route characteristics: domestic (all legs within one country), international (crosses borders), mixed (combination), reserve (standby duty), training (instructional flights), or positioning (deadhead crew movement).

attributes.name: per_diem_amount
attributes.description: Total per diem allowance payable to crew for this pairing, covering meals and incidental expenses during layovers. Calculated per CBA rules.

attributes.name: premium_pay_flag
attributes.description: Indicates whether this pairing qualifies for premium pay under CBA rules (e.g., due to red-eye flights, long duty periods, or undesirable layovers). True if premium pay applies.

attributes.name: published_timestamp
attributes.description: Date and time when this pairing was published and made available for crew assignment. Nullable if pairing has not yet been published.
attributes.references: AIMS Crew Management System - Pairing Module

attributes.name: red_eye_flag
attributes.description: Indicates whether this pairing includes any red-eye (overnight) flights that operate during typical sleep hours (typically 10 PM to 6 AM). True if any leg is a red-eye flight.

attributes.name: start_datetime
attributes.description: The scheduled date and time when the pairing begins (crew report time at base). Represents the start of the first duty period.
attributes.references: AIMS Crew Management System - Pairing Module

attributes.name: time_away_from_base_hours
attributes.description: Total elapsed time from pairing start to pairing end, representing how long crew are away from their base. Includes duty time, rest time, and layover time. Key quality-of-life metric.

attributes.name: total_block_hours
attributes.description: Total flight time (block hours) accumulated across all legs in this pairing, measured from gate departure (off-blocks) to gate arrival (on-blocks). Used for crew pay and legality checks.

attributes.name: total_credit_hours
attributes.description: Total pay credit hours for this pairing, calculated per collective bargaining agreement rules. May differ from block hours due to minimum guarantees, premiums, and duty rigs.

attributes.name: total_duty_hours
attributes.description: Total duty time across all duty periods in this pairing, from crew report to crew release. Includes flight time, ground time, and pre/post-flight duties. Subject to FAR Part 117 and EASA FTL limits.

attributes.name: total_rest_hours
attributes.description: Total rest time provided across all rest periods in this pairing. Must meet minimum rest requirements per FAR Part 117 and EASA FTL.

products.name: duty_period
products.description: A duty period is a continuous block of time during which a crew member is on duty, bounded by report time and release time. Belongs to a pairing. Captures report time, release time, total duty elapsed time (TDT), flight duty period (FDP) start/end, rest period before and after, duty type (flight duty, ground duty, deadhead, training), and FAR Part 117 / EASA FTL legality status. The atomic unit for fatigue risk and FTL compliance calculations.
products.reference: FAR Part 117 / EASA FTL — Flight Duty Period

attributes.name: duty_period_id
attributes.description: Unique identifier for the duty period. Primary key.

attributes.name: base_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to crew.crew_base. Business justification: Normalize duty_period to reference crew_base by FK. Currently duty_period stores crew_base_code (STRING) as a denormalized reference to the crew's home base for the duty period. Adding crew_base_id FK

attributes.name: duty_cost_centre_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to finance.cost_centre. Business justification: Duty periods drive crew cost allocation for flight-level P&L, activity-based costing, and cost centre reporting. Supports detailed operational cost analysis and variance reporting against budget.

attributes.name: member_id
attributes.description: Reference to the crew member assigned to this duty period.

attributes.name: occurrence_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to safety.occurrence. Business justification: Occurrences happen during specific duty periods. Essential for fatigue analysis, FTL investigation, and causal factor determination. Real business process: occurrence context analysis and fatigue risk

attributes.name: pairing_id
attributes.description: Reference to the pairing that contains this duty period. A pairing is a sequence of duty periods and rest periods assigned to a crew member.

attributes.name: acclimation_status
attributes.description: Indicates whether the crew member is acclimated to the local time zone at duty start. Acclimated means the crew member has been in the time zone for sufficient time per FAR Part 117 definitions. Affects maximum FDP limits.

attributes.name: actual_flag
attributes.description: Indicates whether this duty period was actually operated (True) or was planned but not executed (False). Used for payroll and compliance reporting.

attributes.name: augmented_crew_flag
attributes.description: Indicates whether this duty period involves augmented crew (additional crew members allowing in-flight rest). True if augmented, False otherwise. Affects maximum FDP limits.

attributes.name: block_hours_minutes
attributes.description: Total block time (gate departure to gate arrival) in minutes for all flight segments within this duty period. Null for non-flight duty types.

attributes.name: cancellation_reason_code
attributes.description: Code indicating why the duty period was cancelled if actual_flag is False (e.g., CREW_SICK, AIRCRAFT_MAINTENANCE, WEATHER, SCHEDULE_CHANGE). Null if duty was operated.

attributes.name: created_timestamp
attributes.description: Timestamp when this duty period record was first created in the system.

attributes.name: duty_end_station_code
attributes.description: Three-letter IATA airport code where the duty period ends (release location).

attributes.name: duty_period_number
attributes.description: Sequential number of this duty period within the pairing (1, 2, 3, etc.).

attributes.name: duty_start_station_code
attributes.description: Three-letter IATA airport code where the duty period begins (report location).

attributes.name: duty_type
attributes.description: Classification of the duty period: flight duty (operating flights), ground duty (administrative/ground tasks), deadhead (crew repositioning without revenue duty), training (simulator/classroom), standby (on-call at airport), or reserve (on-call at home/hotel).

attributes.name: easa_ftl_compliant_flag
attributes.business_glossary_term: European Union Aviation Safety Agency (EASA) Flight Time Limitations (FTL) Compliant Flag
attributes.description: Indicates whether this duty period is compliant with EASA FTL regulations. True if compliant, False if violation detected.

attributes.name: far_117_compliant_flag
attributes.business_glossary_term: Federal Aviation Regulation (FAR) Part 117 Compliant Flag
attributes.description: Indicates whether this duty period is compliant with FAA FAR Part 117 flight and duty time limitations. True if compliant, False if violation detected.

attributes.name: fatigue_risk_level
attributes.description: Categorical fatigue risk level derived from the fatigue risk score: low (acceptable), moderate (monitor), high (mitigate), critical (unacceptable).

attributes.name: fatigue_risk_score
attributes.description: Calculated fatigue risk score for this duty period based on biomathematical fatigue models (e.g., SAFTE-FAST, Boeing Alertness Model). Higher scores indicate higher fatigue risk. Scale typically 0-100.

attributes.name: fdp_elapsed_time_minutes
attributes.business_glossary_term: Flight Duty Period (FDP) Elapsed Time in Minutes
attributes.description: Total elapsed time in minutes from FDP start to FDP end. Critical for FAR Part 117 and EASA FTL maximum FDP limit checks. Null for non-flight duty types.

attributes.name: fdp_end_time
attributes.description: Timestamp marking the end of the flight duty period, which ends when the aircraft finally comes to rest and the engines are shut down at the last flight segment. Null for non-flight duty types.

attributes.name: fdp_start_time
attributes.description: Timestamp marking the start of the flight duty period, which begins when a crew member is required to report for duty with the intention of conducting a flight. Null for non-flight duty types.

attributes.name: flight_segments_count
attributes.description: Number of flight segments (takeoff and landing cycles) operated during this duty period. Used for fatigue risk assessment. Null for non-flight duty types.

attributes.name: last_modified_timestamp
attributes.description: Timestamp when this duty period record was last modified in the system.

attributes.name: legality_status
attributes.description: Overall legality status of the duty period considering all applicable regulations (FAR Part 117, EASA FTL, company policies). Legal means all checks passed; illegal means one or more violations detected; waiver_granted means a regulatory waiver was approved; under_review means legality is being assessed.

attributes.name: legality_violation_codes
attributes.description: Comma-separated list of violation codes if the duty period is illegal (e.g., MAX_FDP_EXCEEDED, INSUFFICIENT_REST, MAX_DUTY_EXCEEDED). Null if legal.

attributes.name: release_time
attributes.description: Timestamp when the crew member is released from duty. Marks the end of the duty period.

attributes.name: report_time
attributes.description: Timestamp when the crew member is required to report for duty. Marks the start of the duty period.

attributes.name: rest_period_after_minutes
attributes.business_glossary_term: Rest Period After Duty in Minutes
attributes.description: Duration in minutes of the rest period immediately following this duty period. Used to verify minimum rest requirements per FAR Part 117 and EASA FTL.

attributes.name: rest_period_before_minutes
attributes.business_glossary_term: Rest Period Before Duty in Minutes
attributes.description: Duration in minutes of the rest period immediately preceding this duty period. Used to verify minimum rest requirements per FAR Part 117 and EASA FTL.

attributes.name: scheduled_flag
attributes.description: Indicates whether this duty period was part of the original published schedule (True) or was added/modified after publication (False). Used for operational performance tracking.

attributes.name: source_system
attributes.description: Name of the operational system that originated this duty period record (e.g., AIMS, NetLine/Ops).

attributes.name: split_duty_flag
attributes.description: Indicates whether this duty period qualifies as split duty (duty period interrupted by a rest opportunity). True if split duty, False otherwise. Affects FDP extension calculations.

attributes.name: split_duty_rest_minutes
attributes.business_glossary_term: Split Duty Rest Period in Minutes
attributes.description: Duration in minutes of the rest opportunity during a split duty period. Null if not a split duty. Used to calculate FDP extensions.

attributes.name: time_zone_crossings_count
attributes.description: Number of time zones crossed during this duty period. Used for fatigue risk and circadian disruption assessment.

attributes.name: time_zone_end
attributes.description: IANA time zone identifier for the duty end station (e.g., Europe/London). Used for circadian rhythm and fatigue risk calculations.

attributes.name: time_zone_start
attributes.description: IANA time zone identifier for the duty start station (e.g., America/New_York). Used for circadian rhythm and fatigue risk calculations.

attributes.name: total_duty_elapsed_time_minutes
attributes.business_glossary_term: Total Duty Elapsed Time (TDT) in Minutes
attributes.description: Total elapsed time in minutes from report time to release time. Used for FAR Part 117 and EASA FTL compliance calculations.

products.name: roster
products.description: The published monthly crew roster — the assignment of pairings, training events, days off, standby duties, and leave to individual crew members for a bid period. Captures crew member, bid period (month/year), roster publication date, roster version, total credited block hours, total duty days, days off count, reserve days count, roster status (draft, published, revised, frozen), and PBS award reference (if applicable). The SSOT for what each crew member is scheduled to do in a given month. Supports roster comparison (planned vs actual), crew pay calculation inputs, and union compliance verification. Aligns with AIMS rostering module.
products.reference: AIMS Crew Management — Rostering Module

attributes.name: approval_status

attributes.name: effective_end_date

attributes.name: effective_start_date

attributes.name: last_modified_timestamp
attributes.description: Timestamp when this roster record was last modified or updated.

attributes.description: Number of approved leave days (vacation, sick leave, personal leave) included in this roster period.

attributes.name: legality_check_status

attributes.name: legality_check_timestamp

attributes.name: notes

attributes.name: pbs_award_reference

attributes.name: publication_date
attributes.description: The date on which this roster version was officially published to the crew member.

attributes.name: reserve_days_count

attributes.name: roster_source

attributes.name: total_credited_block_hours
attributes.description: Total block hours (gate-to-gate flight time) credited to the crew member for this roster period. Used for pay calculation and regulatory compliance.

attributes.name: total_duty_days

attributes.name: total_duty_hours

attributes.name: total_flight_duty_periods

attributes.name: training_events_count

attributes.name: union_compliance_flag

products.name: roster_activity
products.description: Individual activity line items within a crew roster — each row represents one scheduled activity assigned to a crew member within a bid period. Activity types include: pairing, training, standby (airport or home reserve), day off, deadhead, leave, and ground duty. Captures activity type, start/end datetime, station, pairing reference (if applicable), activity status (scheduled, completed, cancelled, swapped), credit hours, and swap metadata (requesting/receiving crew, approval status) for traded activities. For standby-type activities: additionally captures standby type (airport/home), contact window, activation status, activation time, and triggered flight assignment. Enables day-by-day crew schedule visibility, reserve pool management, roster change audit trail, and IROP crew recovery tracking.
products.reference: AIMS Crew Management — Roster Activity

attributes.name: duty_hours

attributes.name: fatigue_risk_score

products.name: ftl_legality_check
products.description: Unified crew fitness-to-operate assessment records encompassing both regulatory FTL/FDP legality checks (FAR Part 117, EASA FTL) and biomathematical fatigue risk model assessments (SAFE, FAID, FRMS). Each record captures: check timestamp, crew member, duty period or pairing evaluated, assessment method (regulatory_rule or biomathematical_model), regulation/model applied, check trigger (pre-assignment, pre-departure, post-duty, IROP extension), cumulative flight time windows (28-day, 365-day), FDP limit and actual FDP, rest compliance status, fatigue score and risk band (for model-based), mitigations applied, approving authority, and overall fitness result (legal/illegal/waiver/elevated-risk). The SSOT for crew legality and fatigue risk audit trail. Supports SMS, FRMS (ICAO Doc 9966), and regulatory compliance.

products.name: maintenance_authorization
products.description: This association product represents the regulatory authorization relationship between crew members holding maintenance certifications and Part-145 Approved Maintenance Organisations. It captures the authorization scope, validity periods, and recency status for crew-technicians (pilot-engineers, A&P holders) authorized to perform maintenance activities at specific AMOs. Each record links one crew member to one approved maintenance organisation with attributes that exist only in the context of this regulatory authorization relationship.. Existence Justification: In aviation operations, crew members with maintenance certifications (pilot-engineers, A&P mechanics) can hold authorizations at multiple Part-145 approved maintenance organisations simultaneously (e.g., authorized at home base maintenance, multiple line stations, and contracted MRO facilities). Conversely, each maintenance organisation authorizes multiple crew-technicians to perform work within specific scopes. The business actively manages these authorizations with validity periods, scope definitions, and recency tracking as a regulatory compliance requirement.

products.name: operational_qualification
products.description: This association product represents the qualification relationship between crew members and operational approvals. It captures the specific authorization of individual crew members to operate under particular operational approvals (ETOPS, CAT II/III, RNP-AR, RVSM, etc.). Each record links one crew member to one operational approval with qualification-specific attributes including qualification date, expiry, training completion, check dates, and approval status that exist only in the context of this crew-approval relationship.. Existence Justification: In airline operations, crew members must hold specific operational qualifications to operate flights under various regulatory approvals (ETOPS, CAT II/III, RNP-AR, RVSM, etc.). A single crew member typically holds multiple operational approvals (e.g., a captain may be ETOPS-qualified, CAT III-qualified, and RNP-AR qualified), and each operational approval is held by multiple crew members across the airline's crew base. The airline actively manages these qualifications through training programs, proficiency checks, and expiry tracking to ensure regulatory compliance and operational capability.

attributes.name: requesting_crew_base_code
attributes.description: Three-letter IATA code of the crew base for the requesting crew member.

attributes.name: requires_qualification_check
attributes.description: Indicates whether the swap requires validation of crew qualifications, type ratings, and recency requirements.

attributes.name: submission_timestamp
attributes.description: Date and time when the swap request was formally submitted for approval.

attributes.name: swap_type
attributes.description: Type of swap being requested: pairing (full sequence), trip, duty period, single leg, reserve day, or day off.

attributes.name: system_generated_flag
attributes.description: Indicates whether the swap request was automatically generated by the system (true) or manually created by a crew member (false).

attributes.name: target_crew_base_code
attributes.description: Three-letter IATA code of the crew base for the target crew member.

attributes.name: target_response
attributes.description: Response from the target crew member regarding the swap request.

attributes.name: target_response_timestamp
attributes.description: Date and time when the target crew member responded to the swap request.

attributes.name: counterpart_swap_request_id
attributes.description: Self-referencing FK on swap_request (counterpart_swap_request_id)

domains.name: fleet
domains.description: Single source of truth for aircraft and fleet asset master data including aircraft registration, tail numbers, ICAO/IATA type designators, configuration (cabin layout, seat maps), seating capacity, ownership (owned, wet lease, dry lease, ACMI), APU details, ETOPS certification status, MEL applicability, utilization, block hours, cycles, and fleet planning. Owns the physical asset registry referenced by all other operational domains.
domains.references: ICAO Annex 8, FAA Part 91, Aircraft Registration

products.name: aircraft
products.description: Core master record for every physical aircraft asset in the airline's fleet — the Single Source of Truth for aircraft identity referenced by all operational domains. Captures tail number (registration mark), ICAO/IATA type designator, MSN (Manufacturer Serial Number), line number, aircraft family and variant, current operational status (active, stored, parked, retired, wet-lease-out), ownership category (owned, finance-lease, dry-lease, wet-lease-in, ACMI), lessor/owner reference, delivery date, retirement date, country of registration, certificate of registration number, certificate of airworthiness number, airworthiness category, noise chapter classification, ETOPS certification status and minutes rating, RVSM approval, CAT III ILS approval, and current base station. Following merge of aircraft_registration, also holds regulatory registration details including registering authority, registration date/expiry, and registered owner/operator.
products.reference: ICAO Aircraft Register / IATA Aircraft Type Designator

attributes.name: aircraft_id
attributes.description: Unique system identifier for the aircraft asset. Primary key for the aircraft master record.

attributes.name: aircraft_type_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to fleet.aircraft_type. Business justification: Every aircraft is of a specific type. Aircraft currently denormalizes type-level attributes (icao_type_designator, iata_type_code, aircraft_family, aircraft_variant, manufacturer) that belong in aircr

attributes.name: base_station_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to airport.station. Business justification: Aircraft home base assignment drives crew rostering, maintenance scheduling, and fleet deployment planning. Essential for operational planning and cost allocation. Replaces denormalized base_station_c

attributes.name: lease_contract_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to finance.lease_contract. Business justification: Aircraft leasing is core to airline fleet financing. IFRS16 requires tracking right-of-use assets and lease liabilities by specific aircraft. Finance must link lease contracts to aircraft for lease ac

attributes.name: lessor_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to fleet.lessor. Business justification: aircraft has denormalized lessor_name (STRING) attribute. For leased aircraft, the lessor is a critical operational reference. The lessor product exists in fleet domain as the authoritative master. Th

attributes.name: operating_certificate_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to compliance.operating_certificate. Business justification: Aircraft operate under specific operating certificates that authorize commercial service. Essential for airworthiness compliance tracking, operational authorization verification, and regulatory audit

attributes.name: primary_maintenance_engineer_employee_id
attributes.business_glossary_term: Primary Maintenance Engineer Employee Id (Foreign Key)
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to workforce.employee. Business justification: Airlines assign dedicated maintenance engineers to each aircraft for regulatory accountability, airworthiness oversight, and maintenance program compliance tracking. Required for CAMO audit trail and

attributes.name: airworthiness_category
attributes.description: The category of airworthiness certificate issued. Standard = normal commercial operations; Restricted = limited operations; Limited = special purpose; Experimental = testing; Provisional = pre-certification.

attributes.name: apu_manufacturer
attributes.description: The manufacturer of the Auxiliary Power Unit installed on the aircraft (e.g., Honeywell, Pratt & Whitney, Hamilton Sundstrand).

attributes.name: apu_model
attributes.description: The specific model designation of the Auxiliary Power Unit installed on the aircraft.

attributes.name: cabin_configuration_code
attributes.description: Internal code identifying the specific cabin layout and seat map configuration installed on this aircraft (e.g., 2-class, 3-class, high-density). Links to detailed seat map reference data.

attributes.name: cat_iii_ils_approved
attributes.business_glossary_term: Category III Instrument Landing System (CAT III ILS) Approved
attributes.description: Indicates whether the aircraft is equipped and certified for CAT III ILS precision approaches in very low visibility conditions (decision height below 100 feet or no decision height).
attributes.references: ICAO Annex 10 Volume I - Radio Navigation Aids

attributes.name: certificate_of_airworthiness_number
attributes.description: The unique certificate number issued by the civil aviation authority certifying that the aircraft meets all safety and airworthiness standards for flight operations.

attributes.name: certificate_of_registration_number
attributes.description: The unique certificate number issued by the civil aviation authority proving legal registration of the aircraft.

attributes.name: country_of_registration
attributes.description: The three-letter ISO country code of the nation where the aircraft is registered (e.g., USA, GBR, DEU). Determines regulatory jurisdiction.

attributes.name: created_timestamp
attributes.description: The timestamp when this aircraft master record was first created in the system.

attributes.name: delivery_date
attributes.description: The date the aircraft was delivered from the manufacturer to the original customer or the date it entered the current operator's fleet.

attributes.name: etops_certified
attributes.business_glossary_term: Extended-range Twin-engine Operational Performance Standards (ETOPS) Certified
attributes.description: Indicates whether the aircraft holds ETOPS certification allowing extended-range operations over water or remote areas beyond single-engine diversion time limits.
attributes.references: ICAO Annex 6 Part I, FAA 14 CFR Part 121 Appendix P

attributes.name: etops_minutes_rating
attributes.business_glossary_term: Extended-range Twin-engine Operational Performance Standards (ETOPS) Minutes Rating
attributes.description: The maximum diversion time in minutes that the aircraft is certified to fly from the nearest suitable airport under ETOPS rules (e.g., 120, 180, 207, 330 minutes). Null if not ETOPS certified.
attributes.references: ICAO Annex 6 Part I, FAA 14 CFR Part 121 Appendix P

attributes.name: line_number
attributes.description: The sequential production line number assigned by the manufacturer indicating the order in which this aircraft was built within its type series.

attributes.name: mel_applicable
attributes.description: Indicates whether a Minimum Equipment List is applicable to this aircraft, allowing dispatch with certain non-critical equipment inoperative under controlled conditions.
attributes.references: ICAO Annex 6 Part I, FAA 14 CFR Part 121.628

attributes.name: msn
attributes.description: The unique serial number assigned by the aircraft manufacturer at the time of production. Permanent identifier that never changes regardless of ownership or registration.

attributes.name: noise_chapter
attributes.description: The ICAO noise certification standard chapter that the aircraft meets. Chapter 4 is the most stringent current standard. Determines airport access and noise restrictions.
attributes.references: ICAO Annex 16 Volume I - Aircraft Noise

attributes.name: operational_status
attributes.description: Current operational state of the aircraft. Active = in revenue service; Stored = long-term storage; Parked = temporary non-operation; Maintenance = undergoing MRO; Retired = permanently withdrawn; Wet_lease_out = leased to another carrier with crew; AOG = Aircraft on Ground (unscheduled maintenance). [ENUM-REF-CANDIDATE: active|stored|parked|maintenance|retired|wet_lease_out|aog — 7 candidates stripped; promote to reference product]

attributes.name: ownership_category
attributes.description: The legal and financial ownership structure of the aircraft. Owned = airline owns outright; Finance_lease = capital lease with purchase option; Operating_lease = rental without ownership transfer; Dry_lease = aircraft only; Wet_lease_in = aircraft with crew from lessor; ACMI = Aircraft Crew Maintenance Insurance lease.
attributes.references: IFRS 16 Leases, IATA Lease Classification Standards

attributes.name: registered_operator
attributes.description: The airline or operator name registered with the civil aviation authority as the entity authorized to operate this aircraft.

attributes.name: registered_owner
attributes.description: The legal entity name appearing on the certificate of registration as the registered owner of the aircraft. May differ from operator for leased aircraft.

attributes.name: registration_authority
attributes.description: The name of the civil aviation authority that issued the certificate of registration (e.g., FAA, EASA, CAAC, Transport Canada).

attributes.name: registration_date
attributes.description: The date the current certificate of registration was issued by the civil aviation authority.

attributes.name: registration_expiry_date
attributes.description: The expiration date of the current certificate of registration. Aircraft must be re-registered before this date to maintain legal operating authority.

attributes.name: retirement_date
attributes.description: The date the aircraft was permanently withdrawn from service and retired from the fleet. Null for active aircraft.

attributes.name: rvsm_approved
attributes.description: Indicates whether the aircraft is approved for RVSM operations allowing flight in airspace between FL290 and FL410 with 1,000-foot vertical separation.
attributes.references: ICAO Doc 9574 - Manual on Implementation of RVSM

attributes.name: seating_capacity_business
attributes.description: The number of seats in the business class cabin. Zero if aircraft does not have business class configuration.

attributes.name: seating_capacity_economy
attributes.description: The number of seats in the economy class cabin.

attributes.name: seating_capacity_first
attributes.description: The number of seats in the first class cabin. Zero if aircraft does not have first class configuration.

attributes.name: seating_capacity_premium_economy
attributes.description: The number of seats in the premium economy cabin. Zero if aircraft does not have premium economy configuration.

attributes.name: seating_capacity_total
attributes.description: The total number of passenger seats installed on the aircraft across all cabin classes. Used for load factor and capacity planning calculations.

attributes.name: tail_number
attributes.description: The official registration mark painted on the aircraft tail, serving as the globally unique identifier for the physical aircraft asset. Also known as registration mark or tail sign.
attributes.references: ICAO Annex 7 - Aircraft Nationality and Registration Marks

attributes.name: total_block_hours
attributes.description: Cumulative total block hours (gate-to-gate flight time) accumulated by the aircraft since delivery. Critical metric for maintenance planning and asset valuation.
attributes.references: IATA Maintenance Cost Task Force Standards

attributes.name: total_cycles
attributes.description: Cumulative total number of flight cycles (takeoff and landing pairs) accumulated by the aircraft since delivery. Key metric for fatigue life and maintenance interval tracking.
attributes.references: IATA Maintenance Cost Task Force Standards

attributes.name: updated_timestamp
attributes.description: The timestamp when this aircraft master record was last modified in the system.

products.name: aircraft_type
products.description: Reference master for ICAO/IATA aircraft type designators covering all aircraft families and variants operated or planned. Stores ICAO type code, IATA type code, manufacturer name, aircraft family (e.g. B737, A320), variant (e.g. B737-800, A320neo), engine count, engine type (turbofan, turboprop), wake turbulence category (L/M/H/J), maximum certified passenger capacity, maximum structural payload (kg), maximum takeoff weight (MTOW), maximum landing weight (MLW), maximum zero-fuel weight (MZFW), typical range (nm), typical cruise speed (Mach), wingspan (m), fuselage width category (narrowbody/widebody), ETOPS baseline capability, and whether the type is currently in the airline's fleet.
products.reference: ICAO Doc 8643 Aircraft Type Designators

attributes.name: aircraft_type_id
attributes.description: Unique identifier for the aircraft type record. Primary key.

attributes.name: aircraft_family
attributes.description: High-level aircraft family grouping (e.g., B737, A320, B777, A350, E190) used for fleet planning and commonality analysis.

attributes.name: aircraft_type_status
attributes.description: Current lifecycle status of the aircraft type in the airline's context: active (currently operated), retired (formerly operated), planned (future fleet addition), reference (not operated, maintained for codeshare/interline/industry reference).

attributes.name: aircraft_variant
attributes.description: Specific aircraft variant within the family including generation and configuration details (e.g., B737-800, A320neo, B777-300ER, A350-900, E190-E2).

attributes.name: apu_manufacturer
attributes.description: Manufacturer of the Auxiliary Power Unit (APU) (e.g., Honeywell, Pratt & Whitney Canada, Hamilton Sundstrand).

attributes.name: apu_model
attributes.description: Model designation of the Auxiliary Power Unit (APU) installed on this aircraft type (e.g., APS3200, GTCP331-500). Used for maintenance planning and ground operations.

attributes.name: cargo_volume_m3
attributes.business_glossary_term: Cargo Hold Volume in Cubic Meters
attributes.description: Total cargo hold volume in cubic meters. Used for cargo revenue planning and ULD capacity analysis.

attributes.name: created_timestamp
attributes.description: Timestamp when this aircraft type record was first created in the system.

attributes.name: emissions_standard
attributes.description: ICAO engine emissions standard (e.g., CAEP/6, CAEP/8, CAEP/10) indicating compliance level for NOx, CO, HC, and smoke. Used for CORSIA reporting and environmental compliance.
attributes.references: ICAO Annex 16 - Environmental Protection, Volume II

attributes.name: engine_count
attributes.description: Number of engines installed on the aircraft type (typically 2, 3, or 4 for commercial jets; 2 for turboprops).

attributes.name: engine_model
attributes.description: Specific engine model and manufacturer (e.g., CFM56-7B, PW1100G-JM, GE90-115B, Trent XWB) used for maintenance planning and fuel efficiency analysis.

attributes.name: engine_type
attributes.description: Propulsion system type installed on the aircraft (turbofan for modern jets, turboprop for regional aircraft, turbojet for older jets, piston for small aircraft).

attributes.name: etops_baseline_minutes
attributes.business_glossary_term: Extended-range Twin-engine Operational Performance Standards (ETOPS) Baseline Minutes
attributes.description: Baseline ETOPS certification in minutes (e.g., 120, 180, 330, 370) indicating how far the aircraft can fly from the nearest suitable airport with one engine inoperative. Null for non-ETOPS or multi-engine (3+) aircraft.

attributes.name: etops_certified_flag
attributes.business_glossary_term: Extended-range Twin-engine Operational Performance Standards (ETOPS) Certified Flag
attributes.description: Indicates whether this aircraft type holds ETOPS certification, enabling extended overwater and remote area operations for twin-engine aircraft.

attributes.name: fleet_entry_date
attributes.description: Date when this aircraft type first entered the airline's operating fleet. Null if not yet in fleet or planned only.

attributes.name: fleet_exit_date
attributes.description: Date when this aircraft type was retired from the airline's operating fleet. Null if still active or never operated.

attributes.name: fuel_capacity_liters
attributes.description: Total usable fuel capacity in liters. Critical for range calculation, fuel uplift planning, and operational cost analysis.

attributes.name: fuselage_length_m
attributes.description: Overall length of the aircraft fuselage in meters. Impacts gate compatibility and ground handling requirements.

attributes.name: fuselage_width_category
attributes.description: Classification of aircraft by fuselage width: narrowbody (single-aisle, e.g., A320, B737), widebody (twin-aisle, e.g., A350, B777), regional (smaller single-aisle, e.g., E190, CRJ).

attributes.name: iata_type_code
attributes.business_glossary_term: International Air Transport Association (IATA) Type Code
attributes.description: Three-character IATA aircraft type code used in reservation systems, schedules, and commercial documentation (e.g., 738 for Boeing 737-800, 32Q for Airbus A321neo).

attributes.name: icao_type_code
attributes.business_glossary_term: International Civil Aviation Organization (ICAO) Type Code
attributes.description: Four-character ICAO aircraft type designator used globally for flight planning, ATC communication, and operational documentation (e.g., B738 for Boeing 737-800, A20N for Airbus A320neo).

attributes.name: in_fleet_flag
attributes.description: Indicates whether this aircraft type is currently operated in the airline's fleet (true) or is a reference type for codeshare, interline, or future planning (false).

attributes.name: manufacturer_name
attributes.description: Name of the aircraft manufacturer (e.g., Boeing, Airbus, Embraer, Bombardier, ATR).

attributes.name: max_passenger_capacity
attributes.description: Maximum number of passenger seats that can be installed per the aircraft type certificate, regardless of airline-specific configuration. Used for regulatory compliance and emergency planning.
attributes.references: FAA Type Certificate Data Sheet / EASA Type Certificate

attributes.name: max_range_nm
attributes.description: Maximum certified range in nautical miles with maximum fuel and reduced payload. Defines the aircraft's absolute capability for ultra-long-haul operations.

attributes.name: max_structural_payload_kg
attributes.description: Maximum weight of passengers, cargo, and baggage that can be carried, limited by structural design. Critical for load planning and revenue optimization.

attributes.name: mel_applicable_flag
attributes.description: Indicates whether a Minimum Equipment List (MEL) is applicable to this aircraft type, allowing dispatch with certain non-critical equipment inoperative under specific conditions.

attributes.name: mlw_kg
attributes.description: Maximum certified weight at which the aircraft is permitted to land. Determines whether fuel jettison is required in emergency return scenarios.

attributes.name: modified_timestamp
attributes.description: Timestamp when this aircraft type record was last modified.

attributes.name: mtow_kg
attributes.description: Maximum certified weight at which the aircraft is permitted to take off. Determines runway length requirements, fuel capacity, and payload trade-offs.

attributes.name: mzfw_kg
attributes.business_glossary_term: Maximum Zero Fuel Weight (MZFW) in Kilograms
attributes.description: Maximum permitted weight of the aircraft and its contents (excluding usable fuel). Limits payload when fuel load is high. Critical for load planning.

attributes.name: noise_chapter
attributes.description: ICAO Annex 16 noise certification chapter (Chapter 2, 3, 4, or 14). Chapter 4 and 14 represent the latest, quietest standards. Critical for airport slot eligibility and environmental compliance.
attributes.references: ICAO Annex 16 - Environmental Protection, Volume I

attributes.name: typical_block_fuel_per_hour_kg
attributes.business_glossary_term: Typical Block Fuel Consumption per Hour (Kilograms)
attributes.description: Average fuel burn per block hour in kilograms under typical operating conditions. Used for CASK calculation, route profitability analysis, and fuel budgeting.
attributes.references: Manufacturer Performance Data / Internal Operations Analysis

attributes.name: typical_cruise_speed_mach
attributes.description: Typical cruise speed expressed as Mach number (e.g., 0.78, 0.82, 0.85). Used for flight planning, schedule optimization, and block time calculation.

attributes.name: typical_range_nm
attributes.description: Typical operational range in nautical miles with standard passenger load and reserves. Used for route network planning and aircraft assignment.

attributes.name: wake_turbulence_category
attributes.description: ICAO wake turbulence category based on maximum takeoff weight: L (Light, <7000kg), M (Medium, 7000-136000kg), H (Heavy, >136000kg), J (Super, A380 only). Critical for ATC separation standards.

attributes.name: wingspan_m
attributes.description: Aircraft wingspan in meters. Determines gate compatibility, taxiway clearance requirements, and ICAO aerodrome reference code.

products.name: cabin_configuration
products.description: Defines the cabin layout and seating configuration installed on a specific aircraft. Each record represents a named configuration version (e.g. 'B738-CFG-A') linked to an aircraft or aircraft type. Captures total seat count, number of cabin classes (e.g. First, Business, Premium Economy, Economy), seat pitch by class, seat width by class, lie-flat availability, in-flight entertainment (IFE) system type, Wi-Fi availability, galley count, lavatory count, door count, overwing exit count, configuration effective date, and configuration retirement date. Supports revenue management seat inventory and passenger service.
products.reference: IATA SSIM Cabin Configuration / Aircraft Seat Map

attributes.name: cabin_configuration_id
attributes.description: Unique identifier for the cabin configuration record. Primary key.

attributes.name: aircraft_id
attributes.description: Reference to the specific aircraft tail number to which this cabin configuration is installed.

attributes.name: aircraft_type_id
attributes.description: Reference to the aircraft type (e.g., B738, A320) for which this configuration is designed. Used when configuration applies to a fleet type rather than a single tail.

attributes.name: business_class_seat_count
attributes.description: Number of seats in the Business Class cabin. Zero if Business Class is not offered in this configuration.

attributes.name: business_class_seat_pitch_inches
attributes.description: Average seat pitch in Business Class, measured in inches. Null if Business Class is not offered.

attributes.name: business_class_seat_width_inches
attributes.description: Average seat width in Business Class, measured in inches. Null if Business Class is not offered.

attributes.name: cabin_class_count
attributes.description: Number of distinct cabin classes in this configuration (e.g., 1 for all-economy, 2 for business and economy, 3 for first/business/economy).

attributes.name: configuration_code
attributes.description: Unique business identifier for the cabin configuration version (e.g., B738-CFG-A, A320-Y180). Used for operational reference and inventory management.

attributes.name: configuration_name
attributes.description: Human-readable name or description of the cabin configuration (e.g., 'High-Density Economy', 'Premium Three-Class').

attributes.name: configuration_status
attributes.description: Current lifecycle status of the cabin configuration. Active configurations are in operational use; planned configurations are approved but not yet installed; retired configurations are no longer in service.

attributes.name: created_timestamp
attributes.description: Timestamp when this cabin configuration record was first created in the system.

attributes.name: door_count
attributes.description: Total number of passenger entry/exit doors in this cabin configuration. Critical for emergency evacuation certification.

attributes.name: economy_seat_count
attributes.description: Number of seats in the Economy (standard coach) cabin.

attributes.name: economy_seat_pitch_inches
attributes.description: Average seat pitch in Economy class, measured in inches.

attributes.name: economy_seat_width_inches
attributes.description: Average seat width in Economy class, measured in inches.

attributes.name: effective_date
attributes.description: Date on which this cabin configuration became (or will become) active and available for operational use.

attributes.name: first_class_seat_count
attributes.description: Number of seats in the First Class cabin. Zero if First Class is not offered in this configuration.

attributes.name: first_class_seat_pitch_inches
attributes.description: Average seat pitch (distance from one seat to the same point on the seat in front) in First Class, measured in inches. Null if First Class is not offered.

attributes.name: first_class_seat_width_inches
attributes.description: Average seat width in First Class, measured in inches. Null if First Class is not offered.

attributes.name: galley_count
attributes.description: Total number of galleys (food and beverage preparation areas) installed in this cabin configuration.

attributes.name: ife_system_type
attributes.description: Type or model of the In-Flight Entertainment system installed (e.g., 'Panasonic eX3', 'Thales AVANT', 'Streaming-only'). Null if no IFE is installed.

attributes.name: lavatory_count
attributes.description: Total number of lavatories (restrooms) installed in this cabin configuration.

attributes.name: lie_flat_seat_available
attributes.description: Indicates whether this configuration includes lie-flat seats (typically in First or Business Class). True if any cabin class offers lie-flat capability.

attributes.name: modified_timestamp
attributes.description: Timestamp when this cabin configuration record was last modified.

attributes.name: overwing_exit_count
attributes.description: Number of overwing emergency exits in this cabin configuration. Used for evacuation planning and seating restrictions.

attributes.name: power_outlet_availability
attributes.description: Indicates the availability of power outlets (AC or USB) for passenger devices. Values: none (no power outlets), selected_seats (available in premium cabins or select rows), all_seats (available at every seat).

attributes.name: premium_economy_seat_count
attributes.description: Number of seats in the Premium Economy cabin. Zero if Premium Economy is not offered in this configuration.

attributes.name: premium_economy_seat_pitch_inches
attributes.description: Average seat pitch in Premium Economy, measured in inches. Null if Premium Economy is not offered.

attributes.name: premium_economy_seat_width_inches
attributes.description: Average seat width in Premium Economy, measured in inches. Null if Premium Economy is not offered.

attributes.name: retirement_date
attributes.description: Date on which this cabin configuration was retired from service. Null if the configuration is still active or planned.

attributes.name: seat_map_reference
attributes.description: Reference identifier or URL to the detailed seat map diagram for this configuration. Used by reservation systems and passenger-facing applications.

attributes.name: total_seat_count
attributes.description: Total number of passenger seats installed in this cabin configuration across all classes. Critical for revenue management and Available Seat Kilometer (ASK) calculations.

attributes.name: wifi_available
attributes.description: Indicates whether in-flight Wi-Fi connectivity is available in this cabin configuration.

attributes.name: wifi_provider
attributes.description: Name of the Wi-Fi service provider (e.g., 'Gogo', 'Viasat', 'Panasonic Avionics'). Null if Wi-Fi is not available.

products.name: seat_map
products.description: Seat-level detail for a cabin configuration — each row represents one physical seat position. This is the granular seat inventory that passenger service systems, revenue management, and check-in reference for seat assignment, blocking, and special service request (SSR) fulfillment. Captures seat designator (e.g. 12A), deck (main/upper), cabin class assignment, row number, column letter, seat type (window/middle/aisle), location attributes (exit-row, bulkhead, overwing, last-row, bassinet-capable), physical dimensions (pitch inches, width inches), recline capability (standard/limited/lie-flat/angle-flat), blocking flags (is_blocked, block_reason), crew rest indicator, IFE availability, power outlet type (none/AC/USB/both), and premium attributes relevant to ancillary seat selection revenue.
products.reference: IATA PADIS / SSIM Seat Map Standard

attributes.name: seat_map_id
attributes.description: Unique identifier for the seat map record. Primary key for the seat map entity.

attributes.name: cabin_configuration_id
attributes.description: Reference to the specific aircraft configuration that this seat belongs to. Links to the aircraft configuration master data defining the overall cabin layout.

attributes.name: block_reason
attributes.description: The reason why the seat is blocked from assignment. Provides operational context for seat inventory management and passenger service recovery.

attributes.name: cabin_class
attributes.description: The service class or cabin compartment to which this seat is assigned. Determines service level, amenities, and fare eligibility.

attributes.name: column_letter
attributes.description: The alphabetic column identifier for the seat position within the row (A through K). Typically A and K are window seats in wide-body aircraft.

attributes.name: created_timestamp
attributes.description: The timestamp when this seat map record was first created in the system. Used for audit trail and data lineage.

attributes.name: deck
attributes.description: The deck or level of the aircraft where the seat is located. Relevant for wide-body aircraft with multiple passenger decks.

attributes.name: effective_date
attributes.description: The date from which this seat map configuration becomes active and available for passenger assignment. Supports configuration versioning and fleet changes.

attributes.name: expiry_date
attributes.description: The date on which this seat map configuration is retired and no longer valid for passenger assignment. Nullable for current active configurations.

attributes.name: galley_proximity
attributes.description: Indicates the proximity of the seat to galley (kitchen) facilities. Proximity to galleys can impact passenger experience due to noise and crew activity.

attributes.name: has_ife
attributes.description: Flag indicating whether the seat is equipped with an in-flight entertainment system. IFE availability is a key amenity for passenger satisfaction and ancillary revenue.

attributes.name: ife_screen_size_inches
attributes.description: The diagonal screen size in inches of the in-flight entertainment display at this seat. Used for product differentiation and passenger communication.

attributes.name: is_accessible
attributes.description: Flag indicating whether the seat is designated as accessible for passengers with disabilities or reduced mobility. Accessible seats meet regulatory requirements for space and proximity to facilities.

attributes.name: is_bassinet_capable
attributes.description: Flag indicating whether the seat position can accommodate an infant bassinet attachment. Typically available at bulkhead seats with sufficient wall space.

attributes.name: is_blocked
attributes.description: Flag indicating whether the seat is currently blocked from passenger assignment. Blocked seats are unavailable for sale or assignment due to operational, regulatory, or commercial reasons.

attributes.name: is_bulkhead
attributes.description: Flag indicating whether the seat is located directly behind a bulkhead (dividing wall). Bulkhead seats typically offer extra legroom but may have restricted under-seat storage.

attributes.name: is_crew_rest
attributes.description: Flag indicating whether the seat is designated for crew rest on long-haul flights. Crew rest seats are blocked from passenger assignment and reserved for flight crew during rest periods.

attributes.name: is_exit_row
attributes.description: Flag indicating whether the seat is located in an emergency exit row. Exit row seats have special regulatory requirements and passenger eligibility restrictions.

attributes.name: is_last_row
attributes.description: Flag indicating whether the seat is in the last row of the cabin or section. Last row seats often have limited or no recline and proximity to lavatories.

attributes.name: is_overwing
attributes.description: Flag indicating whether the seat is located over the aircraft wing, which may restrict window views. Used for passenger communication and seat selection preferences.

attributes.name: is_preferred_seat
attributes.description: Flag indicating whether the seat is designated as a preferred or premium seat eligible for ancillary seat selection fees. Preferred seats typically offer enhanced comfort or location.

attributes.name: last_modified_timestamp
attributes.description: The timestamp when this seat map record was last updated. Used for change tracking and audit trail.

attributes.name: lavatory_proximity
attributes.description: Indicates the proximity of the seat to lavatory facilities. Proximity to lavatories can be a positive (convenience) or negative (noise, traffic) factor for seat selection.

attributes.name: power_outlet_type
attributes.description: The type of power outlet available at the seat for passenger device charging. Power availability is increasingly important for passenger satisfaction and ancillary revenue.

attributes.name: recline_angle_degrees
attributes.description: The maximum recline angle of the seat in degrees from vertical. Used to communicate seat comfort specifications and differentiate premium products.

attributes.name: recline_type
attributes.description: The recline capability of the seat, ranging from no recline to full lie-flat configurations. Critical for premium cabin differentiation and passenger comfort.

attributes.name: row_number
attributes.description: The numeric row identifier within the aircraft cabin. Used for seat assignment logic and cabin zone management.

attributes.name: seat_designator
attributes.description: The unique seat identifier within the aircraft, combining row number and column letter (e.g., 12A, 34F). This is the seat label passengers see on their boarding pass.

attributes.name: seat_fee_tier
attributes.description: The pricing tier for ancillary seat selection fees. Used by revenue management systems to price seat assignments and optimize ancillary revenue.

attributes.name: seat_map_status
attributes.description: The current lifecycle status of the seat map record. Indicates whether the seat configuration is currently in use, pending activation, or retired.

attributes.name: seat_pitch_inches
attributes.description: The distance in inches from one point on a seat to the same point on the seat in front or behind, measuring legroom and seat spacing. Key metric for passenger comfort and cabin density.

attributes.name: seat_type
attributes.description: The positional type of the seat within the row, indicating whether it is adjacent to the window, in the middle of a seat group, or adjacent to the aisle. Critical for passenger preference and ancillary revenue.

attributes.name: seat_width_inches
attributes.description: The width of the seat in inches, measured at the widest point of the seat cushion. Impacts passenger comfort and cabin configuration.

attributes.name: storage_restriction
attributes.description: Indicates any restrictions on carry-on baggage storage at this seat location. Some seats (e.g., bulkhead, exit row) have limited under-seat or overhead storage.

products.name: fleet_order
products.description: Records aircraft purchase orders and lease commitments placed with OEMs (Boeing, Airbus, Embraer) or lessors for fleet growth, replacement, or renewal. Each record represents a firm order, option, or letter of intent. Captures order reference number, aircraft type ordered, quantity (firm/option/LoI), deliveries completed, cancellations, order date, contractual delivery window (start/end), list price per unit (USD), negotiated price per unit where available, total order value, order status (firm/option/LoI/cancelled/converted), financing structure (cash/debt/sale-leaseback/operating-lease), counterparty (OEM or lessor), and associated fleet plan scenario reference. Supports fleet planning, capital expenditure forecasting, and delivery pipeline management.
products.reference: Aircraft Purchase Agreement / Lease Agreement

attributes.name: fleet_order_id
attributes.description: Unique identifier for the fleet order record. Primary key for aircraft purchase orders and lease commitments.

attributes.name: aircraft_type_id
attributes.description: Reference to the aircraft type being ordered (e.g., Boeing 737-800, Airbus A320neo). Links to aircraft type master data containing ICAO/IATA designators and specifications.

attributes.name: fleet_plan_id
attributes.description: Reference to the strategic fleet planning scenario that this order supports. Links order to long-term fleet growth, replacement, or renewal strategy.

attributes.name: procurement_manager_employee_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to workforce.employee. Business justification: Fleet orders require assigned procurement manager for OEM contract negotiation, pricing approval authority, delivery schedule coordination, and purchase order authorization. Essential for procurement

attributes.name: purchase_order_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to procurement.purchase_order. Business justification: Aircraft orders are major capital purchases requiring formal PO workflow. Links fleet acquisition to procurement system for payment milestone tracking, delivery coordination, invoice matching, and fin

attributes.name: vendor_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to procurement.vendor. Business justification: Aircraft manufacturers and lessors are vendors. Enables OEM performance tracking, delivery compliance monitoring, warranty claim processing, and consolidated vendor relationship management for fleet a

attributes.name: cabin_configuration_code
attributes.description: Planned cabin layout configuration for the ordered aircraft. Defines seating classes and arrangement (e.g., 2-class, 3-class, high-density). Links to detailed seat map specifications.

attributes.name: cancellation_date
attributes.description: Date when the order was officially cancelled or terminated. Null for active orders.

attributes.name: cancellation_penalty_usd
attributes.description: Financial penalty amount in US Dollars if the order is cancelled before delivery. Defined in contract terms.

attributes.name: cancellation_reason
attributes.description: Business reason for order cancellation. Examples: strategic fleet plan change, financial constraints, route network adjustment, OEM delivery delays. Null for active orders.

attributes.name: contract_reference_number
attributes.description: Legal contract or purchase agreement reference number. Links to the binding legal document governing the order terms and conditions.

attributes.name: conversion_date
attributes.description: Date when an option or letter of intent was converted to a firm order. Null if order was firm from inception or has not been converted.

attributes.name: counterparty_type
attributes.description: Classification of the counterparty. OEM = Original Equipment Manufacturer (Boeing, Airbus), Lessor = Aircraft leasing company, Broker = Intermediary facilitating the transaction.

attributes.name: created_timestamp
attributes.description: Timestamp when this fleet order record was first created in the system. Audit trail for data lineage.

attributes.name: delivery_window_end_date
attributes.description: Latest contractual delivery date for aircraft in this order. Defines the end of the delivery period.

attributes.name: delivery_window_start_date
attributes.description: Earliest contractual delivery date for aircraft in this order. Defines the beginning of the delivery period.

attributes.name: deposit_amount_usd
attributes.description: Initial deposit or down payment amount paid to secure the order, in US Dollars. Typically a percentage of total order value.

attributes.name: engine_type
attributes.description: Specific engine model selected for the aircraft order. Examples: CFM LEAP-1A, Pratt & Whitney PW1100G, Rolls-Royce Trent 7000. Critical for maintenance planning and fuel efficiency.

attributes.name: financing_structure
attributes.description: Method of financing the aircraft acquisition. Cash = direct purchase, Debt Financing = loan-backed purchase, Sale-Leaseback = sell and lease back, Operating Lease = rental, Finance Lease = lease-to-own, Hybrid = combination of methods.

attributes.name: last_modified_timestamp
attributes.description: Timestamp when this fleet order record was last updated. Tracks most recent change for audit and data quality purposes.

attributes.name: list_price_per_unit_usd
attributes.business_glossary_term: List Price Per Unit (United States Dollar - USD)
attributes.description: Manufacturer's published list price per aircraft in US Dollars. This is the catalog price before any negotiated discounts.

attributes.name: negotiated_price_per_unit_usd
attributes.business_glossary_term: Negotiated Price Per Unit (United States Dollar - USD)
attributes.description: Actual negotiated price per aircraft in US Dollars after discounts and concessions. Highly confidential commercial terms. Null if not disclosed or still under negotiation.

attributes.name: notes
attributes.description: Free-text field for additional order details, special terms, delivery conditions, or internal planning notes. Supports operational context and decision documentation.

attributes.name: option_expiry_date
attributes.description: Date by which option rights must be exercised or they expire. Applicable only for orders with option quantities. Null for firm orders.

attributes.name: order_date
attributes.description: Date when the order was officially placed with the OEM or lessor. Marks the contractual commitment date.

attributes.name: order_status
attributes.description: Current lifecycle status of the fleet order. Firm = binding commitment, Option = right to purchase, Letter of Intent = preliminary agreement, Cancelled = order terminated, Converted = option converted to firm, Delivered = order fulfilled.

attributes.name: order_type
attributes.description: Classification of the acquisition structure. Purchase = outright ownership, Operating Lease = rental without ownership transfer, Finance Lease = lease with ownership transfer option, Sale-Leaseback = sell owned aircraft and lease back, Wet Lease = aircraft with crew, Dry Lease = aircraft only, ACMI = Aircraft Crew Maintenance Insurance lease. [ENUM-REF-CANDIDATE: purchase|operating_lease|finance_lease|sale_leaseback|wet_lease|dry_lease|acmi — 7 candidates stripped; promote to reference product]

attributes.name: purpose
attributes.description: Strategic business purpose for the aircraft order. Fleet Growth = net addition to fleet size, Fleet Replacement = replacing retiring aircraft, Fleet Renewal = modernizing existing capacity, Capacity Expansion = increasing seat capacity, Route Expansion = supporting new route network.

attributes.name: quantity_cancelled
attributes.description: Number of aircraft from this order that have been cancelled or terminated before delivery.

attributes.name: quantity_delivered
attributes.description: Number of aircraft from this order that have been delivered and accepted into the fleet.

attributes.name: quantity_firm
attributes.description: Number of aircraft under firm binding commitment. These are contractually committed deliveries.

attributes.name: quantity_loi
attributes.description: Number of aircraft covered by letter of intent. Non-binding preliminary agreement expressing purchase interest.

attributes.name: quantity_option
attributes.description: Number of aircraft under option rights. Airline has the right but not obligation to purchase at predetermined terms.

attributes.name: reference_number
attributes.description: External business identifier for the aircraft order or lease commitment. Used in contracts and communications with OEMs and lessors.

attributes.name: total_order_value_usd
attributes.business_glossary_term: Total Order Value (United States Dollar - USD)
attributes.description: Total financial value of the entire order in US Dollars. Calculated as quantity times negotiated price (or list price if negotiated not available). Represents total capital commitment.

attributes.name: total_seat_capacity
attributes.description: Total number of passenger seats in the planned cabin configuration. Sum of all seating classes (First, Business, Premium Economy, Economy).

products.name: aircraft_delivery
products.description: Transactional record of each aircraft delivery event — when a new or leased aircraft is formally accepted into the airline's fleet from a manufacturer or lessor. Captures delivery date, delivery location (airport ICAO), aircraft MSN, tail number assigned at delivery, aircraft type, delivery flight number (ferry flight), acceptance certificate reference, technical acceptance inspection outcome, delivery condition (new/used), hours at delivery, cycles at delivery, engine serial numbers at delivery, APU serial number at delivery, and delivery team sign-off. Triggers aircraft registration and initial airworthiness documentation.
products.reference: Aircraft Delivery Acceptance Certificate

attributes.name: aircraft_delivery_id
attributes.description: Unique identifier for the aircraft delivery event. Primary key for the aircraft delivery transaction.

attributes.name: acceptance_team_lead_employee_id
attributes.business_glossary_term: Acceptance Team Lead Employee Id (Foreign Key)
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to workforce.employee. Business justification: Aircraft delivery acceptance requires named technical lead with sign-off authority for manufacturer handover, certificate of acceptance issuance, and warranty claim accountability. Replaces denormaliz

attributes.name: aircraft_id
attributes.description: Reference to the aircraft master record that was delivered. Links to the aircraft asset registry.

attributes.name: aircraft_type_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to fleet.aircraft_type. Business justification: Aircraft delivery records the type of aircraft being delivered. Currently denormalizes aircraft_type_icao and aircraft_type_iata. Adding aircraft_type_id FK normalizes this and allows delivery records

attributes.name: delivery_station_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to airport.station. Business justification: New aircraft acceptance logistics, delivery team deployment, and acceptance flight planning require station linkage. Fleet planning and delivery coordination depend on accurate station tracking. Repla

attributes.name: fixed_asset_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to finance.fixed_asset. Business justification: When aircraft is delivered, it's capitalized as a fixed asset. Delivery record must link to fixed_asset entry for acquisition cost, depreciation tracking, and asset register reconciliation. Real busin

attributes.name: fleet_order_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to fleet.fleet_order. Business justification: Aircraft delivery fulfills a fleet order. fleet_order tracks purchase orders and lease commitments; aircraft_delivery records the actual delivery event. Linking delivery to order establishes traceabil

attributes.name: vendor_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to procurement.vendor. Business justification: Aircraft deliveries are procured from vendors (manufacturers like Boeing/Airbus or lessors). This FK links the delivery to the vendor master for contract management and payment tracking. Removes redun

attributes.name: acceptance_certificate_reference
attributes.description: Reference number of the formal acceptance certificate document signed by the airline and manufacturer/lessor confirming aircraft delivery and acceptance.

attributes.name: airframe_cycles_at_delivery
attributes.description: Total accumulated flight cycles (takeoff and landing cycles) on the airframe at the time of delivery. Zero for new aircraft, non-zero for used aircraft.

attributes.name: airframe_hours_at_delivery
attributes.description: Total accumulated flight hours (block hours) on the airframe at the time of delivery. Zero for new aircraft, non-zero for used aircraft.

attributes.name: apu_serial_number
attributes.description: Manufacturer serial number of the Auxiliary Power Unit (APU) installed on the aircraft at delivery. APU provides electrical power and pneumatic air on the ground and in-flight backup.

attributes.name: cabin_configuration_code
attributes.description: Code representing the cabin layout and seating configuration installed at delivery (e.g., 2-class, 3-class, all-economy). References the airline's standard configuration catalog.

attributes.name: created_timestamp
attributes.description: Timestamp when this aircraft delivery record was first created in the system.

attributes.name: delivery_condition
attributes.description: Condition classification of the aircraft at delivery: new from manufacturer, used from lessor, refurbished after major overhaul, or pre-owned from another operator.

attributes.name: delivery_date
attributes.description: The date on which the aircraft was formally accepted into the airline's fleet from the manufacturer or lessor. Marks the start of operational availability.

attributes.name: delivery_flight_number
attributes.description: Flight number assigned to the ferry flight that delivered the aircraft from the manufacturer or lessor facility to the airline's base. May be a non-revenue positioning flight.

attributes.name: delivery_notes
attributes.description: Free-text notes capturing additional details about the delivery event, including any special conditions, snags identified during acceptance inspection, or deviations from standard delivery procedures.

attributes.name: delivery_number
attributes.description: Externally-known unique business identifier for this aircraft delivery transaction, typically assigned by the manufacturer or lessor.

attributes.name: delivery_status
attributes.description: Current lifecycle status of the aircraft delivery transaction: scheduled (planned future delivery), in transit (ferry flight underway), accepted (delivery completed and aircraft in service), rejected (delivery refused), cancelled (delivery cancelled), or deferred (delivery postponed).

attributes.name: delivery_timestamp
attributes.description: Precise timestamp when the aircraft delivery acceptance was signed off and the aircraft officially transferred to the airline's operational control.

attributes.name: engine_1_serial_number
attributes.description: Manufacturer serial number of the engine installed in position 1 (typically left engine on twin-engine aircraft) at delivery.

attributes.name: engine_2_serial_number
attributes.description: Manufacturer serial number of the engine installed in position 2 (typically right engine on twin-engine aircraft) at delivery.

attributes.name: engine_3_serial_number
attributes.description: Manufacturer serial number of the engine installed in position 3 (for tri-jet or quad-jet aircraft) at delivery. Null for twin-engine aircraft.

attributes.name: engine_4_serial_number
attributes.description: Manufacturer serial number of the engine installed in position 4 (for quad-jet aircraft) at delivery. Null for twin-engine and tri-jet aircraft.

attributes.name: etops_certified_flag
attributes.business_glossary_term: Extended-range Twin-engine Operational Performance Standards (ETOPS) Certification Flag
attributes.description: Indicates whether the aircraft is certified for ETOPS operations at delivery, allowing extended-range twin-engine flights over routes distant from diversion airports.
attributes.references: FAA Part 121 Appendix P, EASA Part-CAT

attributes.name: etops_rating_minutes
attributes.business_glossary_term: Extended-range Twin-engine Operational Performance Standards (ETOPS) Rating in Minutes
attributes.description: ETOPS rating in minutes (e.g., 120, 180, 207, 330) indicating the maximum diversion time the aircraft is certified for. Null if not ETOPS certified.
attributes.references: FAA Part 121 Appendix P, EASA Part-CAT

attributes.name: mel_applicable_flag
attributes.description: Indicates whether a Minimum Equipment List (MEL) is applicable to this aircraft, allowing dispatch with certain non-critical equipment inoperative under specified conditions.

attributes.name: msn
attributes.description: Unique serial number assigned by the aircraft manufacturer at production. Permanent identifier for the airframe throughout its lifecycle.

attributes.name: ownership_type
attributes.description: Type of ownership or lease arrangement under which the aircraft was acquired: owned (purchased outright), wet lease (aircraft with crew), dry lease (aircraft only), ACMI (Aircraft Crew Maintenance Insurance), finance lease, or operating lease.

attributes.name: tail_number
attributes.description: Civil aviation registration number (tail number) assigned to the aircraft at delivery. Displayed on the aircraft fuselage and used for ATC identification.

attributes.name: technical_acceptance_outcome
attributes.description: Outcome of the technical acceptance inspection performed by the airline's engineering team: accepted (no issues), accepted with conditions (minor snags to be resolved), rejected (major defects), or deferred (inspection postponed).

attributes.name: total_seat_capacity
attributes.description: Total number of passenger seats installed in the aircraft at delivery, across all cabin classes.
