attributes.name: part_145_approval_reference
attributes.description: Reference to the Part-145 maintenance organisation approval certificate number under which this work was performed. Required for regulatory compliance and airworthiness release.
attributes.references: EASA Part-145 Approved Maintenance Organisation, FAA Part 145 Repair Station

attributes.name: priority_level
attributes.description: Business priority assigned to the work order. Critical indicates AOG (Aircraft on Ground) or safety-critical; high indicates flight-impacting; medium indicates scheduled with tight window; low indicates deferrable; routine indicates standard interval work.
attributes.references: IATA Maintenance Cost Standards, SMS (Safety Management System) Risk Matrix

attributes.name: sb_reference
attributes.description: Reference to the manufacturer Service Bulletin number if this work order implements a recommended modification or inspection. Format varies by OEM (e.g., Boeing SB 737-32-1234, Airbus SB A320-32-1234).
attributes.references: OEM Service Bulletin Standards, ATA iSpec 2200

attributes.name: scheduled_completion_timestamp
attributes.description: Planned date and time when maintenance work is scheduled to be completed. Used for aircraft return-to-service planning and slot management.

attributes.name: scheduled_start_timestamp
attributes.description: Planned date and time when maintenance work is scheduled to begin. Used for resource planning and aircraft availability forecasting.

attributes.name: sign_off_timestamp
attributes.description: Date and time when the certifying engineer signed off the work order and issued the Certificate of Release to Service (CRS). Marks the official completion and airworthiness release.
attributes.references: EASA Part-M Continuing Airworthiness, FAA AC 43-9C Maintenance Records

attributes.name: work_order_number
attributes.description: Externally-known business identifier for the work order, typically formatted as WO followed by numeric sequence. Used for cross-system reference and operator communication.
attributes.references: AMOS (Aircraft Maintenance and Engineering System) Work Order Standards, ATA Spec 2000

attributes.name: work_order_status
attributes.description: Current lifecycle state of the work order. Open indicates work is scheduled but not started; in-progress indicates active execution; deferred indicates MEL (Minimum Equipment List) deferral or resource constraint; completed indicates work finished pending sign-off; closed indicates final approval and record closure; cancelled indicates work order voided.
attributes.references: IATA Maintenance Cost Task Force Standards, Part-145 Work Order Lifecycle

attributes.name: work_order_type
attributes.description: Classification of the work order by maintenance category. Scheduled includes routine checks and intervals; unscheduled covers reactive maintenance; AOG (Aircraft on Ground) indicates critical grounding events; modification covers STC (Supplemental Type Certificate) and design changes; inspection includes regulatory and operational checks; defect rectification addresses reported discrepancies.
attributes.references: EASA Part-145 Maintenance Categories, FAA AC 120-16F Maintenance Programs

products.name: work_order_task
products.description: Individual task line within a work order, representing a discrete maintenance action, inspection step, or job card instruction. Tracks task card reference, ATA chapter/section, skill trade required (avionics, airframe, powerplant), estimated hours, actual hours, technician sign-off, inspector sign-off, status, and any deferred or carry-forward flags. Enables granular tracking of multi-task work packages.
products.reference: AMOS Job Card / Task Card

attributes.name: work_order_task_id
attributes.description: Unique identifier for the work order task line item. Primary key.
attributes.references: AMOS Aircraft Maintenance and Engineering System

attributes.name: component_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to maintenance.component. Business justification: Work order task may involve a specific component. The work_order_task table has component_part_number and component_serial_number but no FK. Adding component_id FK normalizes this and removes redundan

attributes.name: crew_technician_crew_member_id
attributes.business_glossary_term: Crew Technician Crew Member Id (Foreign Key)
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to crew.crew_member. Business justification: Dual-role crew members (pilot-engineers, flight engineers with A&P) perform line maintenance tasks. Business process: dual-role workforce utilization tracking, labor cost allocation, regulatory compli

attributes.name: defect_report_id
attributes.description: Reference to the originating defect or discrepancy record that triggered this corrective maintenance task. Links unscheduled maintenance to reported defects.
attributes.references: AMOS Aircraft Maintenance and Engineering System

attributes.name: implementing_corrective_action_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to safety.corrective_action. Business justification: Individual tasks may fulfill specific corrective actions (granular implementation tracking). Enables task-level verification of corrective action completion for audit compliance, supports detailed eff

attributes.name: inspector_employee_id
attributes.description: Reference to the certified inspector who performed independent inspection and verification of the completed task. Required for critical tasks and return-to-service certification.

attributes.name: mel_deferral_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to maintenance.mel_deferral. Business justification: Work order task may be related to a MEL deferral. The work_order_task table has mel_reference (STRING) but no FK. Adding mel_deferral_id FK normalizes this and removes redundant mel_reference.

attributes.name: originating_occurrence_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to safety.occurrence. Business justification: Individual maintenance tasks may be tied to specific safety events requiring rectification (e.g., post-incident inspection tasks). Enables granular tracking of occurrence-driven maintenance actions fo

attributes.name: primary_work_technician_employee_id
attributes.description: Reference to the certified aircraft maintenance technician who performed the work. Links to employee/crew master data.

attributes.name: work_order_id
attributes.description: Reference to the parent work order header that contains this task line.
attributes.references: AMOS Aircraft Maintenance and Engineering System

attributes.name: actual_labor_hours
attributes.description: Actual labor hours expended to complete this task, captured for cost accounting, productivity analysis, and future task planning.
attributes.references: AMOS Aircraft Maintenance and Engineering System

attributes.name: airworthiness_directive_reference
attributes.description: Reference number of the Airworthiness Directive if this task is performed to comply with a mandatory AD issued by the aviation authority (FAA/EASA). Critical for regulatory compliance.
attributes.references: EASA Part-21 Certification of Aircraft and Related Products

attributes.name: ata_chapter
attributes.description: Two-digit ATA chapter code identifying the aircraft system category (e.g., 32=Landing Gear, 71=Power Plant, 24=Electrical Power). Standard aircraft system classification.

attributes.name: ata_section
attributes.description: ATA section code providing finer granularity within the ATA chapter, identifying the specific subsystem or component area.

attributes.name: created_timestamp
attributes.description: System timestamp when this work order task record was first created in the maintenance system, used for audit trail and data lineage.
attributes.references: AMOS Aircraft Maintenance and Engineering System

attributes.name: deferral_expiry_date
attributes.description: The date by which a deferred task must be completed, as specified by MEL category limits (A/B/C/D) or other deferral authorization. Critical for compliance tracking.

attributes.name: deferral_flag
attributes.description: Boolean indicator whether this task has been deferred under MEL or other approved deferral provisions. True indicates the task is deferred and must be tracked for completion within allowable limits.

attributes.name: estimated_labor_hours
attributes.description: Planned or standard labor hours required to complete this task, used for work planning, scheduling, and cost estimation.
attributes.references: AMOS Aircraft Maintenance and Engineering System

attributes.name: inspector_license_number
attributes.description: The Part-66 or equivalent aircraft maintenance license number of the inspector who verified the task, required for regulatory traceability and airworthiness certification.

attributes.name: inspector_signoff_timestamp
attributes.description: Date and time when the inspector signed off the task verification, certifying that the work meets airworthiness standards and approved procedures.

attributes.name: installed_component_serial_number
attributes.description: Serial number of the component installed during a replacement task, required for aircraft configuration control and life-limited parts tracking.

attributes.name: last_modified_timestamp
attributes.description: System timestamp when this work order task record was last updated, used for audit trail, change tracking, and data synchronization.
attributes.references: AMOS Aircraft Maintenance and Engineering System

attributes.name: materials_cost_amount
attributes.description: Total cost of materials, parts, and consumables used in this task, captured for maintenance cost accounting and budget tracking.

attributes.name: removed_component_serial_number
attributes.description: Serial number of the component removed during a replacement task, required for component tracking, warranty claims, and rotable pool management.

attributes.name: service_bulletin_reference
attributes.description: Reference number of the manufacturer Service Bulletin if this task implements a recommended or mandatory modification, inspection, or service action.
attributes.references: EASA Part-21 Certification of Aircraft and Related Products

attributes.name: skill_trade_required
attributes.description: The specialized maintenance trade or skill category required to perform this task (avionics, airframe, powerplant, electrical, hydraulic, composite). Determines technician assignment and certification requirements.

attributes.name: task_card_reference
attributes.description: Reference number or code of the maintenance task card, job card, or work instruction document that defines this task. Links to approved maintenance procedures.

attributes.name: task_completion_timestamp
attributes.description: Date and time when this task was completed and signed off, marking the end of work and enabling aircraft return-to-service processing.
attributes.references: AMOS Aircraft Maintenance and Engineering System

attributes.name: task_description
attributes.description: Detailed narrative description of the maintenance action, inspection step, or repair work to be performed. Includes scope, method, and acceptance criteria.

attributes.name: task_notes
attributes.description: Free-text field for technician notes, observations, findings, or special instructions related to this task. Captures important context not covered by structured fields.

attributes.name: task_priority
attributes.description: Priority level assigned to this task for scheduling and resource allocation: critical (AOG/safety), high (operational impact), medium (scheduled), low (routine).
attributes.references: AMOS Aircraft Maintenance and Engineering System

attributes.name: task_sequence_number
attributes.description: Sequential ordering of this task within the parent work order, used to control execution sequence and dependencies.
attributes.references: AMOS Aircraft Maintenance and Engineering System

attributes.name: task_start_timestamp
attributes.description: Date and time when work on this task was initiated, used for labor tracking, downtime analysis, and task duration measurement.
attributes.references: AMOS Aircraft Maintenance and Engineering System

attributes.name: task_status
attributes.description: Current lifecycle status of the task: open (not started), in_progress (work underway), completed (finished and signed off), deferred (postponed under MEL), cancelled (no longer required).
attributes.references: AMOS Aircraft Maintenance and Engineering System

attributes.name: task_type
attributes.description: Classification of the maintenance task type indicating the nature of work: inspection (visual/NDT), repair (corrective action), replacement (component swap), modification (SB/AD compliance), lubrication, or servicing.

attributes.name: technician_license_number
attributes.description: The Part-66 or equivalent aircraft maintenance license number of the technician who performed the task, required for regulatory traceability and certification compliance.

attributes.name: technician_signoff_timestamp
attributes.description: Date and time when the technician signed off the completed task, certifying that the work was performed in accordance with approved data and procedures.

attributes.name: work_location
attributes.description: Physical location where the task is performed: hangar (heavy maintenance), line (gate/ramp), shop (component workshop), vendor (external MRO facility).
attributes.references: AMOS Aircraft Maintenance and Engineering System

products.name: program
products.description: Approved aircraft maintenance program (AMP) master record defining the scheduled maintenance framework for an aircraft type or individual registration. Captures program revision, EASA/FAA approval reference, maintenance planning document (MPD) baseline, interval structure (flight hours, flight cycles, calendar days), escalation approvals, and effectivity. SSOT for what maintenance is required and at what intervals per regulatory approval.
products.reference: Aircraft Maintenance Programme (AMP) / MPD

attributes.name: program_id
attributes.description: Primary key for program

attributes.name: regulatory_authority_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to compliance.regulatory_authority. Business justification: Maintenance programs require approval from the operator's primary regulatory authority (FAA, EASA, etc.). Tracking this approval is fundamental to Part 121/145 operations, audit compliance, and determ

attributes.name: ad_compliance_status
attributes.description: Overall compliance status of Airworthiness Directives (ADs) incorporated into this maintenance program.

attributes.name: aircraft_registration
attributes.description: Tail number or registration mark of the aircraft to which this maintenance program applies. May be null for type-level programs.

attributes.name: aircraft_type_code
attributes.description: ICAO aircraft type designator (e.g., B738, A320, B77W) defining the aircraft model family for which this maintenance program is approved.

attributes.name: aoc_number
attributes.description: Air Operator Certificate number under which this maintenance program is approved and operated.

attributes.name: approval_date
attributes.description: Date on which the regulatory authority formally approved this maintenance program revision.

attributes.name: approval_reference
attributes.description: Official reference number or certificate identifier issued by the regulatory authority approving this maintenance program.

attributes.name: camo_organization
attributes.description: Name or identifier of the EASA Part-M Subpart G CAMO responsible for managing the continuing airworthiness under this program.

attributes.name: created_timestamp
attributes.description: Timestamp when this maintenance program record was first created in the system.

attributes.name: effective_date
attributes.description: Date from which this maintenance program becomes operationally effective and must be applied to the aircraft or fleet.

attributes.name: effectivity_configuration
attributes.description: Specific aircraft configuration, modification state, or service bulletin incorporation status defining the applicability of this maintenance program.

attributes.name: effectivity_serial_numbers
attributes.description: Comma-separated list or range of aircraft manufacturer serial numbers (MSN) to which this maintenance program applies. Null for type-level programs applicable to all aircraft of the type.

attributes.name: escalation_approval_reference
attributes.description: Regulatory approval reference for any interval escalation applied to this maintenance program. Null if no escalation.

attributes.name: escalation_factor
attributes.description: Multiplier applied to maintenance intervals for escalation purposes (e.g., 1.05 for 5% escalation). Null if no escalation is approved.

attributes.name: expiry_date
attributes.description: Date on which this maintenance program revision expires or is superseded. Null for currently active programs without defined end date.

attributes.name: interval_structure
attributes.description: Primary interval structure used by this maintenance program to schedule tasks: flight hours (FH), flight cycles (FC), calendar days (DY), or combined thresholds.
attributes.references: EASA Part-M, FAA AC 120-16, IATA MSG-3

attributes.name: mel_reference
attributes.description: Reference to the approved Minimum Equipment List (MEL) document associated with this maintenance program, defining permissible equipment deferrals.

attributes.name: modified_by
attributes.description: User identifier or name of the person who last modified this maintenance program record.

attributes.name: modified_timestamp
attributes.description: Timestamp when this maintenance program record was last modified or updated.

attributes.name: mpd_baseline
attributes.description: Manufacturer's Maintenance Planning Document (MPD) baseline version or revision that forms the foundation of this approved maintenance program (e.g., 'Boeing D622W001 Rev 45', 'Airbus A320 MPD Rev 38').

attributes.name: operator_name
attributes.description: Legal name of the airline or aircraft operator to whom this maintenance program is issued and approved.

attributes.name: part_145_organization
attributes.description: Name or identifier of the EASA Part-145 or FAA Part 145 approved maintenance organization responsible for executing this maintenance program.

attributes.name: program_description
attributes.description: Detailed textual description of the maintenance program scope, objectives, and key features.

attributes.name: program_name
attributes.description: Business-friendly name or title of the maintenance program (e.g., 'B737-800 AMP Rev 12', 'A320 Family Maintenance Program').

attributes.name: program_status
attributes.description: Current lifecycle status of the maintenance program indicating its regulatory and operational state. [ENUM-REF-CANDIDATE: draft|pending_approval|approved|active|superseded|withdrawn|archived — 7 candidates stripped; promote to reference product]

attributes.name: program_type
attributes.description: Classification of the maintenance program: AMP (Aircraft Maintenance Program), CMP (Component Maintenance Program), EMP (Engine Maintenance Program), sampling program, MSG-3 based, or other.
attributes.references: EASA Part-M, FAA AC 120-16, IATA MSG-3

attributes.name: reliability_program_reference
attributes.description: Reference to the associated aircraft reliability program or monitoring system that feeds data into maintenance program adjustments.

attributes.name: revision
attributes.description: Revision or version identifier of the maintenance program as approved by the regulatory authority (e.g., 'Rev 12', '2023-01', 'V3.5').

attributes.name: sb_incorporation_status
attributes.description: Status of manufacturer Service Bulletin (SB) incorporation into this maintenance program.

attributes.name: created_by
attributes.description: User identifier or name of the person who created this maintenance program record.

products.name: check
products.description: Scheduled maintenance check event (A-check, B-check, C-check, D-check, line check, transit check) planned or executed against a specific aircraft registration. Records check type, due date, due flight hours, due cycles, actual induction date, release date, station/MRO facility, man-hours consumed, downtime days, and next-due projections. Bridges the maintenance program to actual execution events.
products.reference: AMOS Maintenance Check / Heavy Maintenance Visit (HMV)

attributes.name: check_id
attributes.description: Primary key for check

attributes.name: approved_maintenance_org_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to maintenance.approved_maintenance_org. Business justification: Maintenance check is performed by an approved maintenance organization. The check table has part_145_approval_number and mro_facility_name but no FK. Adding approved_maintenance_org_id FK normalizes t

attributes.name: audit_event_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to compliance.audit_event. Business justification: Major maintenance checks (C-checks, D-checks) are subject to regulatory and internal audits. Linking checks to audit events enables compliance verification, finding resolution tracking, and documentat

attributes.name: budget_plan_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to finance.budget_plan. Business justification: Major maintenance checks are planned against annual maintenance budgets. Links check to budget plan for variance analysis, forecast accuracy tracking, and budget consumption reporting.

attributes.name: certifying_staff_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to maintenance.certifying_staff. Business justification: Maintenance check is certified by a certifying engineer. The check table has certifying_engineer_license (STRING) but no FK. Adding certifying_staff_id FK normalizes this relationship and removes redu

attributes.name: lease_contract_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to finance.lease_contract. Business justification: Major maintenance checks on leased aircraft drive maintenance reserve accruals and lease return condition compliance. Essential for lessor reporting and MR reconciliation at lease expiry.

attributes.name: maintenance_program_id
attributes.description: Reference to the overarching maintenance program that defines the schedule and requirements for this check type. Links to the regulatory-approved maintenance plan.
attributes.references: EASA Part-M, FAA Part 121 Maintenance Programs

attributes.name: maintenance_station_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to airport.station. Business justification: Maintenance checks (A/C/D checks) performed at specific stations. Links maintenance_station_code to station.station_id for hangar capacity planning, check performance tracking by location, and regulat

attributes.name: triggering_occurrence_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to safety.occurrence. Business justification: Major maintenance checks may be triggered by safety occurrences (e.g., heavy landing requiring special inspection). Links unscheduled checks to causal events for fleet-wide risk assessment and regulat

attributes.name: work_order_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to maintenance.work_order. Business justification: Maintenance check is associated with a work order. The check table has work_order_number (STRING) but no FK. Adding work_order_id FK allows proper relational integrity and removes redundant work_order

attributes.name: actual_induction_date
attributes.description: The actual date when the aircraft entered the maintenance facility and work commenced. May differ from scheduled date due to operational constraints.

attributes.name: actual_man_hours
attributes.description: The actual total labor hours consumed during execution of this maintenance check. Used for cost accounting and efficiency analysis.

attributes.name: actual_release_date
attributes.description: The actual date when the aircraft was certified airworthy and released back to operational service after completion of the maintenance check.
attributes.references: EASA Part-145 Release Certificate, FAA Form 8130-3

attributes.name: aircraft_registration
attributes.description: The unique registration identifier (tail number) of the aircraft undergoing this maintenance check. Links to the specific aircraft in the fleet.

attributes.name: airworthiness_directives_complied
attributes.description: The number of mandatory Airworthiness Directives (ADs) complied with during this maintenance check. ADs are legally enforceable safety regulations issued by aviation authorities.
attributes.references: FAA Airworthiness Directives, EASA Airworthiness Directives

attributes.name: aog_event_flag
attributes.description: Boolean indicator of whether this maintenance check was triggered by or resulted in an Aircraft on Ground event, indicating unscheduled downtime with high operational impact.

attributes.name: check_status
attributes.description: Current lifecycle status of the maintenance check event. Tracks progression from planning through execution to completion or cancellation.

attributes.name: check_type
attributes.description: The category of scheduled maintenance check being performed. A-checks are light, frequent inspections; D-checks are heavy overhauls requiring aircraft disassembly.
attributes.references: IATA Maintenance Program Standards, EASA Part-M

attributes.name: completion_timestamp
attributes.description: The precise date and time when all maintenance tasks were completed and the aircraft was certified for return to service. Used for audit trail and performance tracking.

attributes.name: cost_currency_code
attributes.description: The three-letter ISO 4217 currency code for the total cost amount. Airlines operate globally and may incur maintenance costs in multiple currencies.

attributes.name: created_timestamp
attributes.description: The timestamp when this maintenance check record was first created in the system. Part of the audit trail for data lineage and compliance.

attributes.name: defects_found_count
attributes.description: The total number of defects, discrepancies, or non-conformities identified during execution of this maintenance check. Used for quality and reliability analysis.
attributes.references: EASA Part-145 Quality Standards, IATA Safety Management

attributes.name: downtime_days
attributes.description: The total number of days the aircraft was out of service for this maintenance check, calculated from induction to release. Critical for fleet utilization metrics.

attributes.name: due_date
attributes.description: The calendar date by which this maintenance check must be completed to maintain airworthiness certification. Calculated from maintenance program intervals.
attributes.references: EASA Part-M, FAA Part 121 Maintenance Requirements

attributes.name: due_flight_cycles
attributes.description: The cumulative aircraft flight cycles (takeoff-landing pairs) at which this maintenance check is due. Critical for structural fatigue monitoring.
attributes.references: IATA Maintenance Program Standards, ICAO Annex 8

attributes.name: due_flight_hours
attributes.description: The cumulative aircraft flight hours at which this maintenance check is due. One of three interval metrics (hours, cycles, calendar) used to trigger maintenance.

attributes.name: interval_days
attributes.description: The calendar day interval between occurrences of this check type as defined in the maintenance program. For example, A-checks typically occur every 500-800 flight hours or 200-300 cycles or 60-90 days, whichever comes first.
attributes.references: EASA Part-M, Manufacturer Maintenance Planning Documents

attributes.name: interval_flight_cycles
attributes.description: The flight cycle interval between occurrences of this check type as defined in the maintenance program.
attributes.references: EASA Part-M, Manufacturer Maintenance Planning Documents

attributes.name: interval_flight_hours
attributes.description: The flight hour interval between occurrences of this check type as defined in the maintenance program.
attributes.references: EASA Part-M, Manufacturer Maintenance Planning Documents

attributes.name: last_modified_timestamp
attributes.description: The timestamp when this maintenance check record was most recently updated. Tracks data currency and supports change data capture processes.

attributes.name: mel_deferrals_count
attributes.description: The number of defects deferred under Minimum Equipment List provisions during this check, allowing aircraft return to service with specific inoperative equipment.
attributes.references: ICAO Annex 6, FAA MEL Regulations, EASA MEL Standards

attributes.name: next_due_date
attributes.description: The projected calendar date when the next occurrence of this check type will be due, calculated from completion date plus maintenance interval.
attributes.references: EASA Part-M, FAA Part 121 Maintenance Programs

attributes.name: next_due_flight_cycles
attributes.description: The projected cumulative aircraft flight cycles at which the next occurrence of this check type will be due.

attributes.name: next_due_flight_hours
attributes.description: The projected cumulative aircraft flight hours at which the next occurrence of this check type will be due.

attributes.name: planned_man_hours
attributes.description: The estimated total labor hours required to complete this maintenance check, used for resource planning and cost estimation.

attributes.name: release_certificate_number
attributes.business_glossary_term: Certificate of Release to Service (CRS) Number
attributes.description: The unique identifier of the Certificate of Release to Service issued upon completion of this maintenance check, certifying the aircraft is airworthy.

attributes.name: remarks
attributes.description: Free-text field for additional notes, observations, or special circumstances related to this maintenance check. Used for operational context and knowledge transfer.

attributes.name: scheduled_induction_date
attributes.description: The planned date when the aircraft will enter the maintenance facility to begin this check. Used for capacity planning and aircraft rotation scheduling.

attributes.name: scheduled_release_date
attributes.description: The planned date when the aircraft is expected to be released back to service after completion of the maintenance check.

attributes.name: service_bulletins_incorporated
attributes.description: The number of manufacturer service bulletins (recommended but not mandatory modifications or inspections) incorporated during this maintenance check.

attributes.name: total_cost_amount
attributes.description: The total cost incurred for this maintenance check including labor, parts, materials, and overhead. Used for maintenance budget tracking and cost per flight hour analysis.
attributes.references: IATA Maintenance Cost Standards, SAP S/4HANA Cost Accounting

products.name: airworthiness_directive
products.description: Airworthiness Directive (AD) master record issued by FAA, EASA, or national CAA mandating corrective action on aircraft, engines, or components. Captures AD number, issuing authority, effective date, compliance method (one-time/repetitive), threshold (FH/FC/calendar), interval, applicability (aircraft type, serial number range), superseded AD references, and compliance status per tail number. SSOT for regulatory AD tracking.
products.reference: FAA AD / EASA AD

attributes.name: airworthiness_directive_id
attributes.description: Primary key for airworthiness_directive

attributes.name: regulatory_authority_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to compliance.regulatory_authority. Business justification: Airworthiness Directives are issued by regulatory authorities (FAA, EASA, TCCA, etc.). Tracking the issuing authority is fundamental to AD management, compliance verification, and determining applicab

attributes.name: ad_number
attributes.description: Official AD number issued by the regulatory authority (e.g., FAA AD 2023-12-05, EASA AD 2023-0145). Unique identifier assigned by the issuing authority.

attributes.name: ad_status
attributes.description: Current lifecycle status of the AD. Active=currently enforceable, Superseded=replaced by newer AD, Cancelled=no longer applicable, Proposed=under review, Interim=temporary emergency AD.

attributes.name: aircraft_type
attributes.description: Aircraft type designation to which this AD applies (e.g., Boeing 737-800, Airbus A320-200, Embraer E175). May include multiple types if AD applies broadly.
attributes.references: ICAO Annex 8, Type Certificate Data Sheet

attributes.name: airworthiness_directive_description
attributes.description: Detailed description of the unsafe condition, the corrective action required, and the rationale for the airworthiness directive.

attributes.name: alternative_compliance_method
attributes.description: Description of approved Alternative Methods of Compliance (AMOC) that may be used in lieu of the prescribed action, if permitted by the issuing authority.

attributes.name: applicability
attributes.description: Defines which aircraft, engines, propellers, or components are affected by this AD. Includes aircraft type, model, serial number ranges, and part numbers.

attributes.name: compliance_interval_unit
attributes.description: Unit of measure for repetitive compliance interval. FH=Flight Hours, FC=Flight Cycles, days/months/years=calendar time. Null for one-time ADs.

attributes.name: compliance_interval_value
attributes.description: Numeric interval value for repetitive compliance actions (e.g., repeat inspection every 1000 flight hours). Null for one-time ADs.

attributes.name: compliance_method
attributes.description: Type of compliance action required. One-time=single inspection or action, Repetitive=recurring inspections at intervals, Terminating=final action that eliminates need for repetitive compliance.

attributes.name: compliance_threshold_unit
attributes.description: Unit of measure for compliance threshold. FH=Flight Hours, FC=Flight Cycles, days/months/years=calendar time.

attributes.name: compliance_threshold_value
attributes.description: Numeric threshold value at which initial compliance action must be performed (e.g., 5000 flight hours, 2500 flight cycles, 180 calendar days).

attributes.name: component_type
attributes.description: Category of component affected by the AD. Airframe=aircraft structure, Engine=propulsion system, Propeller=propeller assembly, Appliance=accessory or system component, APU=Auxiliary Power Unit.

attributes.name: created_timestamp
attributes.description: Timestamp when this AD record was first created in the system.

attributes.name: document_url
attributes.description: URL link to the official AD document on the issuing authority's website (e.g., FAA AD docket, EASA AD repository).

attributes.name: effective_date
attributes.description: Date when the airworthiness directive becomes legally enforceable and compliance is required.

attributes.name: estimated_cost_per_aircraft
attributes.description: Estimated cost in USD to comply with the AD per affected aircraft, including labor, parts, and downtime. Provided by issuing authority or operator estimate.

attributes.name: estimated_labor_hours
attributes.description: Estimated labor hours required to perform the compliance action per aircraft, as provided by the issuing authority or manufacturer.

attributes.name: issue_date
attributes.description: Date when the airworthiness directive was officially published by the issuing authority.

attributes.name: last_modified_timestamp
attributes.description: Timestamp when this AD record was last updated in the system.

attributes.name: part_number_affected
attributes.description: Specific part number(s) of components affected by this AD. May include multiple part numbers if AD applies to a family of parts.

attributes.name: related_ad_numbers
attributes.description: Comma-separated list of related AD numbers from other authorities addressing the same unsafe condition (e.g., FAA AD referencing equivalent EASA AD).

attributes.name: remarks
attributes.description: Additional notes, clarifications, or operator-specific annotations regarding the AD compliance, interpretation, or fleet impact.

attributes.name: serial_number_range
attributes.description: Serial number range of aircraft or components to which this AD applies (e.g., 'S/N 1001 through 5000'). Null if AD applies to all serial numbers.

attributes.name: subject
attributes.description: Brief title or subject line describing the nature of the airworthiness directive (e.g., 'Engine Fan Blade Inspection', 'Landing Gear Actuator Replacement').

attributes.name: superseded_ad_number
attributes.description: AD number(s) that this directive supersedes or replaces. Multiple ADs may be listed if this AD consolidates previous directives. Null if no supersession.

products.name: ad_compliance
products.description: Compliance record tracking the status of each Airworthiness Directive against each applicable aircraft or component. Records compliance method selected, accomplishment date, flight hours at accomplishment, cycles at accomplishment, next-due date/hours/cycles for repetitive ADs, work order reference, certifying staff sign-off, and open/closed/deferred status. Enables airworthiness compliance reporting to FAA/EASA/CAA.
products.reference: AMOS AD Compliance Tracking

attributes.references: ICAO Annex 7 - Aircraft Nationality and Registration Marks

attributes.name: aog_risk_flag
attributes.description: Boolean flag indicating whether this deferral poses a high risk of causing an AOG event if not rectified promptly (true) or not (false).
attributes.references: AMOS Aircraft Maintenance and Engineering System

attributes.name: certifying_staff_license_number
attributes.description: The license or authorization number of the certifying staff who approved the deferral.

attributes.name: closure_date
attributes.description: The date on which the MEL deferral record was administratively closed in the maintenance system. Null if still open.
attributes.references: AMOS Aircraft Maintenance and Engineering System

attributes.name: closure_remarks
attributes.description: Free-text remarks or notes recorded when the deferral was closed, including any follow-up actions or observations.
attributes.references: AMOS Aircraft Maintenance and Engineering System

attributes.name: created_timestamp
attributes.description: The timestamp when this MEL deferral record was first created in the maintenance system.
attributes.references: AMOS Aircraft Maintenance and Engineering System

attributes.name: deferral_description
attributes.description: Free-text description of the inoperative item and the nature of the deferral, including any operational restrictions or procedures.
attributes.references: AMOS Aircraft Maintenance and Engineering System

attributes.name: deferral_expiry_date
attributes.description: The date by which the deferred item must be rectified according to the MEL category interval. Null if no expiry applies (Category A).
attributes.references: FAA Master Minimum Equipment List (MMEL), EASA CS-MMEL

attributes.name: deferral_open_date
attributes.description: The date on which the MEL deferral was opened and the item was deferred from service.

attributes.name: deferral_open_timestamp
attributes.description: The precise timestamp when the MEL deferral was opened in the maintenance system.
attributes.references: AMOS Aircraft Maintenance and Engineering System

attributes.name: deferral_status
attributes.description: Current lifecycle status of the MEL deferral: open (active), extended (interval extended), rectified (repair completed), closed (administratively closed), expired (exceeded allowed interval).
attributes.references: AMOS Aircraft Maintenance and Engineering System

attributes.name: extension_authority
attributes.description: The name or identifier of the authority (e.g., Chief Engineer, Maintenance Control) who approved the deferral extension.

attributes.name: extension_count
attributes.description: The number of times the deferral expiry date has been extended beyond the original MEL category interval.
attributes.references: AMOS Aircraft Maintenance and Engineering System

attributes.name: flight_cycles_at_deferral
attributes.description: The total accumulated flight cycles (takeoff-landing cycles) on the aircraft at the time the MEL deferral was opened.
attributes.references: AMOS Aircraft Maintenance and Engineering System

attributes.name: flight_hours_at_deferral
attributes.description: The total accumulated flight hours (block hours) on the aircraft at the time the MEL deferral was opened.
attributes.references: AMOS Aircraft Maintenance and Engineering System

attributes.name: last_extension_date
attributes.description: The date of the most recent extension of the deferral expiry date. Null if never extended.
attributes.references: AMOS Aircraft Maintenance and Engineering System

attributes.name: last_modified_timestamp
attributes.description: The timestamp when this MEL deferral record was last updated in the maintenance system.
attributes.references: AMOS Aircraft Maintenance and Engineering System

attributes.name: maintenance_procedures_applied
attributes.description: Description of any maintenance procedures or placarding actions performed when the deferral was opened (e.g., circuit breaker collared, placard installed).
attributes.references: AMOS Aircraft Maintenance and Engineering System

attributes.name: mel_category
attributes.description: The MEL category defining the operational constraints and rectification interval: A (no dispatch allowed), B (rectify within 3 days), C (rectify within 10 days), D (rectify within 120 days).
attributes.references: FAA Master Minimum Equipment List (MMEL), EASA CS-MMEL

attributes.name: operational_restrictions
attributes.description: Specific operational restrictions or limitations imposed by the MEL deferral (e.g., flight altitude limits, route restrictions, weather minimums).
attributes.references: FAA Master Minimum Equipment List (MMEL), EASA CS-MMEL

attributes.name: rectification_date
attributes.description: The date on which the deferred item was rectified and returned to service. Null if not yet rectified.
attributes.references: AMOS Aircraft Maintenance and Engineering System

attributes.name: rectification_station_code
attributes.description: The IATA three-letter airport code of the station where the deferred item was rectified. Null if not yet rectified.

attributes.name: rectification_timestamp
attributes.description: The precise timestamp when the deferred item was rectified and the deferral was closed.
attributes.references: AMOS Aircraft Maintenance and Engineering System

attributes.name: regulatory_notification_date
attributes.description: The date on which the civil aviation authority was notified of this deferral. Null if notification not required or not yet sent.

attributes.name: regulatory_notification_required
attributes.description: Boolean flag indicating whether this deferral requires notification to the civil aviation authority (true) or not (false).

products.name: component
products.description: Aircraft component and rotable part master record tracking individual serialised and batch-tracked parts across the fleet. Captures part number (P/N), serial number (S/N), ATA chapter, component description, manufacturer, life-limited part (LLP) flag, total time since new (TTSN), total cycles since new (TCSN), time since overhaul (TSO), cycles since overhaul (CSO), current location (aircraft/shop/store), airworthiness release certificate (CRS/Form 1/8130-3) reference, and serviceable/unserviceable status.
products.reference: AMOS Component / Rotable Master

attributes.name: component_id
attributes.description: Unique identifier for the aircraft component or rotable part record. Primary key.
attributes.references: AMOS Aircraft Maintenance and Engineering System

attributes.name: ad_compliance_record_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to compliance.ad_compliance_record. Business justification: Components are subject to component-specific Airworthiness Directives. Linking components to their AD compliance records enables tracking of component-level AD compliance (distinct from aircraft-level

attributes.name: aircraft_id
attributes.description: Reference to the aircraft on which this component is currently installed, if applicable. Null if component is in shop or store.
attributes.references: AMOS Aircraft Maintenance and Engineering System

attributes.name: failure_occurrence_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to safety.occurrence. Business justification: Component failures causing safety occurrences need direct linkage for reliability analysis and fleet-wide risk assessment. Enables component-level safety performance tracking, supports manufacturer re

attributes.name: fixed_asset_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to finance.fixed_asset. Business justification: Rotable components meeting capitalization thresholds are fixed assets. Links component to asset record for depreciation tracking, NBV reporting, and asset disposal accounting.

attributes.name: hazard_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to safety.hazard. Business justification: Specific components may be associated with identified hazards (design flaws, known failure modes). Link supports component-level risk tracking, informs procurement decisions, and enables targeted moni

attributes.name: lease_contract_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to finance.lease_contract. Business justification: Components on leased aircraft must track lease contract for lease return inventory reconciliation, maintenance reserve claims, and lessor asset tracking. Required for lease return audits.

attributes.name: vendor_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to procurement.vendor. Business justification: Tracks OEM/supplier of installed component for warranty claims, AD applicability verification, and approved source compliance. Real process: airworthiness staff verify component pedigree against appro

attributes.name: acquisition_cost
attributes.description: Original purchase or acquisition cost of the component in the airlines functional currency. Used for asset valuation and depreciation calculations.

attributes.name: airworthiness_certificate_date
attributes.description: Issue date of the current airworthiness release certificate for this component.

attributes.name: airworthiness_certificate_number
attributes.description: Unique reference number of the airworthiness release certificate (EASA Form 1, FAA 8130-3, or equivalent) certifying this component as airworthy and fit for installation.

attributes.name: airworthiness_certificate_type
attributes.description: Type of airworthiness release certificate accompanying this component. EASA Form 1, FAA Form 8130-3, and CAA CRS are the most common authorized release certificates.

attributes.name: ata_chapter
attributes.description: ATA iSpec 2200 chapter code classifying the component by aircraft system (e.g., 32 for landing gear, 71 for powerplant, 24 for electrical). Industry-standard taxonomy for aircraft systems.

attributes.name: batch_number
attributes.description: Manufacturing batch or lot number for batch-tracked components. Used for traceability in case of manufacturing defects or airworthiness directives. Null for serialized-only components.

attributes.name: component_description
attributes.description: Detailed textual description of the component including type, function, and key characteristics. Used for identification and maintenance planning.
attributes.references: AMOS Aircraft Maintenance and Engineering System

attributes.name: condition_code
attributes.description: Two-letter ATA Spec 2000 condition code indicating the maintenance and airworthiness status of the component (e.g., AR=As Removed, OH=Overhauled, NE=New, RP=Repaired, SV=Serviceable).

attributes.name: created_timestamp
attributes.description: Timestamp when this component record was first created in the maintenance system.
attributes.references: AMOS Aircraft Maintenance and Engineering System

attributes.name: criticality_classification
attributes.description: Classification of the components criticality to flight operations and safety. AOG-critical components ground the aircraft if unserviceable, flight-safety components affect airworthiness, operational components affect dispatch reliability.
attributes.references: ATA MSG-3, AMOS Aircraft Maintenance and Engineering System

attributes.name: currency_code
attributes.description: Three-letter ISO 4217 currency code for the acquisition cost and other monetary values associated with this component.

attributes.name: current_location_code
attributes.description: Code identifying the specific location where the component is currently held. May be aircraft registration, shop code, warehouse code, or station code depending on location type.
attributes.references: IATA Airport Codes, AMOS Aircraft Maintenance and Engineering System

attributes.name: current_location_type
attributes.description: Type of location where the component is currently held. Aircraft indicates installed on aircraft, shop indicates undergoing maintenance, store indicates warehouse inventory, quarantine indicates awaiting inspection, scrap indicates condemned.
attributes.references: AMOS Aircraft Maintenance and Engineering System

attributes.name: cycles_remaining_to_limit
attributes.description: Flight cycles remaining before the component reaches its life limit or next scheduled maintenance event. Null if not applicable or unlimited.

attributes.name: cycles_since_overhaul
attributes.description: Flight cycles accumulated since the last major overhaul or shop visit. Reset to zero after overhaul. Null if component has never been overhauled.

attributes.name: installation_date
attributes.description: Date when the component was installed on the current aircraft. Null if component is not currently installed on an aircraft.

attributes.name: last_modified_timestamp
attributes.description: Timestamp when this component record was last updated in the maintenance system.
attributes.references: AMOS Aircraft Maintenance and Engineering System

attributes.name: last_overhaul_date
attributes.description: Date when the component last underwent major overhaul or shop visit. Null if component has never been overhauled.

attributes.name: life_limited_part_flag
attributes.description: Indicates whether this component is a life-limited part subject to mandatory retirement at specified life limits per airworthiness directives. True if LLP, false otherwise.

attributes.name: maintenance_organization_code
attributes.description: Approval code of the Part-145 approved maintenance organization that last performed maintenance or issued the airworthiness certificate for this component.

attributes.name: manufacture_date
attributes.description: Date when the component was originally manufactured by the OEM. Used for age-based maintenance requirements and warranty tracking.

attributes.name: manufacturer_code
attributes.description: Standardized code identifying the component manufacturer. Typically ICAO or industry-standard manufacturer identifier.

attributes.name: manufacturer_name
attributes.description: Name of the original equipment manufacturer (OEM) who produced this component.

attributes.name: owner_type
attributes.description: Ownership classification of the component. Owned indicates airline-owned, leased indicates leased from lessor, pooled indicates part of rotable pool agreement, consignment indicates supplier-owned inventory.
attributes.references: AMOS Aircraft Maintenance and Engineering System

attributes.name: part_number
attributes.description: Manufacturer part number identifying the component type. Standard alphanumeric identifier used across aviation industry for component cataloging.
attributes.references: IATA Standard Schedules Information Manual (SSIM), ATA Spec 2000

attributes.name: removal_date
attributes.description: Date when the component was last removed from an aircraft. Null if component has never been installed or is currently installed.

attributes.name: removal_reason
attributes.description: Reason code for the last removal of this component from an aircraft. Used for reliability analysis and maintenance planning. [ENUM-REF-CANDIDATE: scheduled_maintenance|unscheduled_maintenance|defect|llp_limit|modification|aog|inspection|lease_return|other — 9 candidates stripped; promote to reference product]
attributes.references: ATA MSG-3, AMOS Aircraft Maintenance and Engineering System

attributes.name: rotable_flag
attributes.description: Indicates whether this component is a rotable (repairable) part that can be overhauled and returned to service, as opposed to expendable parts. True if rotable, false if expendable.
attributes.references: AMOS Aircraft Maintenance and Engineering System

attributes.name: serial_number
attributes.description: Unique serial number assigned by the manufacturer to this individual component instance. Enables traceability throughout component lifecycle.
attributes.references: EASA Part-145, FAA AC 120-16F, ATA Spec 2000

attributes.name: serviceable_status
attributes.description: Current airworthiness and serviceability status of the component. Serviceable indicates ready for installation, unserviceable indicates requires maintenance, quarantine indicates awaiting inspection. [ENUM-REF-CANDIDATE: serviceable|unserviceable|repairable|beyond_economic_repair|condemned|quarantine|inspection_required — 7 candidates stripped; promote to reference product]

attributes.name: shelf_life_expiry_date
attributes.description: Date when the component reaches the end of its shelf life and must be inspected, tested, or scrapped. Applicable to time-sensitive components such as rubber seals, batteries, and life vests. Null if not applicable.
attributes.references: ATA Spec 2000, AMOS Aircraft Maintenance and Engineering System

attributes.name: time_remaining_to_limit
attributes.description: Flight hours remaining before the component reaches its life limit or next scheduled maintenance event. Measured in hours. Null if not applicable or unlimited.

attributes.name: time_since_overhaul
attributes.description: Flight hours accumulated since the last major overhaul or shop visit. Measured in hours. Reset to zero after overhaul. Null if component has never been overhauled.

attributes.name: total_cycles_since_new
attributes.description: Cumulative flight cycles (takeoff/landing cycles) accumulated by this component since original manufacture. Critical for fatigue-sensitive components and LLP tracking.

attributes.name: total_time_since_new
attributes.description: Cumulative flight hours accumulated by this component since original manufacture. Measured in hours. Critical for life-limited part tracking and maintenance scheduling.

attributes.name: warranty_expiry_date
attributes.description: Date when the manufacturer or overhaul shop warranty for this component expires. Null if no warranty applies.
attributes.references: AMOS Aircraft Maintenance and Engineering System

products.name: llp_status
products.description: Life-Limited Part (LLP) status record tracking the accumulated life consumption of each LLP against its certified life limit (cycles, flight hours, or calendar). Captures part number, serial number, life limit type, certified limit value, accumulated value, remaining life, last update flight/cycle reference, and alert threshold. Critical for airworthiness — LLPs must be retired at or before their certified limit. Primarily applies to engine LLPs (discs, shafts, hubs) and landing gear components.
products.reference: AMOS LLP Tracking / Engine Life Management

attributes.name: llp_status_id
attributes.description: Unique identifier for the life-limited part status record. Primary key.

attributes.name: aircraft_id
attributes.description: Reference to the aircraft on which this life-limited part is installed.

attributes.name: component_id
attributes.description: Reference to the parent component or assembly (e.g., engine, landing gear) containing this LLP.

attributes.name: flight_leg_id
attributes.description: Reference to the most recent flight after which the accumulated life was updated. Ensures traceability of life consumption.

attributes.name: removal_work_order_id
attributes.description: Reference to the maintenance work order under which the LLP was removed. Provides traceability to the removal event.

attributes.name: accumulated_life
attributes.description: The total life consumed by the LLP since new or since last overhaul, expressed in the unit defined by life_limit_type. Updated after each flight or maintenance event.

attributes.name: airworthiness_directive_compliance
attributes.description: Indicates whether the LLP is compliant with all applicable Airworthiness Directives issued by aviation authorities. Non-compliance may ground the aircraft.

attributes.name: alert_threshold
attributes.description: The remaining life value at which maintenance planning alerts are triggered. Typically set to allow sufficient lead time for part procurement and scheduling (e.g., 1000 cycles before limit).

attributes.name: alert_threshold_percentage
attributes.description: Alert threshold expressed as a percentage of certified life limit. Typically set between 5% and 15% remaining life.

attributes.name: certified_life_limit
attributes.description: The maximum allowable life of the LLP as certified by the manufacturer and approved by the aviation authority. Expressed in the unit defined by life_limit_type (e.g., 20000 cycles, 50000 flight hours). The part MUST be retired at or before this limit.
attributes.references: EASA Part-M, FAA AC 120-17A, ICAO Annex 8

attributes.name: created_timestamp
attributes.description: Timestamp when this LLP status record was first created in the system. Part of the audit trail.

attributes.name: installation_cycles_at_install
attributes.description: The accumulated cycles on the LLP at the time of installation on the current aircraft or component. Used to calculate total life consumption.

attributes.name: installation_date
attributes.description: Date when the LLP was installed on the current aircraft or component. Critical for calendar-based life tracking.

attributes.name: installation_flight_number
attributes.description: Flight number or operational reference at the time of LLP installation. Provides traceability to the installation event.

attributes.name: last_overhaul_date
attributes.description: Date of the most recent overhaul or refurbishment of the LLP. Null if the part has never been overhauled.

attributes.name: last_update_timestamp
attributes.description: Timestamp when the LLP status record was last updated with new accumulated life data. Critical for data currency verification.

attributes.name: life_limit_type
attributes.description: The unit of measure by which the LLP life is tracked: cycles (takeoff/landing cycles), flight hours, calendar days, or a combination. Defined by the manufacturer and certified by the aviation authority.

attributes.name: llp_category
attributes.description: Classification of the LLP by component type. Engine LLPs (discs, shafts, hubs) and landing gear components are the most common.

attributes.name: llp_status_status
attributes.description: Current operational status of the LLP: serviceable (within normal operating range), alert (approaching threshold), critical (near limit), expired (at or beyond limit, must be removed), removed (no longer installed).

attributes.name: maintenance_organization_code
attributes.description: Code of the Part-145 approved maintenance organization responsible for tracking and maintaining this LLP. Critical for regulatory compliance.

attributes.name: manufacturer_name
attributes.description: Name of the OEM (Original Equipment Manufacturer) who produced the LLP (e.g., GE Aviation, Pratt & Whitney, Rolls-Royce, Safran).

attributes.name: modified_timestamp
attributes.description: Timestamp when this LLP status record was last modified. Part of the audit trail for regulatory compliance.

attributes.name: next_inspection_due_life
attributes.description: The accumulated life value at which the next scheduled inspection of the LLP is due. May be required before the certified life limit.

attributes.name: overhaul_count
attributes.description: Number of times the LLP has been overhauled or refurbished. Some LLPs may be overhauled with life extension, others are single-life components.

attributes.name: part_number
attributes.description: Manufacturer part number identifying the specific LLP type (e.g., engine disc, shaft, hub). Critical for airworthiness tracking.

attributes.name: remaining_life
attributes.description: The remaining life before the LLP reaches its certified limit, calculated as certified_life_limit minus accumulated_life. Critical for maintenance planning and AOG prevention.

attributes.name: remaining_life_percentage
attributes.description: Percentage of remaining life relative to the certified limit, calculated as (remaining_life / certified_life_limit) * 100. Used for threshold alerting and planning.

attributes.name: remarks
attributes.description: Free-text field for additional notes, special conditions, or maintenance history relevant to the LLP status. Used for operational context and audit trail.

attributes.name: removal_date
attributes.description: Date when the LLP was removed from service. Null if the part is still installed and serviceable.

attributes.name: removal_reason
attributes.description: Reason for LLP removal from service: life limit reached (planned retirement), scheduled maintenance, unscheduled removal (defect), AOG event, or component replacement.

attributes.name: serial_number
attributes.description: Unique serial number of the individual LLP unit. Each LLP must be individually tracked throughout its lifecycle.

attributes.name: service_bulletin_compliance
attributes.description: Indicates whether the LLP is compliant with all applicable manufacturer Service Bulletins. Some SBs are mandatory for continued airworthiness.

products.name: component_removal
products.description: Component removal and installation transaction recording the physical swap of a serialised component on an aircraft. Captures removal reason (scheduled/unscheduled/defect/upgrade), removed component S/N, installed component S/N, aircraft registration, ATA position, station, technician, work order reference, aircraft hours/cycles at removal, and CRS reference. Maintains the full fitment history and traceability chain for each component.

Real process: warranty claims require proof of replacement part procurement; finance allocates

attributes.name: ad_reference_number
attributes.description: Reference number of the airworthiness directive that mandated the component removal, if applicable. ADs are mandatory safety directives issued by aviation authorities.

attributes.name: aircraft_registration
attributes.description: The tail number or registration mark of the aircraft from which the component was removed. Unique identifier assigned by the national civil aviation authority.

attributes.name: aircraft_total_cycles_at_removal
attributes.description: Cumulative total flight cycles (takeoff and landing pairs) recorded on the aircraft at the time the component was removed. Critical for fatigue-sensitive component tracking.

attributes.name: aircraft_total_hours_at_removal
attributes.description: Cumulative total flight hours recorded on the aircraft at the time the component was removed. Used for component life tracking and trend analysis.

attributes.name: aog_event_flag
attributes.description: Boolean indicator of whether this component removal was part of an AOG event (aircraft grounded and unable to operate). True indicates AOG situation requiring expedited parts and maintenance.

attributes.name: ata_chapter
attributes.description: Two-digit ATA chapter code identifying the aircraft system to which the component belongs (e.g., 32 for Landing Gear, 71 for Power Plant).

attributes.name: ata_position_code
attributes.description: Specific location code on the aircraft where the component is installed (e.g., LH-ENG-1 for left engine position 1). Defines the physical mounting point.

attributes.name: component_cycles_at_removal
attributes.description: Total operating cycles accumulated by the removed component since new or since last overhaul. Critical for life-limited parts tracking.

attributes.name: component_cycles_since_new
attributes.description: Total cycles the removed component has operated since it was manufactured (cycles since new). Never resets, tracks full component life.

attributes.name: component_hours_at_removal
attributes.description: Total operating hours accumulated by the removed component since new or since last overhaul. Used to determine remaining life and maintenance intervals.

attributes.name: component_time_since_new_hours
attributes.description: Total hours the removed component has operated since it was manufactured (time since new). Never resets, tracks full component life.

attributes.name: crs_reference_number
attributes.business_glossary_term: Certificate of Release to Service (CRS) Reference Number
attributes.description: Reference number of the Certificate of Release to Service document that authorizes the aircraft to return to operation after the component installation. Required by EASA Part-145.

attributes.name: installation_date
attributes.description: Calendar date on which the replacement component was installed on the aircraft.

attributes.name: installation_timestamp
attributes.description: Precise date and time when the replacement component installation was completed and recorded in the maintenance system.

attributes.name: installed_component_condition_code
attributes.description: Condition of the replacement component at installation: new from manufacturer, overhauled (zero-timed), serviceable (used but airworthy), or repaired.

attributes.name: installed_component_part_number
attributes.description: Manufacturer part number of the replacement component that was installed on the aircraft. May be same or alternate part number as removed component.

attributes.name: installed_component_serial_number
attributes.description: Unique serial number of the replacement component that was installed. Establishes the new fitment record for the aircraft position.

attributes.name: mel_deferral_reference
attributes.description: Reference number of the MEL deferral if the component removal was deferred under minimum equipment list provisions, allowing aircraft operation with the defect.

attributes.name: record_created_timestamp
attributes.description: System timestamp when this component removal record was first created in the maintenance management system.

attributes.name: record_updated_timestamp
attributes.description: System timestamp when this component removal record was last modified in the maintenance management system.

attributes.name: removal_date
attributes.description: Calendar date on which the component was physically removed from the aircraft.

attributes.name: removal_reason_code
attributes.description: Classification of why the component was removed: scheduled maintenance, unscheduled failure, defect found, upgrade/modification, inspection requirement, life-limited part expiry, or airworthiness directive compliance. [ENUM-REF-CANDIDATE: scheduled|unscheduled|defect|upgrade|inspection|life_limit|ad_compliance — 7 candidates stripped; promote to reference product]

attributes.name: removal_reason_description
attributes.description: Detailed free-text explanation of the reason for component removal, including any defect descriptions, pilot reports, or maintenance findings that triggered the removal.

attributes.name: removal_timestamp
attributes.description: Precise date and time when the component removal was completed and recorded in the maintenance system.

attributes.name: removed_component_condition_code
attributes.description: Assessment of the removed component condition: serviceable (can be reused as-is), unserviceable (requires maintenance), repairable (can be overhauled), beyond repair, or scrap (must be disposed).

attributes.name: sb_reference_number
attributes.description: Reference number of the manufacturer service bulletin that recommended or required the component removal, if applicable. Service bulletins are OEM-issued maintenance instructions.

attributes.name: transaction_status
attributes.description: Current workflow status of the component removal transaction: draft (initiated), in progress (work underway), completed (physical work done), certified (CRS issued), or cancelled.
attributes.references: AMOS Aircraft Maintenance and Engineering System

attributes.name: warranty_claim_flag
attributes.description: Boolean indicator of whether the component removal is eligible for warranty claim against the manufacturer or vendor. True indicates warranty coverage applies.

Critical for operational recovery and MRO performance measurement.
