attributes.description: The date on which the certifying staff member commenced employment or contract with the current maintenance organisation.

attributes.name: employment_status
attributes.description: Current employment or contract status of the certifying staff member with the maintenance organisation. Active = currently employed and authorized; Inactive = on leave or temporarily not working; Suspended = authorization withdrawn pending investigation; Terminated = no longer employed.

attributes.name: full_name
attributes.description: The full legal name of the certifying staff member as it appears on their licence and official identification documents.
attributes.references: EASA Part-66, FAA Part 65, GDPR Article 4

attributes.name: issuing_authority
attributes.description: The national aviation authority or regulatory body that issued the licence (e.g., EASA, FAA, CAAC, DGCA, Transport Canada). This determines the regulatory framework and reciprocity agreements applicable to the licence.

attributes.name: last_modified_timestamp
attributes.description: The timestamp when this certifying staff record was last updated. Used for audit trail and change tracking.

attributes.name: last_recency_activity_date
attributes.description: The date of the most recent maintenance activity that counts toward recency requirements. Used to calculate whether the certifying staff member remains current.
attributes.references: EASA Part-66, Part-145 Maintenance Organisation Approval

attributes.name: licence_category
attributes.description: The category of aircraft maintenance licence held. EASA categories: A (line maintenance), B1 (mechanical systems), B2 (avionics), B3 (non-pressurized piston aircraft), C (base maintenance). FAA: A&P (Airframe and Powerplant).

attributes.name: licence_expiry_date
attributes.description: The date on which the aircraft maintenance licence expires and must be renewed. Critical for compliance tracking and work assignment eligibility.

attributes.name: licence_issue_date
attributes.description: The date on which the aircraft maintenance licence was originally issued by the regulatory authority.

attributes.name: licence_number
attributes.description: The unique aircraft maintenance engineer (AME) or Airframe and Powerplant (A&P) licence number issued by the national aviation authority. This is the regulatory identifier that authorizes the individual to certify maintenance work.
attributes.references: EASA Part-66, FAA Part 65, ICAO Annex 1

attributes.name: licence_subcategory
attributes.description: The subcategory or endorsement within the licence category, such as B1.1 (turbine aeroplanes), B1.2 (piston aeroplanes), B1.3 (turbine helicopters), B1.4 (piston helicopters), B2 (avionics). Defines the specific aircraft propulsion and structural systems the licence holder is qualified for.

attributes.name: medical_certificate_expiry_date
attributes.description: The expiry date of the medical certificate required for certifying staff in some jurisdictions. Ensures the individual is medically fit to perform safety-critical maintenance tasks.
attributes.references: ICAO Annex 1, National Aviation Authority Medical Standards

attributes.name: next_training_due_date
attributes.description: The date by which the certifying staff member must complete their next recurrent training to maintain authorization. Critical for proactive compliance management.

attributes.name: part_145_organization_code
attributes.description: The approval code of the Part-145 maintenance organisation that currently employs or contracts this certifying staff member. This links the individual to the approved maintenance organisation under which they are authorized to issue Certificates of Release to Service (CRS).

attributes.name: phone_number
attributes.description: Primary contact phone number for emergency callouts, Aircraft on Ground (AOG) situations, and operational coordination.

attributes.name: recency_experience_status
attributes.description: Indicates whether the certifying staff member has maintained the required recency of experience (e.g., performed maintenance within the last 2 years on the relevant aircraft type) as mandated by Part-66 and Part-145. Current = meets recency requirements; Lapsed = recency expired, requalification needed; Suspended = temporarily not authorized.
attributes.references: EASA Part-66, Part-145 Maintenance Organisation Approval

attributes.name: remarks
attributes.description: Free-text field for additional notes, special qualifications, limitations, or administrative comments related to the certifying staff member (e.g., authorized for AOG callouts, restricted to line maintenance only, pending type rating renewal).

attributes.name: shift_pattern
attributes.description: The typical shift or roster pattern for the certifying staff member (e.g., day shift, night shift, rotating 4-on-3-off, on-call). Used for crew scheduling and availability planning.

attributes.name: staff_number
attributes.description: The externally-known employee or contractor identifier assigned by the maintenance organization or airline HR system. Used for payroll, access control, and work order assignment.

attributes.name: training_completion_date
attributes.description: The date on which the certifying staff member completed their most recent mandatory training (e.g., type rating course, human factors, dangerous goods, SMS). Used for compliance tracking and audit trails.
attributes.references: EASA Part-145, FAA Part 145, IATA Training Standards

attributes.name: type_ratings
attributes.description: Comma-separated list of aircraft type ratings held by the certifying staff member (e.g., B737, A320, B777, A350). Type ratings authorize the individual to certify maintenance on specific aircraft models.
attributes.references: EASA Part-66, FAA Part 65, ICAO Annex 1

products.name: forecast
products.description: Forward-looking maintenance planning forecast record projecting when each aircraft will next reach scheduled maintenance thresholds (check due dates, component hard-time limits, AD repetitive intervals). Captures tail number, forecast type (A/C/D-check, LLP retirement, AD repetitive), projected due date, projected due FH, projected due FC, planning horizon, confidence level, and last recalculation timestamp. Enables long-range maintenance planning and hangar slot reservation.
products.reference: AMOS Maintenance Forecast / Long-Range Planning

attributes.name: forecast_id
attributes.description: Primary key for forecast

attributes.name: approved_maintenance_org_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to maintenance.approved_maintenance_org. Business justification: Maintenance forecast identifies the maintenance organization. The forecast table has part_145_organization_code (STRING) but no FK. Adding approved_maintenance_org_id FK normalizes this and removes re

attributes.name: budget_plan_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to finance.budget_plan. Business justification: Maintenance forecasts feed annual budget planning. Links forecast to budget plan for multi-year planning, budget version control, and forecast-to-actual variance analysis.

attributes.name: component_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to maintenance.component. Business justification: Maintenance forecast may be for a specific component. The forecast table has component_part_number and component_serial_number but no FK. Adding component_id FK normalizes this and removes redundant c

attributes.name: maintenance_program_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to maintenance.program. Business justification: Maintenance forecast is based on a maintenance program. The forecast table has maintenance_program_reference (STRING) but no FK. Adding maintenance_program_id FK normalizes this and removes redundant

attributes.name: purchase_order_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to procurement.purchase_order. Business justification: Links forecasted maintenance event to advance parts procurement for long-lead-time items (engines, landing gear). Real process: maintenance planning triggers PO 6-12 months ahead of forecast check; pr

attributes.name: aircraft_registration
attributes.description: Tail number uniquely identifying the aircraft for which this forecast applies. Links to fleet master data.
attributes.references: ICAO Annex 7 - Aircraft Nationality and Registration Marks

attributes.name: airworthiness_directive_number
attributes.description: Official AD number issued by the aviation authority (FAA, EASA, etc.) when the forecast pertains to a repetitive AD compliance interval.

attributes.name: ata_chapter
attributes.description: Two-digit ATA chapter code categorizing the aircraft system or component subject to the forecasted maintenance (e.g., 32 for Landing Gear, 71 for Powerplant).

attributes.name: average_daily_utilization_cycles
attributes.description: Average flight cycles per day for this aircraft over the recent historical period, used to project future due dates from cycle-based intervals.

attributes.name: average_daily_utilization_hours
attributes.description: Average flight hours per day for this aircraft over the recent historical period, used to project future due dates from hour-based intervals.

attributes.name: calculation_timestamp
attributes.description: Date and time when this forecast record was calculated or last recalculated. Used to track forecast freshness and trigger recalculation cycles.

attributes.name: confidence_level
attributes.description: Qualitative assessment of forecast accuracy based on data quality, utilization stability, and planning assumptions. High indicates stable utilization and reliable data; low indicates volatile operations or incomplete data.

attributes.name: created_timestamp
attributes.description: Timestamp when this forecast record was first created in the system. Part of audit trail for data lineage and compliance.

attributes.name: current_flight_cycles
attributes.description: Current cumulative flight cycles on the aircraft or component at the time of forecast calculation. Baseline for projecting due thresholds.

attributes.name: current_flight_hours
attributes.description: Current cumulative flight hours on the aircraft or component at the time of forecast calculation. Baseline for projecting due thresholds.

attributes.name: estimated_cost_usd
attributes.description: Projected total cost in US dollars for the forecasted maintenance event, including labor, parts, and overhead. Used for budget planning and financial forecasting.
attributes.references: Internal Finance and Maintenance Planning Standard

attributes.name: estimated_downtime_days
attributes.description: Projected number of days the aircraft will be out of service (AOG or in maintenance) to complete the forecasted maintenance event.

attributes.name: estimated_labor_hours
attributes.description: Projected total labor hours required to complete the forecasted maintenance task, used for resource planning and cost estimation.
attributes.references: ATA MSG-3 / Internal Maintenance Planning Standard

attributes.name: forecast_status
attributes.description: Current lifecycle status of the forecast record. Active forecasts are used for planning; superseded forecasts have been replaced by newer calculations; completed forecasts correspond to executed maintenance events.

attributes.name: forecast_type
attributes.description: Category of maintenance event being forecasted: scheduled check (A/C/D), life-limited part retirement, airworthiness directive repetitive interval, or APU overhaul.
attributes.references: EASA Part-M / FAA Part 43 Maintenance Program Standards

attributes.name: hangar_slot_reservation_required
attributes.description: Indicates whether this forecasted maintenance event requires advance reservation of hangar capacity and maintenance slots at a Part-145 facility.

attributes.name: last_modified_timestamp
attributes.description: Timestamp when this forecast record was last updated. Tracks data currency and supports change auditing.

attributes.name: maintenance_station_code
attributes.description: Three-letter IATA or ICAO station code of the planned maintenance facility or base where the forecasted maintenance is expected to be performed.
attributes.references: IATA Airport Codes / ICAO Location Indicators

attributes.name: maintenance_task_code
attributes.description: Alphanumeric code identifying the specific maintenance task or check from the Maintenance Planning Document (MPD) or maintenance program.
attributes.references: ATA iSpec 2200 / MSG-3 Maintenance Program Development

attributes.name: planning_horizon_days
attributes.description: Number of days from the forecast calculation date to the projected due date. Indicates how far in advance this maintenance event is being planned.

attributes.name: projected_due_date
attributes.description: Forecasted calendar date when the maintenance event is expected to become due based on current utilization trends and remaining intervals.

attributes.name: projected_due_flight_cycles
attributes.description: Forecasted cumulative flight cycles (takeoff-landing pairs) at which the maintenance event will become due. Used for cycle-based maintenance intervals.

attributes.name: projected_due_flight_hours
attributes.description: Forecasted cumulative flight hours at which the maintenance event will become due. Used for hour-based maintenance intervals.

attributes.name: remaining_flight_cycles
attributes.description: Calculated remaining flight cycles until the maintenance event becomes due (projected_due_flight_cycles minus current_flight_cycles).

attributes.name: remaining_flight_hours
attributes.description: Calculated remaining flight hours until the maintenance event becomes due (projected_due_flight_hours minus current_flight_hours).

attributes.name: remarks
attributes.description: Free-text field for maintenance planners to record notes, assumptions, special conditions, or planning considerations related to this forecast.

attributes.name: version
attributes.description: Sequential version number of this forecast for the same aircraft and maintenance task. Increments each time the forecast is recalculated, enabling historical trend analysis.

products.name: visit
products.description: Planned or actual maintenance visit (induction) record at a specific MRO facility or line station. Captures visit reference, aircraft registration, visit type (line/base/engine shop), induction date, planned release date, actual release date, AMO facility, work scope summary, total man-hours, total material cost, total labour cost, and visit status. Bridges maintenance planning to MRO commercial management and cost tracking.
products.reference: AMOS Maintenance Visit / HMV (Heavy Maintenance Visit)

attributes.name: visit_id
attributes.description: Primary key for visit

attributes.name: approved_maintenance_org_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to maintenance.approved_maintenance_org. Business justification: Maintenance visit is at an approved maintenance organization facility. The visit table has amo_facility_code (STRING) but no FK. Adding approved_maintenance_org_id FK normalizes this and removes redun

attributes.name: budget_plan_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to finance.budget_plan. Business justification: Maintenance visits are tracked against budgeted maintenance spend. Links visit to budget plan for cost control, variance reporting, and annual budget performance tracking.

attributes.name: certifying_staff_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to maintenance.certifying_staff. Business justification: Maintenance visit is certified by certifying staff. The visit table has certifying_staff_licence_number (STRING) but no FK. Adding certifying_staff_id FK normalizes this and removes redundant certifyi

attributes.name: maintenance_program_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to maintenance.program. Business justification: Maintenance visit is based on a maintenance program. The visit table has maintenance_program_reference (STRING) but no FK. Adding maintenance_program_id FK normalizes this and removes redundant mainte

attributes.name: maintenance_release_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to maintenance.release. Business justification: Maintenance visit results in a Certificate of Release to Service. The visit table has crs_reference_number (STRING) but no FK. Adding maintenance_release_id FK normalizes this and removes redundant cr

attributes.name: station_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to airport.station. Business justification: Maintenance visits occur at specific stations. Links station_code to station.station_id for hangar capacity planning, visit cost tracking by location, and maintenance network performance analysis.

attributes.name: actual_release_date
attributes.description: Actual date when the aircraft was released from maintenance and returned to service. Null until visit is completed.

attributes.name: actual_release_timestamp
attributes.description: Precise timestamp when the aircraft was released from maintenance, including time zone. Used for on-time performance and turnaround time analysis.

attributes.name: ad_compliance_count
attributes.description: Number of airworthiness directives complied with during this maintenance visit. Critical for regulatory compliance tracking.

attributes.name: aircraft_registration
attributes.description: Tail number or registration mark of the aircraft undergoing maintenance. Links to fleet master data.
attributes.references: ICAO Annex 7 - Aircraft Nationality and Registration Marks

attributes.name: aircraft_total_cycles_at_induction
attributes.description: Cumulative total flight cycles (takeoff/landing pairs) of the aircraft at the time of maintenance visit induction. Used for cycle-based maintenance tracking.

attributes.name: aircraft_total_flight_hours_at_induction
attributes.business_glossary_term: Aircraft Total Flight Hours at Induction
attributes.description: Cumulative total flight hours (block hours) of the aircraft at the time of maintenance visit induction. Used for interval-based maintenance tracking.

attributes.name: check_type
attributes.description: Maintenance check designation (A, B, C, D, 1C, 2C, etc.) indicating the scope and depth of scheduled maintenance performed during this visit.

attributes.name: created_timestamp
attributes.description: Timestamp when this maintenance visit record was first created in the system. Used for audit trail and data lineage.

attributes.name: crs_issue_date
attributes.business_glossary_term: Certificate of Release to Service (CRS) Issue Date
attributes.description: Date when the Certificate of Release to Service (EASA Form 1 / FAA Form 337 equivalent) was issued, certifying the aircraft is airworthy and released from maintenance.

attributes.name: currency_code
attributes.description: Three-letter ISO 4217 currency code for all monetary amounts in this visit record. Typically USD but may vary by MRO facility location.

attributes.name: defect_count
attributes.description: Total number of defects or discrepancies identified and rectified during this maintenance visit. Used for quality and reliability analysis.

attributes.name: delay_hours
attributes.description: Total delay in hours between planned release date and actual release date. Negative values indicate early completion. Used for schedule adherence and performance analysis.

attributes.name: delay_reason_category
attributes.description: Primary category explaining any delay in the maintenance visit: on_time (no delay), parts_delay (awaiting material), technical_finding (unexpected defects), resource_constraint (labor/tooling shortage), weather (environmental), vendor_delay (external supplier), scope_change (work scope expansion). [ENUM-REF-CANDIDATE: on_time|parts_delay|technical_finding|resource_constraint|weather|vendor_delay|scope_change — 7 candidates stripped; promote to reference product]

attributes.name: estimated_release_date
attributes.description: Current estimated date for aircraft release, updated as work progresses. May differ from planned date due to findings or delays.

attributes.name: induction_date
attributes.description: Date when the aircraft was inducted into the maintenance facility and work commenced. Marks the start of the visit lifecycle.

attributes.name: induction_timestamp
attributes.description: Precise timestamp when the aircraft was inducted into the maintenance facility, including time zone. Used for detailed scheduling and SLA tracking.

attributes.name: last_modified_timestamp
attributes.description: Timestamp when this maintenance visit record was last updated. Used for audit trail and change tracking.

attributes.name: llp_replacement_count
attributes.description: Number of life-limited parts replaced during this maintenance visit. Critical for airworthiness and component life tracking.
attributes.references: FAA AC 120-17A - Maintenance Control by Reliability Methods

attributes.name: mel_deferral_count
attributes.description: Number of MEL deferrals addressed or cleared during this maintenance visit. Used for dispatch reliability analysis.

attributes.name: planned_release_date
attributes.description: Originally scheduled date for aircraft release back to service. Used for capacity planning and schedule recovery analysis.

attributes.name: reference_number
attributes.description: External business identifier for the maintenance visit, used for tracking and invoicing across MRO facilities and operators.

attributes.name: remarks
attributes.description: Free-text field for additional notes, special instructions, or observations related to this maintenance visit. Used for operational context and audit trail.

attributes.name: sb_incorporation_count
attributes.description: Number of manufacturer service bulletins incorporated during this maintenance visit. Used for fleet modification tracking.

attributes.name: total_labour_cost_usd
attributes.description: Total labor cost for all maintenance work performed during this visit, in US dollars. Calculated from man-hours and labor rates.

attributes.name: total_man_hours_actual
attributes.description: Total actual labor hours expended on all maintenance tasks in this visit. Used for cost tracking and productivity analysis.

attributes.name: total_man_hours_planned
attributes.description: Total planned labor hours for all maintenance tasks in this visit, used for resource planning and capacity management.

attributes.name: total_material_cost_usd
attributes.description: Total cost of all parts, components, consumables, and materials used during this maintenance visit, in US dollars. Excludes labor costs.

attributes.name: total_visit_cost_usd
attributes.description: Total cost of the maintenance visit including labor, material, overhead, and facility charges, in US dollars. Used for MRO commercial management and budget tracking.

attributes.name: visit_status
attributes.description: Current lifecycle status of the maintenance visit: planned (scheduled but not started), inducted (aircraft received at facility), in_progress (work underway), inspection (quality assurance), awaiting_parts (work paused for material), released (aircraft returned to service), cancelled (visit aborted). [ENUM-REF-CANDIDATE: planned|inducted|in_progress|inspection|awaiting_parts|released|cancelled — 7 candidates stripped; promote to reference product]

attributes.name: visit_type
attributes.description: Classification of maintenance visit: line (routine checks at gate/hangar), base (scheduled major checks), heavy (C/D checks), engine_shop (engine overhaul), component_shop (component repair), aog_recovery (Aircraft on Ground emergency repair).

attributes.name: work_order_count
attributes.description: Total number of individual work orders or work packages executed during this maintenance visit. Used for complexity and scope tracking.

attributes.name: work_scope_summary
attributes.description: High-level textual summary of the maintenance work scope, including major tasks, inspections, modifications, and component replacements planned or performed during this visit.

attributes.name: aircraft_registration
attributes.description: Tail number or registration mark of the aircraft to which this engineering order applies. May be null for fleet-wide orders.

attributes.name: aircraft_type_code
attributes.description: ICAO or manufacturer aircraft type designator (e.g., B737, A320, B77W) indicating the aircraft model family to which this order applies.

attributes.name: approval_date
attributes.description: Date on which the engineering order was approved by the engineering authority or CAMO.

attributes.name: ata_chapter

attributes.name: compliance_due_date

attributes.name: compliance_due_flight_hours

attributes.name: compliance_method
attributes.description: Method of compliance for this engineering order: mandatory (must be done), optional (operator discretion), on-condition (when defect found), or at next opportunity (next scheduled maintenance).

attributes.name: created_timestamp
attributes.description: Timestamp when this engineering order record was first created in the system.

attributes.name: design_approval_reference
attributes.description: Reference to the design approval document: EASA Form 1, FAA Form 337, DER (Designated Engineering Representative) approval, or STC number authorizing the modification.

attributes.name: document_url
attributes.description: URL or file path to the engineering order document, technical drawings, or supporting documentation stored in the document management system.

attributes.name: effective_date
attributes.description: Date from which this engineering order becomes effective and may be applied to aircraft.

attributes.name: effectivity
attributes.description: Effectivity statement defining which aircraft, serial numbers, or configurations this engineering order applies to (e.g., all aircraft, specific MSN range, or configuration-dependent).

attributes.name: eo_number
attributes.description: The externally-known business identifier for the engineering order, typically formatted as EO- followed by alphanumeric code.

attributes.name: eo_revision
attributes.description: Revision level of the engineering order, incremented when the order is modified or updated.

attributes.name: eo_status
attributes.description: Current lifecycle status of the engineering order in the approval and execution workflow.

attributes.name: eo_type
attributes.description: Classification of the engineering order: structural repair, modification, STC (Supplemental Type Certificate), deviation from type design, design change, or service bulletin incorporation.

attributes.name: estimated_cost_usd
attributes.description: Estimated total cost in US dollars to accomplish the engineering order, including labor, parts, and materials.

attributes.name: estimated_labor_hours
attributes.description: Estimated total labor hours required to accomplish the engineering order, used for planning and cost estimation.

attributes.name: expiry_date
attributes.description: Date on which this engineering order expires or is superseded. Null for orders with indefinite validity.

attributes.name: last_modified_timestamp
attributes.description: Timestamp when this engineering order record was last updated in the system.

attributes.name: modification_description
attributes.description: Detailed technical description of the structural repair, modification, or deviation being authorized by this engineering order.

attributes.name: part_145_organization_code
attributes.description: EASA Part-145 or FAA Part 145 approval number of the maintenance organization authorized to perform the work defined in this engineering order.

attributes.name: related_ad_number
attributes.description: Airworthiness Directive number if this engineering order is issued in response to or in compliance with an AD. Null if not AD-related.

attributes.name: related_sb_number
attributes.description: Manufacturer Service Bulletin number if this engineering order implements or references an SB. Null if not SB-related.

attributes.name: remarks

attributes.name: stc_number

attributes.name: superseded_by_eo_number

products.name: material_request

attributes.name: quantity_issued

attributes.references: AMOS Aircraft Maintenance and Engineering System

attributes.name: quantity_requested
attributes.description: The quantity of the part or material requested for the maintenance work order.
attributes.references: AMOS Aircraft Maintenance and Engineering System

attributes.name: remarks
attributes.description: Free-text field for additional notes, special handling instructions, or comments related to the material requisition.
attributes.references: AMOS Aircraft Maintenance and Engineering System

attributes.name: request_status

attributes.name: requested_date

attributes.name: required_by_date

attributes.name: requisition_number

attributes.name: return_quantity

attributes.name: return_to_store_flag

attributes.name: serial_number

attributes.name: shelf_life_expiry_date

attributes.name: store_location_code

products.name: apu_status
products.description: Auxiliary Power Unit (APU) status and utilisation record tracking the operational and maintenance state of the APU fitted to each aircraft. Captures APU part number, serial number, total APU hours, total APU cycles, time since last overhaul (TSO hours/cycles), next overhaul due, current serviceability status, last borescope inspection date, and fitted aircraft registration. APU has its own maintenance programme separate from the airframe.
products.reference: AMOS APU Utilisation / APU Maintenance Programme

attributes.name: apu_status_id
attributes.description: Unique identifier for the APU status record. Primary key.
attributes.references: AMOS Aircraft Maintenance and Engineering System

attributes.name: aircraft_id
attributes.description: Reference to the aircraft on which this APU is currently installed.
attributes.references: AMOS Aircraft Maintenance and Engineering System

attributes.name: last_defect_report_id
attributes.description: Reference to the most recent defect report raised against this APU, if any.
attributes.references: AMOS Aircraft Maintenance and Engineering System

attributes.name: last_work_order_id
attributes.description: Reference to the most recent maintenance work order performed on this APU.
attributes.references: AMOS Aircraft Maintenance and Engineering System

attributes.name: lease_contract_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to finance.lease_contract. Business justification: APU status on leased aircraft requires lease contract linkage for maintenance reserve calculations and lease return condition verification. Critical for lessor APU condition reporting.

attributes.name: airworthiness_certificate_expiry_date
attributes.description: Expiry date of the APU airworthiness certificate. APU must not be operated beyond this date without certificate renewal.

attributes.name: airworthiness_certificate_number
attributes.description: Certificate number issued by the aviation authority confirming the APU meets airworthiness standards and is approved for installation.

attributes.name: apu_model
attributes.description: APU model designation as specified by the manufacturer (e.g., GTCP131-9A, APS3200).
attributes.references: AMOS Aircraft Maintenance and Engineering System

attributes.name: apu_part_number
attributes.description: Manufacturer part number identifying the APU model and configuration. Used for parts catalog and maintenance program applicability.
attributes.references: AMOS Aircraft Maintenance and Engineering System

attributes.name: apu_serial_number
attributes.description: Unique serial number assigned by the APU manufacturer to this specific unit. Used for tracking maintenance history and airworthiness compliance.

attributes.name: borescope_inspection_interval_hours
attributes.description: Operating hours interval between borescope inspections as specified in the APU maintenance program.
attributes.references: APU Maintenance Manual, AMOS Maintenance Program

attributes.name: cycles_since_new
attributes.description: Total operating cycles accumulated by the APU since it was manufactured (never reset, even after overhaul).

attributes.name: cycles_since_overhaul
attributes.description: Operating cycles accumulated since the last major overhaul or shop visit. Reset to zero after overhaul. Used to determine next overhaul due.
attributes.references: AMOS Aircraft Maintenance and Engineering System, APU Maintenance Manual

attributes.name: hours_since_new
attributes.description: Total operating hours accumulated by the APU since it was manufactured (never reset, even after overhaul).

attributes.name: hours_since_overhaul
attributes.description: Operating hours accumulated since the last major overhaul or shop visit. Reset to zero after overhaul. Used to determine next overhaul due.
attributes.references: AMOS Aircraft Maintenance and Engineering System, APU Maintenance Manual

attributes.name: installation_date
attributes.description: Date when the APU was installed on the current aircraft. Used to calculate time-in-service and time-since-installation intervals.

attributes.name: installation_flight_cycles
attributes.business_glossary_term: Aircraft Flight Cycles at APU Installation
attributes.description: Total aircraft flight cycles at the time the APU was installed. Used as baseline for calculating APU cycles-on-wing.
attributes.references: AMOS Aircraft Maintenance and Engineering System

attributes.name: installation_flight_hours
attributes.business_glossary_term: Aircraft Flight Hours at APU Installation
attributes.description: Total aircraft flight hours at the time the APU was installed. Used as baseline for calculating APU time-on-wing.
attributes.references: AMOS Aircraft Maintenance and Engineering System

attributes.name: last_borescope_inspection_date
attributes.description: Date of the most recent borescope inspection of the APU hot section. Borescope inspections are performed to assess internal condition without disassembly.
attributes.references: APU Maintenance Manual, AMOS Maintenance Program

attributes.name: last_borescope_inspection_hours
attributes.business_glossary_term: APU Hours at Last Borescope Inspection
attributes.description: Total APU operating hours at the time of the last borescope inspection. Used to calculate next inspection due.
attributes.references: APU Maintenance Manual, AMOS Maintenance Program

attributes.name: last_overhaul_date
attributes.description: Date when the APU last underwent major overhaul or shop visit at a Part-145 approved maintenance organization.

attributes.name: last_overhaul_organization
attributes.description: Name or code of the Part-145 approved maintenance organization that performed the last APU overhaul.

attributes.name: lease_status
attributes.description: Ownership and lease status of the APU. Indicates whether the APU is owned by the operator, leased from a lessor, on loan from another operator, or part of a pooling agreement.
attributes.references: AMOS Aircraft Maintenance and Engineering System

attributes.name: maintenance_program_reference
attributes.description: Reference to the approved APU maintenance program document that defines all scheduled maintenance tasks and intervals for this APU model.

attributes.name: manufacturer_name
attributes.description: Name of the original equipment manufacturer (OEM) of the APU (e.g., Honeywell, Pratt & Whitney Canada).
attributes.references: AMOS Aircraft Maintenance and Engineering System

attributes.name: mel_category
attributes.description: MEL category of the APU deferral if applicable. Category A requires rectification before next flight, B within 3 days, C within 10 days, D within 120 days.

attributes.name: mel_deferral_reference
attributes.description: Reference to the active MEL deferral if the APU is currently operating under a deferral. Empty if APU is fully serviceable.

attributes.name: next_borescope_inspection_due_hours
attributes.business_glossary_term: Next APU Borescope Inspection Due Hours
attributes.description: Total APU operating hours at which the next borescope inspection is due.
attributes.references: AMOS Aircraft Maintenance and Engineering System

attributes.name: next_overhaul_due_cycles
attributes.description: Total APU operating cycles at which the next overhaul is due. Calculated as cycles_since_overhaul plus overhaul_interval_cycles.
attributes.references: AMOS Aircraft Maintenance and Engineering System

attributes.name: next_overhaul_due_date
attributes.description: Calendar date by which the next APU overhaul must be completed, based on the calendar interval limit.
attributes.references: AMOS Aircraft Maintenance and Engineering System

attributes.name: next_overhaul_due_hours
attributes.description: Total APU operating hours at which the next overhaul is due. Calculated as hours_since_overhaul plus overhaul_interval_hours.
attributes.references: AMOS Aircraft Maintenance and Engineering System

attributes.name: operational_status
attributes.description: Current functional state of the APU independent of airworthiness status. Indicates whether the APU can be started and operated.
attributes.references: AMOS Aircraft Maintenance and Engineering System

attributes.name: overhaul_interval_cycles
attributes.description: Manufacturer-specified or operator-approved interval in operating cycles between major overhauls. Defines when the next overhaul is due.
attributes.references: APU Maintenance Manual, AMOS Maintenance Program

attributes.name: overhaul_interval_hours
attributes.description: Manufacturer-specified or operator-approved interval in operating hours between major overhauls. Defines when the next overhaul is due.
attributes.references: APU Maintenance Manual, AMOS Maintenance Program

attributes.name: overhaul_interval_months
attributes.description: Calendar time interval in months between major overhauls, whichever limit is reached first (hours, cycles, or months).
attributes.references: APU Maintenance Manual, AMOS Maintenance Program

attributes.name: owner_organization
attributes.description: Legal owner of the APU (airline, lessor, or leasing company). May differ from the aircraft operator.
attributes.references: AMOS Aircraft Maintenance and Engineering System

attributes.name: record_created_timestamp
attributes.description: Timestamp when this APU status record was first created in the system.
attributes.references: AMOS Aircraft Maintenance and Engineering System

attributes.name: record_updated_timestamp
attributes.description: Timestamp when this APU status record was last modified in the system.
attributes.references: AMOS Aircraft Maintenance and Engineering System

attributes.name: remaining_cycles_to_overhaul
attributes.description: Operating cycles remaining until the next overhaul is due. Calculated as next_overhaul_due_cycles minus total_apu_cycles.
attributes.references: AMOS Aircraft Maintenance and Engineering System

attributes.name: remaining_hours_to_overhaul
attributes.description: Operating hours remaining until the next overhaul is due. Calculated as next_overhaul_due_hours minus total_apu_hours.
attributes.references: AMOS Aircraft Maintenance and Engineering System

attributes.name: remarks
attributes.description: Free-text field for additional notes, observations, or special conditions related to the APU status and maintenance history.
attributes.references: AMOS Aircraft Maintenance and Engineering System

attributes.name: removal_date
attributes.description: Date when the APU was removed from the aircraft. Null if the APU is currently installed.

attributes.name: removal_reason
attributes.description: Reason for APU removal from the aircraft (e.g., scheduled overhaul, unscheduled failure, aircraft retirement, component upgrade).
attributes.references: AMOS Aircraft Maintenance and Engineering System

attributes.name: serviceability_status
attributes.description: Current operational and airworthiness status of the APU. Serviceable means the APU is fully operational and meets all airworthiness requirements. Unserviceable indicates the APU has a defect that prevents operation. Deferred indicates operation under MEL deferral.

attributes.name: storage_location
attributes.description: Physical storage location or warehouse code where the APU is stored if removed from aircraft. Empty if currently installed.
attributes.references: AMOS Aircraft Maintenance and Engineering System

attributes.name: total_apu_cycles
attributes.business_glossary_term: Total Auxiliary Power Unit (APU) Operating Cycles
attributes.description: Cumulative start-stop cycles of the APU since new or since last zero-time overhaul. One cycle equals one start and shutdown sequence.
attributes.references: AMOS Aircraft Maintenance and Engineering System, APU Maintenance Manual

attributes.name: total_apu_hours
attributes.business_glossary_term: Total Auxiliary Power Unit (APU) Operating Hours
attributes.description: Cumulative operating hours of the APU since new or since last zero-time overhaul. Primary maintenance interval parameter for APU maintenance program.
attributes.references: AMOS Aircraft Maintenance and Engineering System, APU Maintenance Manual

products.name: reliability_event
products.description: Reliability programme event record capturing technical dispatch reliability data per IATA AHM (Airline Handbook of Maintenance) standards. Records technical delays (>15 min), cancellations, in-flight shutdowns (IFSD), air turnbacks (ATB), diversions, and unscheduled component removals. Captures event type, ATA chapter, aircraft type/MSN, tail number, station, flight number, event date, delay minutes, root cause category (design/maintenance/operational/no-fault-found), corrective action, and repeat/chronic flag. Feeds monthly reliability reports, alert level monitoring, and MSG-3 task effectiveness reviews.
products.reference: IATA Reliability Programme / Technical Dispatch Reliability

attributes.name: reliability_event_id
attributes.description: Unique identifier for the reliability event record. Primary key for the reliability event entity.

attributes.name: component_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to maintenance.component. Business justification: Reliability event may involve a specific component. The reliability_event table has component_part_number and component_serial_number but no FK. Adding component_id FK normalizes this and removes redu

attributes.name: employee_id
attributes.description: The user identifier of the person who last modified this reliability event record.

attributes.name: identified_hazard_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to safety.hazard. Business justification: Reliability events may identify or confirm hazards (chronic issues revealing systemic risks). Link supports proactive hazard identification from operational data, enables reliability-driven SMS hazard

attributes.name: investigation_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to safety.investigation. Business justification: Reliability events (chronic issues, trends) may trigger formal safety investigations when patterns indicate systemic risk. Link supports proactive safety management, enables reliability-driven investi

attributes.name: part_master_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to procurement.part_master. Business justification: Captures which part number experienced reliability event (delay, repeat defect) for MSG-3 analysis and manufacturer notification. Real process: reliability engineers analyze event rates by part number

attributes.name: station_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to airport.station. Business justification: Reliability events (delays, defects, cancellations) occur at specific stations. Links station_code to station.station_id for reliability analysis by location, identifying stations with chronic issues,

attributes.name: work_order_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to maintenance.work_order. Business justification: Reliability event may be resolved via a work order. The reliability_event table has work_order_number (STRING) but no FK. Adding work_order_id FK normalizes this and removes redundant work_order_numbe

attributes.name: aircraft_registration
attributes.description: The unique registration identifier (tail number) of the aircraft on which the reliability event occurred.
attributes.references: ICAO Annex 7 - Aircraft Nationality and Registration Marks

attributes.name: aircraft_total_cycles_at_event
attributes.business_glossary_term: Aircraft Total Flight Cycles at Event
attributes.description: The cumulative total flight cycles (takeoff/landing cycles) of the aircraft at the time the reliability event occurred.

attributes.name: aircraft_total_hours_at_event
attributes.business_glossary_term: Aircraft Total Flight Hours at Event
attributes.description: The cumulative total flight hours (airframe hours) of the aircraft at the time the reliability event occurred.

attributes.name: aircraft_type_code
attributes.description: IATA or ICAO aircraft type designator code (e.g., B738 for Boeing 737-800, A320 for Airbus A320).
attributes.references: IATA Aircraft Type Codes, ICAO Doc 8643

attributes.name: alert_level
attributes.description: The alert level assigned to this reliability event based on frequency and severity thresholds: green (within normal limits), amber (approaching alert threshold), red (exceeds alert threshold, requires immediate action).
attributes.references: IATA AHM Chapter 3 - Alert Level Monitoring

attributes.name: ata_chapter
attributes.description: The two-digit ATA chapter code identifying the aircraft system involved in the reliability event (e.g., 21=Air Conditioning, 32=Landing Gear, 71=Power Plant).

attributes.name: ata_section
attributes.description: The ATA section code providing more granular system identification within the ATA chapter (format: XX-YY).

attributes.name: chronic_event_flag
attributes.description: Boolean indicator (True/False) identifying whether this reliability event is part of a chronic (recurring) reliability issue requiring fleet-wide attention or MSG-3 task review.
attributes.references: IATA AHM Chapter 3 - Chronic Event Monitoring

attributes.name: closure_date
attributes.description: The date when the reliability event was formally closed after completion of all corrective actions and documentation.

attributes.name: corrective_action
attributes.description: Description of the corrective maintenance action or operational procedure change implemented to resolve the reliability event and prevent recurrence.
attributes.references: IATA AHM Chapter 3, Part-145 Maintenance Standards

attributes.name: created_timestamp
attributes.description: The timestamp when this reliability event record was first created in the system (format: yyyy-MM-ddTHH:mm:ss.SSSXXX).

attributes.name: defect_code
attributes.description: The standardized defect code or fault code identifying the specific technical issue that caused the reliability event.
attributes.references: Operator Maintenance Manual, AMOS Defect Code Library

attributes.name: defect_description
attributes.description: Free-text description of the technical defect or issue that triggered the reliability event, as reported by flight crew or maintenance personnel.

attributes.name: delay_minutes
attributes.description: The total delay duration in minutes caused by the reliability event. Null if event type is not a delay. Technical delays are typically >15 minutes per IATA standards.
attributes.references: IATA AHM Chapter 3 - Delay Reporting Standards

attributes.name: event_date
attributes.description: The calendar date on which the reliability event occurred (format: yyyy-MM-dd).

attributes.name: event_status
attributes.description: The current lifecycle status of the reliability event: open (newly reported), under_investigation (root cause analysis in progress), resolved (corrective action completed), closed (event fully documented and archived).

attributes.name: event_timestamp
attributes.description: The precise date and time when the reliability event was recorded or occurred (format: yyyy-MM-ddTHH:mm:ss.SSSXXX).

attributes.name: event_type
attributes.description: The category of reliability event: technical_delay (delay >15 minutes due to technical issue), cancellation (flight cancelled due to technical issue), ifsd (In-Flight Shutdown), atb (Air Turnback), diversion (unscheduled landing at alternate airport), unscheduled_removal (component removed outside scheduled maintenance).
attributes.references: IATA AHM Chapter 3 - Reliability Programme Standards

attributes.name: flight_number
attributes.description: The airline flight number associated with the reliability event (e.g., AA1234, BA456).

attributes.name: last_modified_timestamp
attributes.description: The timestamp when this reliability event record was last updated or modified (format: yyyy-MM-ddTHH:mm:ss.SSSXXX).

attributes.name: maintenance_organization_code
attributes.description: The code identifying the Part-145 approved maintenance organization or station that performed the corrective action.
attributes.references: EASA Part-145, FAA Part 145 - Repair Station Certification

attributes.name: manufacturer_serial_number
attributes.description: The unique serial number assigned by the aircraft manufacturer to this specific airframe.

attributes.name: msg3_task_reference
attributes.description: Reference to the MSG-3 scheduled maintenance task that may require effectiveness review based on this reliability event.

attributes.name: pirep_reference
attributes.description: Reference number or identifier of the pilot report (PIREP) that documented the in-flight reliability event.
attributes.references: FAA Order 7110.65 - Air Traffic Control, ICAO Annex 6

attributes.name: remarks
attributes.description: Additional free-text notes, observations, or contextual information related to the reliability event.

attributes.name: repeat_event_flag
attributes.description: Boolean indicator (True/False) identifying whether this reliability event is a repeat occurrence of a previously reported issue on the same aircraft or component.
attributes.references: IATA AHM Chapter 3 - Repeat Event Tracking

attributes.name: reporting_period
attributes.description: The year-month reporting period for monthly reliability reporting aggregation (format: YYYY-MM).
attributes.references: IATA AHM Chapter 3 - Monthly Reliability Reporting

attributes.name: root_cause_category
attributes.description: The high-level classification of the root cause: design (inherent design issue), maintenance (maintenance-induced), operational (crew or operational procedure issue), no_fault_found (defect could not be replicated), external (weather, FOD, bird strike, etc.).
attributes.references: IATA AHM Chapter 3 - Root Cause Analysis Standards

attributes.name: root_cause_description
attributes.description: Detailed explanation of the identified root cause of the reliability event, including contributing factors and failure mode analysis.

products.name: vendor_contract
products.description: This association product represents the commercial contract between an approved Part-145 maintenance organisation and a vendor for procurement of parts, tooling, consumables, or services. It captures contract terms, service level agreements, rate cards, capability scope, and performance metrics that exist only in the context of this specific org-vendor relationship. Each record links one approved maintenance organisation to one vendor with contractual and performance attributes.. Existence Justification: In airline maintenance operations, approved Part-145 maintenance organisations frequently engage multiple vendors for different procurement categories (parts suppliers, tooling vendors, consumables providers), and each vendor may serve multiple maintenance organisations across the airline's network or third-party MRO facilities. The business actively manages these relationships as commercial contracts with specific terms, SLAs, rate cards, capability scopes, and performance metrics that vary by org-vendor pairing.
products.reference: Internal - M:N Association

attributes.description: Unique identifier for this maintenance vendor contract record. Primary key.

attributes.name: approved_maintenance_org_id
attributes.business_glossary_term: Maintenance Vendor Contract - Approved Maintenance Org Id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to the approved Part-145 maintenance organisation that is party to this vendor contract.

attributes.name: vendor_id

attributes.name: capability_scope
attributes.description: Textual description of the specific maintenance capabilities, part categories, or service types covered under this contract (e.g., engine components, avionics repair, AOG support). Explicitly identified in detection phase relationship data.

attributes.name: contract_end_date
attributes.description: Expiry or termination date of the commercial contract. Null indicates open-ended or evergreen contract. Explicitly identified in detection phase relationship data.

attributes.name: contract_start_date
attributes.description: Effective start date of the commercial contract between the maintenance organisation and vendor. Explicitly identified in detection phase relationship data.

attributes.name: contract_status
attributes.description: Current lifecycle status of this maintenance vendor contract: active, inactive, suspended, expired, or pending renewal.

attributes.name: last_performance_review_date
attributes.description: Date of the most recent formal performance review or scorecard assessment conducted for this vendor relationship.

attributes.name: next_review_due_date
attributes.description: Scheduled date for the next formal performance review or contract renewal discussion for this vendor relationship.

attributes.name: performance_score
attributes.description: Quantitative performance rating or scorecard result for this vendor relationship, typically based on on-time delivery, quality defect rate, and responsiveness. Explicitly identified in detection phase relationship data.

attributes.name: rate_card
attributes.description: Reference identifier or document number for the pricing schedule, labor rates, or unit costs applicable to this maintenance org-vendor contract. Explicitly identified in detection phase relationship data.

attributes.name: service_level_agreement
attributes.description: Textual description or reference to the SLA terms governing response time, turnaround time, quality standards, and availability commitments for this vendor relationship. Explicitly identified in detection phase relationship data.

domains.name: cargo
domains.description: Air freight and cargo commercial and operational data including AWB (Air Waybill) lifecycle, ULD (Unit Load Device) management, cargo bookings, shipment tracking, cargo capacity allocation, weight and balance, dangerous goods (DG) declarations, freight rates, cargo revenue accounting, and shipper/consignee relationships. Manages both belly cargo and dedicated freighter operations. Aligns with Mercator Cargo Management System.
domains.references: IATA Cargo Services Conference Resolutions, ICAO Annex 18

products.name: awb
products.description: Air Waybill (AWB) master record — the primary contractual and operational document governing a cargo shipment. Captures AWB number (IATA 8-digit format), origin and destination airports, shipper and consignee details, commodity description, declared value, number of pieces, gross weight, chargeable weight, volume, nature of goods, special handling codes, freight charges, prepaid/collect indicator, routing instructions, and AWB status lifecycle (booked, accepted, manifested, departed, arrived, delivered). SSOT for all AWB-level cargo data. Aligns with Mercator Cargo Management System AWB module.
products.reference: IATA Air Waybill (AWB) — IATA Resolution 600a

attributes.name: regulatory_filing_id

attributes.name: regulatory_requirement_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to compliance.regulatory_requirement. Business justification: AWBs must comply with IATA, customs, and dangerous goods regulations. Airlines verify regulatory compliance during acceptance and booking processes. Essential for legal shipment acceptance and audit t

attributes.description: Foreign key linking to route.route. Business justification: AWBs are booked and transported on specific routes. Cargo yield management, route profitability analysis, and capacity planning require linking shipments to routes. Essential for cargo revenue managem

attributes.name: awb_status
attributes.description: Current lifecycle status of the AWB indicating its position in the cargo handling workflow from initial booking through final delivery. [ENUM-REF-CANDIDATE: booked|accepted|manifested|departed|in_transit|arrived|delivered|cancelled — 8 candidates stripped; promote to reference product]

attributes.name: awb_type

attributes.name: booking_timestamp

attributes.name: commodity_code

products.name: cargo_booking

products.name: shipment
products.description: Physical shipment record tracking the end-to-end movement of cargo from acceptance to delivery, including granular milestone events. Captures shipment status (received, built-up, loaded, in-transit, arrived, delivered, on-hold), actual pieces and weight at acceptance, volume, commodity code (IATA/HS), special handling codes (SHC), temperature range for perishables, routing segments, current location, estimated and actual arrival times, proof of delivery, exception flags, and milestone event history (event code per IATA Cargo-XML: RCS, DEP, ARR, NFD, DLV, DIS with timestamps, station, flight, and responsible party). Links AWB to physical ULD build-up and flight manifest. SSOT for shipment lifecycle tracking and real-time shipment visibility.

attributes.name: actual_arrival_timestamp

attributes.name: commodity_description
attributes.description: Free-text description of the goods being shipped. Provides human-readable detail for handling, customs, and security screening.

attributes.name: consignee_name
attributes.description: Name of the party receiving the goods. Business-confidential commercial relationship data.

products.name: uld

Captures ULD serial number (IATA format: type code + serial + owner code), ULD type (LD3, LD7, LD11, PMC, PAG, etc.), tare weight, maximum gross weight, maximum volume, material, owner airline code, serviceable status, current location (airport/station), last inspection date, next inspection due date, damage status, and lease/ownership indicator. attributes.name: route_id

attributes.name: customs_declaration_reference

attributes.name: customs_submission_timestamp

attributes.name: dangerous_goods_indicator

attributes.name: destination_airport_code

attributes.name: finalized_timestamp

attributes.name: flight_date

attributes.name: flight_number

attributes.name: last_modified_timestamp

attributes.name: live_animals_indicator

attributes.name: mail_indicator

attributes.name: manifest_number
attributes.description: Externally-known unique manifest document number assigned by the cargo system for regulatory and operational tracking.

attributes.name: manifest_status
attributes.description: Current lifecycle status of the cargo manifest. Preliminary indicates draft; final indicates locked for departure; amended indicates post-departure correction; submitted indicates transmitted to customs.

attributes.name: operation_type
attributes.description: Indicates whether cargo is carried on a dedicated freighter aircraft, in the belly hold of a passenger aircraft, or on a combi (mixed passenger/cargo) configuration.

attributes.name: origin_airport_code

attributes.name: perishables_indicator
attributes.description: Flag indicating whether this manifest includes perishable cargo (e.g., fresh produce, pharmaceuticals) requiring temperature-controlled handling.

attributes.name: remarks
attributes.description: Free-text field for operational notes, special handling instructions, or discrepancy explanations related to this manifest.

attributes.name: security_screening_status
attributes.description: Indicates the security screening completion status for all cargo on this manifest, required for regulatory compliance.
attributes.references: TSA Cargo Security Requirements, EU Regulation 300/2008

attributes.name: shipper_count
attributes.description: Total number of distinct shippers (consignors) represented across all AWBs on this manifest.

attributes.name: total_chargeable_weight_kg
attributes.description: Total chargeable weight in kilograms used for revenue calculation, which is the greater of actual weight or volumetric weight across all AWBs.

attributes.name: total_declared_value_usd
attributes.description: Total declared value for customs and insurance purposes across all AWBs on this manifest, expressed in US dollars.

attributes.name: total_pieces
attributes.description: Total count of individual cargo pieces (packages, cartons, pallets) loaded on this flight across all AWBs.

attributes.name: total_volume_cbm
attributes.description: Total volume of all cargo loaded on this flight in cubic meters, used for capacity planning and dimensional analysis.

attributes.name: total_weight_kg
attributes.description: Total actual gross weight of all cargo loaded on this flight in kilograms, used for weight and balance calculations.

attributes.name: transit_cargo_indicator
attributes.description: Flag indicating whether this manifest includes transit cargo that will continue on a connecting flight rather than being delivered at the destination airport.

attributes.name: uld_count
attributes.description: Total number of Unit Load Devices (containers and pallets) loaded on this flight.

attributes.name: valuable_cargo_indicator
attributes.description: Flag indicating whether this manifest includes high-value cargo requiring enhanced security and handling procedures.

Mandatory for all DG shipments. Aligns with Mercator DG module.

Critical for safety compliance, acceptance verification, and regulatory audit defense.

attributes.name: acceptance_certificate_number
attributes.description: Reference number of the dangerous goods acceptance certificate or checklist issued upon successful acceptance inspection.

attributes.name: acceptance_check_status
attributes.description: Result of the airline's dangerous goods acceptance inspection: passed (accepted for carriage), failed (rejected), pending (under review), waived (exempted).

attributes.name: acceptance_check_timestamp
attributes.description: Date and time when the dangerous goods acceptance check was completed by airline cargo acceptance staff.

attributes.name: additional_handling_information
attributes.description: Free-text field for supplementary handling instructions, warnings, or remarks specific to this dangerous goods shipment.

attributes.name: all_packed_in_one_flag
attributes.description: Indicates whether all dangerous goods packages covered by this declaration are contained within a single overpack or freight container.

attributes.name: cargo_aircraft_only_flag
attributes.description: Indicates whether the dangerous goods are restricted to cargo aircraft only (true) or may be carried on passenger aircraft (false).

attributes.name: compliance_verified_flag
attributes.description: Indicates whether the dangerous goods declaration has been verified for full regulatory compliance with IATA DGR, ICAO Technical Instructions, and applicable national regulations.

attributes.name: created_timestamp
attributes.description: Date and time when this dangerous goods declaration record was first created in the cargo management system.

attributes.name: dg_class
attributes.description: Primary hazard class of the dangerous goods (1-9): 1=Explosives, 2=Gases, 3=Flammable Liquids, 4=Flammable Solids, 5=Oxidizing Substances, 6=Toxic and Infectious Substances, 7=Radioactive Material, 8=Corrosives, 9=Miscellaneous.

attributes.name: dg_division
attributes.description: Subdivision within the DG class providing further hazard classification (e.g., 2.1 for flammable gases, 6.2 for infectious substances). May be null for classes without divisions.

attributes.name: emergency_contact_name
attributes.description: Name of the person or organization to contact in case of emergency involving the dangerous goods shipment.

attributes.name: emergency_contact_phone
attributes.description: 24-hour emergency telephone number for the contact person or organization, including country and area codes.

attributes.name: gross_weight_per_package_kg
attributes.description: Gross weight of each package including dangerous goods and packaging material, measured in kilograms.

attributes.name: last_modified_timestamp
attributes.description: Date and time when this dangerous goods declaration record was last updated in the cargo management system.

attributes.name: net_quantity_per_package
attributes.description: Net quantity of dangerous goods per package, excluding packaging material. Unit specified in net_quantity_unit.

attributes.name: net_quantity_unit
attributes.description: Unit of measure for net quantity: kg (kilograms), L (liters), g (grams), mL (milliliters).

attributes.name: number_of_packages
attributes.description: Total count of packages containing dangerous goods within this declaration.

attributes.name: overpack_used_flag
attributes.description: Indicates whether an overpack (single enclosure containing one or more packages) was used for this dangerous goods shipment.

attributes.name: packing_group
attributes.description: Degree of danger presented by the substance: I=Great Danger, II=Medium Danger, III=Minor Danger. Not applicable to all DG classes.

attributes.name: packing_instruction
attributes.description: IATA packing instruction code specifying how the dangerous goods must be packaged for air transport (e.g., PI 965 for lithium ion batteries).

attributes.name: proper_shipping_name
attributes.description: The official IATA-recognized name used to describe the dangerous goods substance or article as specified in the DGR List of Dangerous Goods.

attributes.name: radioactive_category
attributes.description: Category label for radioactive materials (Class 7) based on transport index and surface radiation level. Applicable only to radioactive shipments.

attributes.name: shipper_declaration_text
attributes.description: Full text of the shipper's declaration certifying that the dangerous goods are properly classified, packaged, marked, labeled, and in proper condition for transport by air.

attributes.name: shipper_name
attributes.description: Name of the shipper who prepared and signed the dangerous goods declaration.

attributes.name: shipper_signature_date
attributes.description: Date on which the shipper signed the dangerous goods declaration, certifying compliance with IATA DGR.

attributes.name: special_provision_codes
attributes.description: Comma-separated list of IATA special provision codes (e.g., A1, A2) that apply additional conditions or exemptions to the shipment.

attributes.name: state_variation_codes
attributes.description: Comma-separated list of country-specific variation codes indicating deviations from IATA DGR by national civil aviation authorities.

attributes.name: subsidiary_risk_class
attributes.description: Secondary hazard class if the dangerous goods present more than one hazard. May be null if no subsidiary risk exists.

attributes.name: total_gross_weight_kg
attributes.description: Total gross weight of all packages containing dangerous goods in this declaration, measured in kilograms.

attributes.name: total_net_quantity
attributes.description: Total net quantity of dangerous goods across all packages in this declaration. Calculated as net_quantity_per_package multiplied by number_of_packages.

attributes.name: transport_index
attributes.description: Single number assigned to a package, overpack, or freight container containing radioactive material to provide control over radiation exposure. Applicable only to Class 7 DG.

attributes.name: un_number
attributes.description: Four-digit UN identification number assigned to the dangerous substance or article. Mandatory for all DG shipments per IATA DGR.
attributes.references: UN Recommendations on the Transport of Dangerous Goods - Model Regulations

products.name: freight_rate
products.description: Cargo freight rate and pricing master record defining all pricing structures for cargo transportation including base rates, surcharges, and interline proration. Captures rate type (general cargo rate GCR, specific commodity rate SCR, class rate, ULD rate, IATA tariff rate, surcharge, interline prorate), origin and destination airport pair, commodity code, weight break thresholds, rate per kg, minimum charge, currency, validity period, rate class, routing restrictions, rate source (TACT, bilateral agreement, spot rate, interline), surcharge details (fuel FSC, security SSC, handling, DG, oversize, remote area, CAF with calculation basis), interline partner code, proration method, and settlement references. SSOT for all cargo pricing and revenue sharing. Aligns with Mercator rating and interline modules.

attributes.name: route_id

attributes.name: commodity_code
attributes.description: IATA commodity classification code identifying the type of cargo this rate applies to (e.g., PER for perishables, VAL for valuables, AVI for live animals).

attributes.name: created_timestamp
attributes.description: Timestamp when this freight rate record was first created in the system. Audit trail for data lineage.

attributes.name: currency_code
attributes.description: Three-letter ISO 4217 currency code for all monetary amounts in this rate record.

attributes.name: dangerous_goods_applicable
attributes.description: Indicates whether this rate applies to dangerous goods shipments requiring special handling and documentation per IATA DGR.

attributes.name: destination_airport_code
attributes.description: Three-letter IATA airport code representing the shipment destination point for this rate.

attributes.name: effective_from_date
attributes.description: Date when this freight rate becomes valid and can be applied to bookings. Part of the rate validity period.

attributes.name: effective_to_date
attributes.description: Date when this freight rate expires and can no longer be applied to new bookings. Null indicates open-ended validity.

attributes.name: interline_partner_code
attributes.description: IATA two or three-letter airline code of the interline partner carrier for revenue proration. Applicable when rate_type is INTERLINE_PRORATE.

attributes.name: last_modified_timestamp
attributes.description: Timestamp when this freight rate record was last updated. Audit trail for change tracking.

attributes.name: minimum_charge
attributes.description: Minimum freight charge that applies regardless of weight. Ensures revenue floor for small shipments.

attributes.name: notes
attributes.description: Free-text notes providing additional context, restrictions, or special conditions applicable to this freight rate.

attributes.name: proration_method

attributes.name: proration_percentage
attributes.description: Percentage of total freight revenue allocated to this carrier segment in interline operations. Used when proration_method is AGREED_PERCENTAGE.

attributes.name: rate_approval_authority
attributes.description: Name or identifier of the authority or department that approved this freight rate (e.g., Revenue Management, Pricing Committee, IATA CSC).

attributes.name: rate_class

attributes.name: rate_code

attributes.name: rate_per_kg

attributes.name: rate_source
attributes.description: Origin of the freight rate. TACT (The Air Cargo Tariff published rate), BILATERAL_AGREEMENT (negotiated carrier-to-carrier), SPOT_RATE (one-time negotiated rate), INTERLINE (multi-carrier agreement), CONTRACT (shipper contract rate), MARKET_RATE (dynamic market-based pricing).
attributes.references: IATA TACT (The Air Cargo Tariff) Rules

attributes.name: rate_status
attributes.description: Current lifecycle status of the freight rate. ACTIVE (in use), INACTIVE (not available), PENDING (awaiting approval), EXPIRED (past effective_to_date), SUSPENDED (temporarily disabled).
attributes.references: Mercator Cargo Management System Data Model

attributes.name: rate_type
attributes.description: Classification of the freight rate. GCR (General Cargo Rate) applies to standard shipments, SCR (Specific Commodity Rate) applies to designated commodities, CLASS_RATE applies to rate classes, ULD_RATE applies to unit load devices, IATA_TARIFF applies to published IATA rates, SURCHARGE applies to additional charges, INTERLINE_PRORATE applies to revenue sharing between carriers. attributes.name: routing_restriction
attributes.description: Routing constraints or requirements for this rate to apply. May specify required connection points, prohibited routings, or carrier restrictions.

attributes.name: settlement_reference
attributes.description: Reference identifier for IATA Cargo Accounts Settlement Systems (CASS) or bilateral settlement agreement. Used for interline revenue reconciliation.

attributes.name: surcharge_calculation_basis
attributes.description: Method for calculating surcharge amount. PERCENTAGE (percent of base freight), FLAT_AMOUNT (fixed charge), PER_KG (per kilogram), PER_SHIPMENT (per AWB).

attributes.name: surcharge_type
attributes.description: Type of surcharge if rate_type is SURCHARGE. FSC (Fuel Surcharge), SSC (Security Surcharge), HANDLING (special handling), DG (Dangerous Goods), OVERSIZE (oversized cargo), REMOTE_AREA (remote destination), CAF (Currency Adjustment Factor), NONE (not a surcharge). [ENUM-REF-CANDIDATE: FSC|SSC|HANDLING|DG|OVERSIZE|REMOTE_AREA|CAF|NONE — 8 candidates stripped; promote to reference product]

attributes.name: surcharge_value
attributes.description: Numeric value for surcharge calculation. Interpretation depends on surcharge_calculation_basis (e.g., 15.5 for 15.5% or 15.5 currency units).

attributes.name: weight_break_upper_kg
attributes.description: Upper weight threshold in kilograms for this rate tier. Null indicates no upper limit (open-ended tier).
