attributes.name: deicing_crew_id
attributes.description: Identifier for the ground crew or team that performed the de-icing treatment. Used for quality tracking and training purposes.

attributes.name: flight_leg_id
attributes.description: Reference to the flight receiving de-icing treatment. Links to the scheduled or operational flight record.

attributes.name: gate_assignment_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to airport.gate_assignment. Business justification: deicing_event occurs at a specific location, often at the gate or a deicing pad. Currently stores deicing_location_identifier (STRING). FK to gate_assignment provides precise location, time window, an

attributes.name: occurrence_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to safety.occurrence. Business justification: Deicing operations have inherent safety risks (fluid exposure, equipment incidents, slip hazards). Direct occurrence link consolidates safety reporting alongside existing occurrence_report_id FK for c

attributes.name: station_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to airport.station. Business justification: De-icing events occur at specific airport stations. The deicing_event table currently has airport_code as a STRING denormalized attribute, but no FK to station. Adding station_id normalizes this relat

attributes.name: supervisor_employee_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to workforce.employee. Business justification: Deicing operations require certified workforce supervision for safety compliance, fluid application oversight, and holdover time validation. Regulatory requirement for accountable supervisor beyond cr

attributes.name: created_timestamp
attributes.description: The date and time when this de-icing event record was first created in the system. Audit trail for data lineage.

attributes.name: currency_code
attributes.description: Three-letter ISO 4217 currency code for all monetary amounts in this record (e.g., USD, EUR, CAD).

attributes.name: deicing_location_type
attributes.description: The type of location where de-icing was performed: dedicated de-icing pad, gate position, remote stand, or runway holding area.

attributes.name: deicing_vendor_code
attributes.description: Code identifying the third-party vendor or ground handling company that performed the de-icing service. Used for billing and performance tracking.

attributes.name: environmental_reporting_flag
attributes.description: Indicates whether this de-icing event must be included in environmental compliance reporting (CORSIA, ISO 14001). True if glycol usage exceeds reporting thresholds.
attributes.references: CORSIA Carbon Offsetting and Reduction Scheme, ISO 14001

attributes.name: equipment_identifier
attributes.description: Identifier for the specific de-icing truck or equipment unit used. Enables equipment maintenance correlation and utilization tracking.

attributes.name: flight_number
attributes.description: The airline flight number for the flight being de-iced (e.g., AA1234). Includes carrier code and flight number.

attributes.name: fluid_concentration_primary_percent
attributes.description: Concentration percentage of the primary de-icing fluid mixture (glycol to water ratio). Affects freezing point and holdover time.
attributes.references: SAE AMS1424 and AMS1428 De-icing Fluid Standards

attributes.name: fluid_concentration_secondary_percent
attributes.description: Concentration percentage of the secondary anti-icing fluid mixture. Null if no secondary treatment was performed.
attributes.references: SAE AMS1424 and AMS1428 De-icing Fluid Standards

attributes.name: fluid_cost_total_amount
attributes.description: Total cost of de-icing and anti-icing fluids used in this treatment event. Used for financial tracking and cost recovery.

attributes.name: fluid_type_primary
attributes.description: The primary de-icing fluid type applied in the first treatment step. Type I is typically used for de-icing (removing contamination).
attributes.references: SAE AMS1424 and AMS1428 De-icing Fluid Standards

attributes.name: fluid_type_secondary
attributes.description: The secondary anti-icing fluid type applied in the second treatment step, if applicable. Types II, III, or IV provide longer holdover time protection.
attributes.references: SAE AMS1424 and AMS1428 De-icing Fluid Standards

attributes.name: fluid_volume_primary_liters
attributes.description: Volume of primary de-icing fluid applied, measured in liters. Used for cost tracking and environmental reporting.

attributes.name: fluid_volume_secondary_liters
attributes.description: Volume of secondary anti-icing fluid applied, measured in liters. Null if no secondary treatment was performed.

attributes.name: holdover_time_minutes
attributes.description: The estimated time in minutes that the anti-icing treatment will remain effective under current weather conditions. Critical for flight safety and departure timing.
attributes.references: FAA AC 120-60B Ground De-icing and Anti-icing Program

attributes.name: inspection_performed_by
attributes.description: Identifier of the person or crew who performed the post-treatment inspection. May be pilot, ground crew, or designated inspector.
attributes.references: FAA AC 120-60B Ground De-icing and Anti-icing Program

attributes.name: last_modified_timestamp
attributes.description: The date and time when this de-icing event record was last updated. Audit trail for data lineage and change tracking.

attributes.name: outside_air_temperature_celsius
attributes.description: The outside air temperature in degrees Celsius at the time of treatment. Critical factor in determining holdover time and fluid effectiveness.

attributes.name: post_treatment_inspection_result
attributes.description: Result of the post-treatment inspection to verify aircraft surfaces are free of contamination. Critical safety check before departure.
attributes.references: FAA AC 120-60B Ground De-icing and Anti-icing Program

attributes.name: precipitation_intensity
attributes.description: The intensity of precipitation during treatment. Combined with precipitation type to determine holdover time from FAA/Transport Canada tables.
attributes.references: FAA AC 120-60B Ground De-icing and Anti-icing Program

attributes.name: precipitation_type
attributes.description: The type of precipitation or frozen contamination present during treatment. Affects holdover time calculation and treatment requirements. [ENUM-REF-CANDIDATE: none|light_snow|moderate_snow|heavy_snow|freezing_rain|freezing_drizzle|ice_pellets|frost|mixed — 9 candidates stripped; promote to reference product]
attributes.references: FAA AC 120-60B Ground De-icing and Anti-icing Program

attributes.name: remarks
attributes.description: Free-text field for additional notes, special circumstances, or operational comments related to the de-icing event.

attributes.name: service_charge_amount
attributes.description: Labor and equipment service charge for the de-icing treatment, separate from fluid costs. Used for vendor billing and cost allocation.

attributes.name: treatment_duration_minutes
attributes.description: Total duration of the de-icing treatment in minutes, calculated from start to end timestamp. Used for operational efficiency analysis.

attributes.name: treatment_end_timestamp
attributes.description: The date and time when de-icing treatment was completed. Marks the start of the holdover time window.

attributes.name: treatment_reason_code
attributes.description: The primary reason or trigger for performing the de-icing treatment. Used for operational analysis and cost allocation. [ENUM-REF-CANDIDATE: scheduled|frost|snow|ice|freezing_rain|preventive|regulatory_requirement — 7 candidates stripped; promote to reference product]

attributes.name: treatment_start_timestamp
attributes.description: The date and time when de-icing treatment began. Used to calculate holdover time expiration and turnaround impact.

attributes.name: treatment_status
attributes.description: Current status of the de-icing treatment event in its lifecycle. Tracks operational workflow state.

attributes.name: treatment_type
attributes.description: The type of de-icing and anti-icing fluid treatment applied. Type I is heated de-icing fluid; Types II, III, IV are thickened anti-icing fluids with varying viscosities and holdover times. [ENUM-REF-CANDIDATE: type_i_only|type_i_and_ii|type_i_and_iii|type_i_and_iv|type_ii_only|type_iii_only|type_iv_only — 7 candidates stripped; promote to reference product]
attributes.references: SAE AMS1424 and AMS1428 De-icing Fluid Standards

attributes.name: visibility_meters
attributes.description: Visibility in meters at the time of treatment. Indicates severity of weather conditions.

attributes.name: wind_speed_knots
attributes.description: Wind speed in knots at the time of treatment. High winds can reduce holdover time effectiveness.

products.name: pfc_record
products.description: Transactional record for a Passenger Facility Charge (PFC) collected on behalf of a US airport authority. Captures PNR reference, passenger reference, ticket number, collecting carrier, airport authority, PFC amount per segment, currency, collection date, remittance batch reference, and remittance status (collected/remitted/adjusted/refunded). Supports DOT PFC remittance compliance and ARC/BSP settlement reconciliation.
products.reference: FAA PFC Program — 14 CFR Part 158 — Passenger Facility Charge Record

attributes.name: pfc_record_id
attributes.description: Unique identifier for the PFC record. Primary key.

attributes.name: accounts_receivable_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to finance.accounts_receivable. Business justification: Passenger Facility Charges collected by airlines create receivables from airport authorities or payables to authorities depending on collection method. Required for regulatory remittance tracking, DOT

attributes.name: flight_leg_id
attributes.description: Reference to the specific flight leg on which this PFC was collected. Links to the flight operations entity.

attributes.name: original_pfc_record_id
attributes.description: Reference to the original PFC record if this is an adjustment or correction. Links to the superseded record for audit trail.

attributes.name: pax_profile_id
attributes.description: Reference to the passenger for whom this PFC was collected. Links to the passenger master entity.

attributes.name: adjustment_reason_code
attributes.description: Code indicating the reason for any adjustment to the PFC amount. Examples include ticket refunds, exchanges, schedule changes, or data corrections.

attributes.name: adjustment_reason_description
attributes.description: Detailed explanation of the adjustment made to this PFC record. Provides audit trail for compliance and reconciliation.

attributes.name: airport_authority_name
attributes.description: Legal name of the airport authority or municipality that imposed the PFC. Required for DOT remittance reporting.

attributes.name: airport_code
attributes.description: Three-letter IATA airport code identifying the US airport authority that imposed this PFC. The airport where the charge applies.

attributes.name: arc_report_period
attributes.description: ARC reporting period (YYYY-MM format) in which this PFC collection was reported. Used for reconciliation with ARC settlement data.

attributes.name: bsp_period
attributes.description: BSP billing period (YYYY-MM format) in which this PFC collection was processed. Used for international settlement reconciliation.

attributes.name: collecting_carrier_code
attributes.description: Two-character IATA airline code of the carrier that collected the PFC on behalf of the airport authority. May differ from the operating carrier in codeshare scenarios.

attributes.name: collection_date
attributes.description: Date on which the PFC was collected from the passenger. Typically the ticket issuance date or payment date.

attributes.name: collection_status
attributes.description: Current lifecycle status of the PFC transaction. Tracks the charge from collection through remittance to the airport authority or refund to the passenger.

attributes.name: coupon_sequence_number
attributes.description: Sequential number of the flight coupon within the ticket on which this PFC applies. Identifies the specific segment within a multi-segment ticket.

attributes.name: created_timestamp
attributes.description: Timestamp when this PFC record was first created in the system. Audit trail for data lineage and compliance.

attributes.name: currency_code
attributes.description: Three-letter ISO 4217 currency code for the PFC amount. Typically USD for US domestic PFC collections.

attributes.name: dot_reporting_flag
attributes.description: Indicates whether this PFC record must be included in the quarterly DOT PFC reporting submission. True for all collected and remitted charges.

attributes.name: exemption_code
attributes.description: Code indicating the reason for PFC exemption if the charge was not collected. Examples include connecting passenger exemptions, through-ticketing exemptions, or regulatory waivers.

attributes.name: exemption_reason
attributes.description: Detailed explanation of why the PFC was exempted or not collected. Supports audit and compliance review.

attributes.name: last_modified_timestamp
attributes.description: Timestamp when this PFC record was last updated. Tracks changes for audit and reconciliation purposes.

attributes.name: operating_carrier_code
attributes.description: Two-character IATA airline code of the carrier that operated the flight segment. Identifies the actual airline providing the service.

attributes.name: pfc_amount
attributes.description: Monetary amount of the PFC collected for this segment. Typically $4.50 per eligible segment under current DOT regulations, but may vary by airport approval.

attributes.name: pnr_locator
attributes.description: Six-character alphanumeric code uniquely identifying the passenger reservation in the GDS or PSS. Links this PFC collection to the originating booking.

attributes.name: point_of_sale_country
attributes.description: Three-letter ISO 3166-1 alpha-3 country code where the ticket was sold. Used for revenue accounting and regulatory reporting.

attributes.name: refund_amount
attributes.description: Monetary amount of the PFC refunded to the passenger. May differ from the original collection amount due to partial refunds or currency adjustments.

attributes.name: refund_date
attributes.description: Date on which the PFC was refunded to the passenger due to ticket cancellation, schedule change, or other qualifying event.

attributes.name: remittance_batch_number
attributes.description: Identifier of the remittance batch in which this PFC was submitted to the airport authority. Links to the batch payment and DOT reporting cycle.

attributes.name: remittance_date
attributes.description: Date on which the PFC was remitted to the airport authority. Must occur within the DOT-mandated remittance period (typically monthly).

attributes.name: sales_channel
attributes.description: Channel through which the ticket and PFC were sold. GDS (Global Distribution System), airline direct website, OTA (Online Travel Agency), traditional travel agent, corporate booking tool, or call center.

attributes.name: settlement_method
attributes.description: Method by which the PFC was settled. ARC (Airlines Reporting Corporation) for US domestic, BSP (Billing and Settlement Plan) for international, direct for airline-direct sales, or interline for interline ticketing agreements.
attributes.references: IATA BSP Manual, ARC Settlement Procedures

attributes.name: ticket_number
attributes.description: Thirteen-digit IATA standard ticket number (3-digit airline code + 10-digit serial number) on which the PFC was collected. Uniquely identifies the e-ticket document.

attributes.name: travel_date
attributes.description: Scheduled date of travel for the flight segment on which this PFC applies. Used for eligibility validation and reporting.

products.name: ground_handler
products.description: Master record for ground handling service providers contracted to deliver ramp, passenger, and cargo handling services at specific stations, including performance measurement history. Captures handler name, IATA ground handler code, handling categories (ramp/passenger/cargo/fuel/catering), contracted stations, SGHA agreement reference, license and permit details, insurance expiry, performance tier, operational contact details, and periodic performance KPIs (on-time departure contribution, baggage delivery time, damage rate, SLA breach flags, penalty triggers, performance scores). SSOT for ground handler identity and SLA governance within the airport domain.
products.reference: IATA Standard Ground Handling Agreement (SGHA) — Handler Master

attributes.name: ground_handler_id
attributes.description: Unique identifier for the ground handling service provider record. Primary key.

attributes.name: vendor_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to procurement.vendor. Business justification: Ground handlers are vendors providing contracted services (ramp, passenger, baggage handling). Linking ground_handler to vendor master unifies vendor management, enables procurement spend analysis, co

attributes.name: agreement_effective_date
attributes.description: The date when the ground handling agreement becomes effective and services may commence.

attributes.name: agreement_expiry_date
attributes.description: The date when the ground handling agreement expires or is scheduled for renewal.

attributes.name: aircraft_damage_incident_count
attributes.description: The total number of aircraft damage incidents caused by this handler during the current performance measurement period.
attributes.references: IATA Safety Audit for Ground Operations (ISAGO)

attributes.name: average_baggage_delivery_time_minutes
attributes.business_glossary_term: Average Baggage Delivery Time in Minutes
attributes.description: The average time in minutes from aircraft arrival to first baggage on carousel for flights handled by this provider.

attributes.name: baggage_handling_flag
attributes.description: Indicates whether the handler provides baggage sorting, loading, unloading, and tracing services.

attributes.name: baggage_mishandling_rate_per_1000
attributes.description: The number of mishandled baggage incidents per 1000 passengers handled, including delayed, damaged, and lost baggage.
attributes.references: IATA Baggage Resolution System (BRS), SITA Baggage IT Insights

attributes.name: cargo_handling_flag
attributes.description: Indicates whether the handler provides cargo and freight handling services including loading, unloading, and warehouse operations.

attributes.name: catering_handling_flag
attributes.description: Indicates whether the handler provides aircraft catering loading and unloading services.

attributes.name: contracted_stations
attributes.description: Comma-separated list of IATA airport codes where this handler is contracted to provide services.

attributes.name: emergency_contact_phone
attributes.description: The 24/7 emergency contact telephone number for urgent operational issues and Aircraft on Ground (AOG) situations.

attributes.name: fuel_handling_flag
attributes.description: Indicates whether the handler provides aircraft refueling and defueling services.

attributes.name: handler_name
attributes.description: The legal registered name of the ground handling service provider organization.

attributes.name: handler_type
attributes.description: Classification of the ground handler by ownership and operational model.

attributes.name: iata_ground_handler_code
attributes.business_glossary_term: International Air Transport Association (IATA) Ground Handler Code
attributes.description: The IATA-assigned unique code identifying this ground handling service provider globally.

attributes.name: insurance_coverage_amount
attributes.description: The total liability coverage amount provided by the handler's insurance policy.

attributes.name: insurance_currency_code
attributes.description: The three-letter ISO 4217 currency code for the insurance coverage amount.

attributes.name: insurance_expiry_date
attributes.description: The date when the handler's liability insurance policy expires and must be renewed.

attributes.name: insurance_policy_number
attributes.description: The policy number of the handler's liability insurance coverage as required by the ground handling agreement.

attributes.name: isago_certification_expiry_date
attributes.business_glossary_term: IATA Safety Audit for Ground Operations (ISAGO) Certification Expiry Date
attributes.description: The date when the handler's ISAGO certification expires and must be renewed.
attributes.references: IATA Safety Audit for Ground Operations (ISAGO)

attributes.name: isago_certified_flag
attributes.business_glossary_term: IATA Safety Audit for Ground Operations (ISAGO) Certified Flag
attributes.description: Indicates whether the handler holds current IATA Safety Audit for Ground Operations (ISAGO) certification.
attributes.references: IATA Safety Audit for Ground Operations (ISAGO)

attributes.name: last_performance_review_date
attributes.description: The date of the most recent formal performance review conducted with this ground handler.

attributes.name: license_expiry_date
attributes.description: The date when the ground handler's operating license expires and must be renewed.
attributes.references: ICAO Annex 6, National Civil Aviation Authority Regulations

attributes.name: license_issuing_authority
attributes.description: The name of the civil aviation authority or regulatory body that issued the ground handling license.
attributes.references: ICAO Annex 6, National Civil Aviation Authority Regulations

attributes.name: license_number
attributes.description: The regulatory license or permit number issued by the civil aviation authority authorizing ground handling operations.
attributes.references: ICAO Annex 6, National Civil Aviation Authority Regulations

attributes.name: on_time_departure_contribution_pct
attributes.description: The percentage of flights handled by this provider that departed on time, measuring contribution to overall On-Time Performance (OTP).
attributes.references: IATA Airport Handling Manual (AHM), DOT On-Time Performance Reporting

attributes.name: operational_status
attributes.description: Current operational status of the ground handler within the airline's network.

attributes.name: passenger_handling_flag
attributes.description: Indicates whether the handler provides passenger services including check-in, boarding, and gate operations.

attributes.name: penalty_triggered_flag
attributes.description: Indicates whether contractual penalties have been triggered due to performance failures during the current period.

attributes.name: performance_score
attributes.description: The composite performance score (0-100) calculated from weighted Key Performance Indicators (KPIs) including on-time performance, baggage handling, safety, and SLA compliance.

attributes.name: performance_tier
attributes.description: The current performance tier classification of the handler based on historical Service Level Agreement (SLA) compliance and quality metrics.

attributes.name: primary_contact_email
attributes.description: The email address of the primary operational contact at the ground handler.
attributes.references: GDPR Article 4, IATA Ground Handling Agreement (IGHA) Standards

attributes.name: primary_contact_name
attributes.description: The full name of the primary operational contact person at the ground handler for day-to-day coordination.

attributes.name: primary_contact_phone
attributes.description: The telephone number of the primary operational contact at the ground handler.
attributes.references: GDPR Article 4, IATA Ground Handling Agreement (IGHA) Standards

attributes.name: ramp_handling_flag
attributes.description: Indicates whether the handler provides ramp services including aircraft marshalling, chocking, towing, and ground power.

attributes.name: record_created_timestamp
attributes.description: The timestamp when this ground handler record was first created in the system.

attributes.name: record_updated_timestamp
attributes.description: The timestamp when this ground handler record was last modified in the system.

attributes.name: sgha_agreement_reference
attributes.business_glossary_term: Standard Ground Handling Agreement (SGHA) Reference Number
attributes.description: The unique reference number of the Standard Ground Handling Agreement contract governing the relationship with this handler.

attributes.name: sla_breach_count
attributes.description: The total number of Service Level Agreement breaches recorded against this handler during the current measurement period.

products.name: handling_performance
products.description: Transactional record capturing ground handler performance measurement for a completed turnaround or service order. Captures ground handler reference, turnaround or ramp service order reference, flight reference, station, measurement period, KPIs measured (on-time departure contribution, baggage delivery time, damage rate, no-show bag rate), actual vs target values, SLA breach flag, penalty trigger flag, and performance score. Supports SGHA SLA governance and handler contract management.
products.reference: IATA SGHA Annex B — Ground Handling Performance Measurement

attributes.name: handling_performance_id
attributes.description: Unique identifier for the ground handler performance measurement record.

attributes.name: accounts_payable_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to finance.accounts_payable. Business justification: SLA penalties and performance charges from ground handlers are processed through AP for invoice adjustment and payment settlement. Required for contract compliance enforcement, dispute resolution, and

attributes.name: flight_leg_id
attributes.description: Reference to the flight leg associated with this performance measurement. Enables correlation of handler performance with specific flight operations.

attributes.name: ground_handler_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to airport.ground_handler. Business justification: handling_performance measures the performance of a specific ground handler. Currently stores ground_handler_code (STRING). FK to ground_handler provides access to handler details, contract terms, and

attributes.name: occurrence_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to safety.occurrence. Business justification: Handler performance measurement includes safety metrics. Occurrences during turnarounds affect performance scoring, SLA compliance, and penalty triggers. Links operational performance management to sa

attributes.name: ramp_service_order_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to airport.ramp_service_order. Business justification: handling_performance measures performance against a specific ramp_service_order. Currently stores ramp_service_order_number (STRING). FK to ramp_service_order provides access to ordered services, SLA

attributes.name: station_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to airport.station. Business justification: Ground handler performance measurements are recorded for specific airport stations. The handling_performance table currently has station_code as a STRING denormalized attribute, but no FK to station.

attributes.name: turnaround_id
attributes.description: Reference to the turnaround operation being measured. Links to the turnaround record for which this performance assessment applies.

attributes.name: airline_remarks
attributes.description: Free-text remarks or notes provided by airline operations or quality assurance regarding handler performance. Used for dispute resolution and contract management.

attributes.name: baggage_delivery_target_minutes
attributes.description: Contractual target time in minutes for first baggage delivery. Defined in the SGHA or service level agreement with the ground handler.

attributes.name: baggage_delivery_time_minutes
attributes.description: Actual time in minutes from aircraft block-in to first baggage delivered to carousel or claim area. Key KPI for passenger experience and SGHA compliance.

attributes.name: cdm_milestone_compliance_flag
attributes.business_glossary_term: Collaborative Decision Making (CDM) Milestone Compliance Flag
attributes.description: Indicates whether the ground handler met all CDM milestone reporting requirements for this turnaround. Critical for airport slot management and A-CDM compliance.

attributes.name: damage_incident_count
attributes.description: Number of damage incidents (aircraft, baggage, cargo, or GSE) attributed to the ground handler during this turnaround. Used for safety and quality performance tracking.
attributes.references: IATA Safety Audit for Ground Operations (ISAGO)

attributes.name: damage_rate_per_turnaround
attributes.description: Calculated damage rate for this turnaround, expressed as incidents per turnaround. Used for trend analysis and handler comparison.
attributes.references: IATA Safety Audit for Ground Operations (ISAGO)

attributes.name: delay_code_attributed
attributes.description: IATA two-digit delay code attributed to the ground handler if their performance caused or contributed to flight delay. Used for OTP analysis and accountability.

attributes.name: delay_minutes_attributed
attributes.description: Number of delay minutes attributed to the ground handler. Used for OTP impact assessment and cost recovery calculations.

attributes.name: handler_remarks
attributes.description: Free-text remarks or notes provided by the ground handler regarding this turnaround performance. May include explanations for delays or incidents.

attributes.name: measurement_period_end
attributes.description: End timestamp of the performance measurement window. Typically aligned with aircraft block-out time or service order completion.

attributes.name: measurement_period_start
attributes.description: Start timestamp of the performance measurement window. Typically aligned with aircraft block-in time or service order activation.

attributes.name: measurement_recorded_by
attributes.description: Identifier of the system, user, or automated process that recorded this performance measurement. Supports audit trail and data quality validation.

attributes.name: measurement_source_system
attributes.description: Name or code of the source system that generated this performance measurement. Typically SITA Airport Management Platform, CDM system, or airline operations control system.

attributes.name: mishandled_baggage_count
attributes.description: Number of baggage pieces mishandled (delayed, damaged, or lost) during this turnaround attributed to ground handler error. Key metric for IATA Resolution 753 compliance.

attributes.name: no_show_bag_count
attributes.description: Number of bags that failed to arrive at the aircraft for loading despite being checked in. Indicates handler process failures in baggage sorting or transport.

attributes.name: on_time_departure_contribution_flag
attributes.description: Indicates whether the ground handler contributed to achieving on-time departure. True if handler completed all services within target time and did not cause delay.

attributes.name: penalty_amount
attributes.description: Calculated financial penalty amount in the contract currency resulting from SLA breach. Null if no penalty applies. Used for accounts payable adjustment.

attributes.name: penalty_currency_code
attributes.description: ISO 4217 three-letter currency code for the penalty amount. Aligns with the ground handling contract currency.

attributes.name: penalty_trigger_flag
attributes.description: Indicates whether this performance measurement triggers a contractual penalty or financial adjustment. Used for automated billing and contract enforcement.

attributes.name: performance_score
attributes.description: Composite performance score for this turnaround, typically on a 0-100 scale. Calculated from weighted KPIs defined in the SGHA. Used for handler ranking and contract renewal decisions.

attributes.name: record_created_timestamp
attributes.description: Timestamp when this performance measurement record was first created in the system. Used for audit trail and data lineage tracking.

attributes.name: record_updated_timestamp
attributes.description: Timestamp when this performance measurement record was last modified. Supports change tracking and dispute resolution workflows.

attributes.name: safety_incident_flag
attributes.description: Indicates whether a safety incident occurred during this turnaround involving the ground handler. Triggers mandatory reporting and investigation per ISAGO standards.
attributes.references: IATA Safety Audit for Ground Operations (ISAGO)

attributes.name: safety_incident_severity
attributes.description: Severity classification of the safety incident if one occurred. Determines investigation depth and regulatory reporting requirements.
attributes.references: IATA Safety Audit for Ground Operations (ISAGO)

attributes.name: sla_breach_category
attributes.description: Category of SLA breach if applicable. Classifies the type of performance failure for root cause analysis and penalty calculation.

attributes.name: sla_breach_flag
attributes.description: Indicates whether any SLA threshold defined in the SGHA was breached during this turnaround. Triggers contract review and potential penalty assessment.

attributes.name: turnaround_completion_status
attributes.description: Overall completion status of the turnaround from the handlers perspective. Indicates whether all contracted services were successfully delivered.

products.name: airport_irop_event
products.description: Transactional record for an Irregular Operations (IROP) event affecting airport and ground operations. Captures IROP type (weather/ATC/mechanical/security/crew/airport-closure), affected station, start and end timestamps, impacted flight count, impacted PAX count, IROP severity level, CDM coordination flag, recovery plan reference, and responsible operations control center. Serves as the SSOT for IROP events within the airport domain, linking to gate reassignments, turnaround delays, and passenger reaccommodation actions.
products.reference: IATA AHM 780 — Irregular Operations Management

attributes.name: airport_irop_event_id
attributes.description: Unique identifier for the airport IROP event record. Primary key for the airport_irop_event product.

attributes.name: employee_id
attributes.description: Identifier of the airport operations manager or duty manager responsible for coordinating the IROP response at the affected station.

attributes.name: occurrence_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to safety.occurrence. Business justification: IROPs often involve or trigger safety occurrences (emergency evacuations, passenger injuries, operational deviations under pressure). IROP context is essential for understanding safety events during i

attributes.name: station_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to airport.station. Business justification: airport_irop_event affects a specific station. Currently stores affected_station_code (STRING). FK to station provides access to station details, operational capabilities, and ground handler informati

attributes.name: atc_restriction_type
attributes.description: Type of ATC restriction imposed during the IROP event if ATC-related. Examples: ground stop, ground delay program, flow control, airspace closure, reduced arrival rate, departure spacing.
attributes.references: FAA Air Traffic Control Procedures, EUROCONTROL Network Operations

attributes.name: cancelled_flight_count
attributes.description: Number of flights cancelled as a direct result of this IROP event.

attributes.name: cdm_coordination_flag
attributes.description: Indicates whether this IROP event required CDM coordination with airport authority, ATC, and other stakeholders. True if CDM messages were exchanged for collaborative recovery planning.

attributes.name: created_timestamp
attributes.description: Date and time when this IROP event record was first created in the system. Represents initial event detection and logging.

attributes.name: delayed_flight_count
attributes.description: Number of flights delayed beyond scheduled departure or arrival time as a result of this IROP event.

attributes.name: diverted_flight_count

attributes.name: duration_minutes

attributes.name: estimated_cost_currency_code

attributes.name: gate_reassignment_count

attributes.name: impacted_pax_count

attributes.name: irop_end_timestamp

attributes.name: irop_subtype_code

attributes.name: irop_type_code
attributes.description: Classification of the IROP event cause. attributes.name: last_modified_timestamp
attributes.description: Date and time when this IROP event record was last updated. Tracks ongoing event management and status changes.

attributes.name: lessons_learned_documented_flag

attributes.name: notam_reference_number

attributes.name: operational_status
attributes.description: Current lifecycle status of the IROP event. ACTIVE: event is ongoing and impacting operations; MONITORING: event conditions present but not yet impacting; RECOVERING: event ended, recovery actions in progress; RESOLVED: all recovery actions complete; CLOSED: event fully documented and archived.

attributes.name: operations_control_center_code

attributes.name: passenger_compensation_triggered_flag

attributes.name: reaccommodation_action_count

attributes.name: recovery_plan_reference

attributes.name: regulatory_notification_required_flag

attributes.name: regulatory_notification_timestamp

attributes.name: root_cause_analysis_completed_flag

attributes.name: severity_level

attributes.name: weather_condition_description

products.name: station_mro_contract
products.description: This association product represents the commercial maintenance service contract between an approved Part-145 maintenance organisation and an airline operating station. It captures the contractual relationship governing MRO services provided at a specific station, including contract terms, service scope, SLA commitments, and performance tracking. Each record links one approved maintenance organisation to one station with attributes that exist only in the context of this contractual relationship.. Existence Justification: Airlines contract multiple Part-145 approved maintenance organisations at each operating station to provide line maintenance, heavy checks, component services, and AOG support. Each MRO provider operates at multiple stations across the airline's network. The business actively manages these relationships as station-specific MRO service contracts, tracking contract terms, service scope, SLA commitments, pricing, and performance metrics for each station-provider combination.

products.name: station_authorization
products.description: This association product represents the authorization relationship between certifying staff and stations. It captures the station-specific authorization scope, validity periods, shift assignments, and on-call status for licensed aircraft maintenance engineers at each operating station. Each record links one certifying staff member to one station with attributes that exist only in the context of this station-specific authorization.. Existence Justification: In airline maintenance operations, certifying staff (licensed AMEs/A&P mechanics) are authorized to perform maintenance and issue Certificates of Release to Service (CRS) at multiple stations across the airline's network. Each station requires multiple certifying staff to cover shifts, on-call rotations, and operational demands. The business actively manages station-specific authorizations with effective dates, expiry dates, shift assignments, and on-call status for each staff-station combination.

products.name: airport_slot_allocation
products.description: This association product represents the allocation relationship between a scheduled flight and an airport slot. It captures the regulatory and operational linkage between a planned flight operation and its assigned takeoff or landing time at capacity-constrained airports. Each record links one scheduled_flight to one slot with attributes that track allocation timing, compliance, historic rights, and confirmation status that exist only in the context of this specific allocation.. Existence Justification: In airline operations at slot-coordinated airports, a single scheduled flight requires multiple slot allocations (departure slot at origin airport and arrival slot at destination airport), and slots can be reallocated, swapped, or transferred between different scheduled flights across IATA seasons. The slot allocation process is a distinct regulatory and operational business process with relationship-specific data including allocation dates, confirmation status, compliance tracking, and historic precedence rights that belong to neither the scheduled flight nor the slot alone.

A scheduled flight may have different slot times across different seasons or when slots are reallocated, making this an attribute of the allocation relationship rather than an intrinsic property of the scheduled flight itself.]

attributes.name: average_turnaround_time_minutes

attributes.name: certification_level

attributes.name: created_timestamp

attributes.name: crew_size

attributes.name: crew_status

attributes.name: crew_type

attributes.name: currency_code

attributes.name: effective_from_date

attributes.name: effective_to_date

attributes.name: emergency_response_capable

attributes.name: equipment_assigned

attributes.name: fluid_type_authorized

attributes.name: language_proficiency

attributes.name: last_modified_timestamp

attributes.name: last_training_date

attributes.name: next_training_date

attributes.name: notes

attributes.name: operational_hours_capacity

attributes.name: performance_rating

attributes.name: safety_incident_count

attributes.name: shift_pattern
attributes.description: Work schedule pattern assigned to the deicing crew (day shift, night shift, rotating shifts, on-call, or continuous 24x7 coverage).

attributes.name: supervisor_name

attributes.name: relieved_deicing_crew_id

domains.name: route
domains.description: Route network planning and schedule design data including origin-destination (O&D) route definitions, hub-and-spoke network topology, city pairs, frequencies, flight numbers, seasonal schedules, slot allocations at constrained airports, bilateral agreements, codeshare route agreements, ASK (Available Seat Kilometer) capacity planning, and network performance KPIs (OTP, load factor by route). Aligns with Jeppesen scheduling.

products.name: city_pair
products.description: Master definition of an origin-destination (O&D) city pair — the fundamental commercial unit of the airline route network. Captures origin and destination airport/city codes, directionality (one-way vs bidirectional), great circle distance, scheduled distance, IATA region pairing (e.g., TC1-TC2), and market classification (domestic, international, transborder). Serves as the SSOT for all O&D-level demand analysis, RPK aggregation, yield reporting, and market sizing. Referenced by route, market_assessment, and interline agreements.
products.reference: IATA O&D Statistics

attributes.name: city_pair_id
attributes.description: Unique identifier for the origin-destination city pair. Primary key for the city pair master entity.

attributes.name: destination_content_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to marketing.destination_content. Business justification: Destination content often covers city-pair markets broadly ("Traveling to London" content serves all NYC-LON routes). Content marketing operates at market level to maximize content reuse and SEO effec

attributes.name: origin_station_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to airport.station. Business justification: City pairs define markets between specific stations. Market analysis, demand forecasting, competitive assessment, and bilateral agreement evaluation require direct station links. Role prefix 'origin_'

attributes.name: active_flag
attributes.description: Indicates whether this city pair is currently active in the airline's route network. Inactive city pairs are retained for historical analysis and potential future reactivation.

attributes.name: bilateral_agreement_code
attributes.description: Reference code for the bilateral air service agreement governing this city pair (e.g., US-UK Open Skies, US-Japan bilateral). Determines traffic rights, capacity limits, and operational freedoms.

attributes.name: codeshare_eligible_flag
attributes.description: Indicates whether this city pair is eligible for codeshare operations under existing alliance agreements and regulatory approvals.

attributes.name: competitive_intensity
attributes.description: Market competition classification based on number of carriers serving the city pair: monopoly (single carrier), duopoly (two carriers), oligopoly (3-5 carriers), highly_competitive (6+ carriers).

attributes.name: created_timestamp
attributes.description: Timestamp when this city pair record was first created in the system. Used for data lineage and audit trail.

attributes.name: destination_airport_code
attributes.description: Three-letter IATA airport code representing the destination point of the city pair (e.g., JFK, LAX, LHR).

attributes.name: destination_city_code
attributes.description: Three-letter IATA city code for the destination metropolitan area. May differ from airport code when multiple airports serve one city (e.g., LON for LHR/LGW/STN).

attributes.name: destination_country_code
attributes.description: Three-letter ISO country code for the destination country (e.g., USA, GBR, FRA).

attributes.name: destination_iata_region
attributes.description: IATA Traffic Conference region for the destination (TC1=Americas, TC2=Europe/Africa/Middle East, TC3=Asia/Pacific). Used for fare construction and bilateral agreement classification.

attributes.name: directionality
attributes.description: Indicates whether the city pair is defined as one-way (origin to destination only) or bidirectional (both directions treated as same market for analysis).

attributes.name: distance_band
attributes.description: Categorical classification of route length: short_haul (<1500km), medium_haul (1500-4000km), long_haul (4000-8000km), ultra_long_haul (>8000km). Used for fleet assignment, crew planning, and market segmentation.

attributes.name: effective_from_date
attributes.description: Date when this city pair definition became effective in the airline's route network. Used for historical analysis and schedule planning.

attributes.name: effective_to_date
attributes.description: Date when this city pair definition ceased to be effective (nullable for currently active city pairs). Used for historical analysis and route discontinuation tracking.

attributes.name: etops_required_flag
attributes.business_glossary_term: Extended-Range Twin-Engine Operational Performance Standards (ETOPS) Required Flag
attributes.description: Indicates whether ETOPS certification is required for twin-engine aircraft operations on this city pair due to extended overwater or remote routing beyond 60 minutes single-engine diversion time.

attributes.name: great_circle_distance_km
attributes.description: Shortest distance between origin and destination airports measured along the surface of the Earth (great circle route), expressed in kilometers. Used for ASK and RPK calculations.

attributes.name: great_circle_distance_miles
attributes.description: Shortest distance between origin and destination airports measured along the surface of the Earth (great circle route), expressed in statute miles. Used for mileage accrual in FFP programs.

attributes.name: hub_spoke_classification
attributes.description: Network topology classification indicating whether the city pair connects two hubs, a hub to a spoke, two spokes, or operates as a point-to-point route outside the hub network.

attributes.name: interline_eligible_flag
attributes.description: Indicates whether this city pair is eligible for interline ticketing agreements with partner carriers, allowing through-ticketing and baggage transfer.

attributes.name: last_modified_timestamp
attributes.description: Timestamp when this city pair record was last updated. Used for change tracking and data quality monitoring.

attributes.name: market_classification
attributes.description: Classification of the city pair market type: domestic (within same country), international (between different countries), or transborder (specific cross-border markets with special regulatory treatment, e.g., US-Canada).

attributes.name: market_maturity
attributes.description: Lifecycle stage of the city pair market: emerging (new route, low traffic), growth (increasing demand), mature (stable established market), declining (reducing demand).

attributes.name: minimum_connecting_time_minutes
attributes.description: Minimum time in minutes required for passenger connections at the origin or destination hub when this city pair is part of a connecting itinerary. Used for schedule feasibility and inventory availability.

attributes.name: origin_city_code
attributes.description: Three-letter IATA city code for the origin metropolitan area. May differ from airport code when multiple airports serve one city (e.g., NYC for JFK/LGA/EWR).

attributes.name: origin_country_code
attributes.description: Three-letter ISO country code for the origin country (e.g., USA, GBR, FRA).

attributes.name: origin_iata_region
attributes.description: IATA Traffic Conference region for the origin (TC1=Americas, TC2=Europe/Africa/Middle East, TC3=Asia/Pacific). Used for fare construction and bilateral agreement classification.

attributes.name: scheduled_distance_km
attributes.description: Actual flown distance based on typical flight routing including airways, ATC routing, and operational constraints. May differ from great circle distance due to airspace restrictions, weather routing, or operational procedures.

attributes.name: seasonal_pattern
attributes.description: Typical seasonal operating pattern for this city pair: year_round (continuous service), summer_only (IATA summer season), winter_only (IATA winter season), peak_season (high-demand periods), shoulder_season (transitional periods).

attributes.name: slot_constrained_flag
attributes.description: Indicates whether either the origin or destination airport is slot-controlled under IATA Worldwide Slot Guidelines (Level 3 airport), requiring allocated takeoff and landing slots.

attributes.name: time_zone_difference_hours
attributes.description: Time difference in hours between origin and destination time zones. Positive values indicate destination is ahead; negative values indicate destination is behind. Used for schedule planning and passenger communication.

attributes.name: traffic_rights_category
attributes.business_glossary_term: Traffic Rights Category (Freedoms of the Air)
attributes.description: ICAO freedom of the air classification applicable to this city pair, defining the operational rights granted under bilateral agreements (e.g., third_freedom for outbound, fourth_freedom for inbound, fifth_freedom for beyond rights). [ENUM-REF-CANDIDATE: first_freedom|second_freedom|third_freedom|fourth_freedom|fifth_freedom|sixth_freedom|seventh_freedom|eighth_freedom|ninth_freedom — 9 candidates stripped; promote to reference product]

attributes.name: typical_block_time_minutes
attributes.description: Average scheduled block time (gate-to-gate time) in minutes for flights operating this city pair, including taxi time. Used for crew scheduling, aircraft utilization planning, and schedule design.

attributes.name: typical_flight_time_minutes
attributes.description: Average airborne flight time in minutes for this city pair, excluding taxi time. Used for fuel planning and flight operations analysis.

products.name: route
products.description: Master record for a defined airline route between an origin and destination airport pair, representing the authoritative network topology entity. Captures route code, origin and destination IATA airport codes, route type (hub-to-hub, hub-to-spoke, spoke-to-spoke, point-to-point), service type (passenger, cargo, mixed), route status (active, suspended, planned, discontinued), inaugural date, suspension date, and applicable bilateral air service agreement reference. Aligns with Jeppesen NetLine/Sched route master.
products.reference: IATA Route Network Definition

attributes.name: route_id
attributes.description: Unique identifier for the airline route. Primary key for the route master record.

attributes.name: bilateral_asa_id

attributes.name: city_pair_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to route.city_pair. Business justification: Route operates on a specific origin-destination city pair. Currently route has origin_airport_code and destination_airport_code as separate strings. Adding city_pair_id FK normalizes this relationship

attributes.name: cost_centre_id
