attributes.name: destination_content_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to marketing.destination_content. Business justification: Destination marketing content is created for routes served. Content marketing teams produce route-specific destination guides, travel tips, and promotional content to drive bookings on specific routes

attributes.name: destination_station_id
attributes.description: FK to airport.station

attributes.name: manager_employee_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to workforce.employee. Business justification: Routes require assigned route managers who own performance targets, capacity planning, and competitive response. Standard airline network management practice - every major route has a designated manag

attributes.name: origin_station_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to airport.station. Business justification: Routes operate between origin and destination stations. Network planning, slot coordination, bilateral rights validation, and operational readiness all require direct station references. Role prefix '

attributes.name: regulatory_requirement_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to compliance.regulatory_requirement. Business justification: Routes must comply with specific operational requirements (ETOPS certification, noise restrictions, slot coordination mandates). Network planning teams verify regulatory compliance before route launch

attributes.name: authority_type
attributes.description: Regulatory classification of the route: domestic (within single country), international (between countries), or cabotage (domestic service by foreign carrier, typically restricted).

attributes.name: average_load_factor_percent
attributes.description: Historical average load factor (percentage of seats filled) for this route over the trailing 12 months. Key performance indicator for route profitability.

attributes.name: average_otp_percent
attributes.description: Historical average on-time performance percentage (flights arriving within 15 minutes of scheduled time) for this route over the trailing 12 months.

attributes.name: block_time_minutes
attributes.description: Standard scheduled block time in minutes from gate departure (off-blocks) at origin to gate arrival (on-blocks) at destination. Used for crew scheduling and aircraft utilization planning.

attributes.name: codeshare_eligible
attributes.description: Flag indicating whether this route is eligible for codeshare agreements with partner airlines (true) or restricted to own-metal operations only (false).

attributes.name: competitive_route_indicator
attributes.description: Flag indicating whether this route faces direct competition from other carriers (true) or is operated exclusively by this airline (false).

attributes.name: created_timestamp
attributes.description: Timestamp when this route record was first created in the system.

attributes.name: distance_km
attributes.description: Great circle distance between origin and destination airports in kilometers. Used for ASK (Available Seat Kilometer) and RPK (Revenue Passenger Kilometer) calculations.

attributes.name: distance_miles
attributes.description: Great circle distance between origin and destination airports in statute miles. Used for frequent flyer mileage accrual and US DOT reporting.

attributes.name: etops_rating_minutes
attributes.business_glossary_term: Extended-range Twin-engine Operational Performance Standards (ETOPS) Rating (Minutes)
attributes.description: Required ETOPS rating in minutes (e.g., 120, 180, 207, 330) for aircraft operating this route. Null if ETOPS not required.

attributes.name: etops_required
attributes.business_glossary_term: Extended-range Twin-engine Operational Performance Standards (ETOPS) Required Indicator
attributes.description: Flag indicating whether this route requires ETOPS certification due to extended overwater or remote area operations beyond 60 minutes single-engine diversion time.

attributes.name: flight_time_minutes
attributes.description: Standard airborne flight time in minutes from wheels-up at origin to wheels-down at destination, excluding taxi time.

attributes.name: inaugural_date
attributes.description: Date when the route was first launched and entered commercial service.

attributes.name: interline_eligible
attributes.description: Flag indicating whether this route participates in interline ticketing agreements (true), allowing through-ticketing with other carriers, or is restricted (false).

attributes.name: last_modified_timestamp
attributes.description: Timestamp when this route record was last updated in the system.

attributes.name: number_of_competitors
attributes.description: Count of other airlines operating direct service on this origin-destination pair. Zero indicates monopoly route.

attributes.name: operating_season
attributes.description: Season during which the route operates: year-round (all seasons), summer-only (IATA summer schedule), or winter-only (IATA winter schedule).

attributes.name: planned_launch_date
attributes.description: Expected date for route launch for routes in planned status. Null for active or discontinued routes.

attributes.name: profitability_tier
attributes.description: Internal classification of route profitability: tier_1 (highest margin), tier_2 (above average), tier_3 (break-even), tier_4 (loss-making). Used for strategic network decisions.

attributes.name: route_code
attributes.description: Six-character alphanumeric code representing the origin-destination pair (e.g., JFKLHR for New York JFK to London Heathrow). Typically constructed as origin IATA code + destination IATA code.

attributes.name: route_status
attributes.description: Current operational status of the route: active (currently operating), suspended (temporarily halted), planned (approved but not yet launched), or discontinued (permanently ceased).

attributes.name: route_type
attributes.description: Classification of the route based on network topology: hub-to-hub (connecting two major hubs), hub-to-spoke (hub to regional destination), spoke-to-spoke (regional to regional), or point-to-point (direct service bypassing hubs).

attributes.name: seasonal_indicator
attributes.description: Flag indicating whether this route operates seasonally (true) or year-round (false). Seasonal routes typically align with IATA summer/winter schedule seasons.

attributes.name: service_type
attributes.description: Type of service operated on this route: passenger (pax only), cargo (freight only), or mixed (combination of passenger and cargo).

attributes.name: slot_controlled_destination
attributes.description: Flag indicating whether the destination airport is slot-controlled (true), requiring allocated takeoff/landing slots, or non-slot-controlled (false).

attributes.name: slot_controlled_origin
attributes.description: Flag indicating whether the origin airport is slot-controlled (true), requiring allocated takeoff/landing slots, or non-slot-controlled (false).

attributes.name: suspension_date
attributes.description: Date when the route was suspended or discontinued. Null if route is currently active or planned.

attributes.name: weekly_frequency
attributes.description: Number of scheduled flights per week on this route. Used for capacity planning and network optimization.

products.name: flight_number
products.description: Master record for airline flight number designators assigned to routes, capturing the IATA/ICAO carrier code prefix, numeric flight number, suffix (if applicable), direction (outbound/inbound), operating carrier, marketing carrier (for codeshare), flight number type (operating, codeshare, wetlease), effective date range, and associated route. Serves as the SSOT for flight number lifecycle management and codeshare number assignment. Aligns with Jeppesen scheduling and Amadeus Altéa inventory.
products.reference: IATA Flight Number Standard

attributes.name: flight_number_id
attributes.description: Unique system identifier for the flight number record. Primary key.

attributes.name: aircraft_type_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to fleet.aircraft_type. Business justification: Flight numbers are typically assigned with planned aircraft type for schedule publication, GDS distribution, and passenger booking. Linking to aircraft_type enables fleet assignment validation, seat i

attributes.name: assigned_crew_scheduler_employee_id
attributes.business_glossary_term: Assigned Crew Scheduler Employee Id (Foreign Key)
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to workforce.employee. Business justification: Flight numbers are managed by crew scheduling staff who coordinate crew assignments, handle disruptions, and ensure regulatory compliance. Operational necessity for accountability in crew resource man

attributes.name: operating_carrier_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to route.carrier. Business justification: flight_number currently has operating_carrier_code as STRING. Normalizing to carrier.carrier_id creates proper referential integrity. The operating carrier is the airline that physically operates the

attributes.name: partnership_id
attributes.description: Reference to the codeshare agreement governing this flight number assignment. Null for operating flights. Links to the bilateral codeshare contract between marketing and operating carriers.

attributes.name: route_id
attributes.description: Reference to the origin-destination route that this flight number serves. Links to the route master data defining city pairs and network topology.

attributes.name: route_slot_allocation_id
attributes.description: Reference to the airport slot allocation record for constrained airports. Links to the assigned takeoff/landing time window granted by the airport coordinator or Air Traffic Control (ATC).

attributes.name: bilateral_agreement_reference
attributes.description: Reference code or identifier for the bilateral air service agreement between countries that authorizes this route. Governs traffic rights and frequencies under international aviation treaties.
attributes.references: ICAO Policies on Charges for Airports and Air Navigation Services

attributes.name: block_time_minutes
attributes.description: Scheduled block time in minutes from gate departure (out) to gate arrival (in) for this flight number. Represents the total elapsed time including taxi, flight, and arrival taxi.

attributes.name: carrier_code
attributes.business_glossary_term: International Air Transport Association (IATA) Carrier Code
attributes.description: Two-character IATA airline designator code identifying the carrier (e.g., AA for American Airlines, BA for British Airways). Used as prefix for flight numbers.

attributes.name: created_timestamp
attributes.description: Timestamp when this flight number record was first created in the system. Audit trail for data lineage and compliance.

attributes.name: destination_airport_code
attributes.description: Three-letter IATA airport code for the flight's destination/arrival airport (e.g., LAX, CDG, SIN).

attributes.name: direction
attributes.description: Directional classification of the flight within the route network: outbound (departing from hub), inbound (arriving at hub), circular (multi-leg routing returning to origin).

attributes.name: distance_km
attributes.description: Great circle distance in kilometers between origin and destination airports. Used for Revenue Passenger Kilometer (RPK) and Available Seat Kilometer (ASK) calculations.

attributes.name: effective_from_date
attributes.description: Date when this flight number assignment becomes active and valid for scheduling and reservations. Start of the flight number's lifecycle.

attributes.name: effective_to_date
attributes.description: Date when this flight number assignment expires or is discontinued. Null indicates an open-ended assignment. End of the flight number's lifecycle.

attributes.name: etops_certified_indicator
attributes.business_glossary_term: Extended-range Twin-engine Operational Performance Standards (ETOPS) Certified Indicator
attributes.description: Flag indicating whether this flight operates under Extended-range Twin-engine Operational Performance Standards (ETOPS) certification for extended overwater or remote area operations (true) or standard operations (false).

attributes.name: flight_number
attributes.description: Numeric flight number designator (1-4 digits) with optional single-letter suffix. Combined with carrier code forms the complete flight identifier (e.g., 1234, 567A).

attributes.name: flight_number_status
attributes.description: Current lifecycle status of the flight number: active (in operational use), inactive (temporarily not scheduled), suspended (operationally blocked), pending (approved but not yet active), retired (permanently discontinued).

attributes.name: flight_number_type
attributes.description: Classification of the flight number based on operational arrangement: operating (airline operates the flight), codeshare (marketing carrier sells seats on another carrier's flight), wetlease (aircraft leased with crew), drylease (aircraft leased without crew), blocked (reserved but not in active use).

attributes.name: flight_time_minutes
attributes.description: Scheduled airborne flight time in minutes from wheels-off to wheels-on. Excludes ground taxi time.

attributes.name: frequency_pattern
attributes.description: Seven-character string indicating days of operation (1=operates, 0=does not operate) in sequence Monday through Sunday (e.g., 1111100 = Monday-Friday only, 0000011 = weekends only).

attributes.name: full_flight_number
attributes.description: Complete flight number including carrier code and numeric designator (e.g., AA1234, BA567A). This is the externally-known business identifier displayed to passengers and used in reservations.

attributes.name: gds_distribution_indicator
attributes.description: Flag indicating whether this flight number is distributed through Global Distribution Systems (GDS) such as Amadeus, Sabre, Travelport for travel agency bookings (true) or restricted to direct channels (false).

attributes.name: icao_carrier_code
attributes.business_glossary_term: International Civil Aviation Organization (ICAO) Carrier Code
attributes.description: Three-character ICAO airline designator code for the carrier (e.g., AAL for American Airlines, BAW for British Airways). Used in flight plans and air traffic control communications.

attributes.name: interline_eligible_indicator
attributes.description: Flag indicating whether this flight number is eligible for interline ticketing agreements with partner carriers (true) or restricted to online bookings only (false).

attributes.name: last_modified_timestamp
attributes.description: Timestamp when this flight number record was last updated. Audit trail for change tracking and data quality monitoring.

attributes.name: marketing_carrier_code
attributes.description: IATA code of the airline that markets and sells the flight. For codeshare flights, this is the carrier whose flight number is displayed. For operating flights, this matches the carrier_code.

attributes.name: modified_by_user
attributes.description: User identifier or system account that last modified this flight number record. Supports audit trail and accountability for schedule changes.

attributes.name: network_hub_indicator
attributes.description: Flag indicating whether this flight serves a hub airport in the carrier's hub-and-spoke network topology (true) or is a point-to-point spoke route (false).

attributes.name: origin_airport_code
attributes.description: Three-letter IATA airport code for the flight's origin/departure airport (e.g., JFK, LHR, DXB).

attributes.name: priority_ranking
attributes.description: Internal priority ranking for this flight number within the carrier's network. Lower numbers indicate higher priority for resource allocation, slot protection, and operational recovery during Irregular Operations (IROP).

attributes.name: remarks
attributes.description: Free-text field for operational notes, special handling instructions, or additional context about this flight number assignment. May include codeshare display rules, seasonal variations, or historical notes.

attributes.name: revenue_management_class
attributes.description: Revenue management classification code used for yield optimization and inventory control strategies. Aligns with Sabre AirVision Revenue Management system classifications.

attributes.name: season_code
attributes.description: IATA season code indicating the scheduling season (e.g., S24 for Summer 2024, W24 for Winter 2024/2025). Format: S/W followed by two-digit year.

attributes.name: seasonal_indicator
attributes.description: Flag indicating whether this flight number is assigned on a seasonal basis (true) or year-round (false). Seasonal flights typically operate during peak travel periods (summer, winter holidays).

attributes.name: service_type
attributes.description: Type of service provided by the flight: passenger (revenue passenger service), cargo (freight only), combi (mixed passenger and cargo), ferry (non-revenue aircraft repositioning), positioning (crew or equipment repositioning).

attributes.name: traffic_rights_category
attributes.business_glossary_term: Traffic Rights Category (Freedoms of the Air)
attributes.description: Classification of air traffic rights under the Freedoms of the Air framework (e.g., First Freedom, Second Freedom, Third Freedom, Fourth Freedom, Fifth Freedom, Sixth Freedom, Seventh Freedom, Eighth Freedom, Ninth Freedom). Defines the scope of international route authority.
attributes.references: ICAO Convention on International Civil Aviation (Chicago Convention)

products.name: schedule_season
products.description: Reference master for IATA scheduling seasons defining the temporal boundaries for all schedule planning, slot coordination, and capacity deployment activities. Captures season code (e.g., S25, W25/26), season type (summer/winter), start and end dates per IATA calendar, schedule submission deadlines (initial, supplementary), slot return deadlines, and IATA Schedules Conference dates. Serves as the mandatory temporal anchor referenced by seasonal_schedule, route_slot_allocation, ask_plan, and route_fleet_assignment.
products.reference: IATA Scheduling Guidelines

attributes.name: schedule_season_id
attributes.description: Unique identifier for the IATA scheduling season record. Primary key.

attributes.name: created_timestamp
attributes.description: The timestamp when this schedule season record was first created in the system. Supports audit trail and data lineage tracking.

attributes.name: daylight_saving_transition_applicable_flag
attributes.business_glossary_term: Daylight Saving Time (DST) Transition Applicable Flag
attributes.description: Indicates whether daylight saving time transitions occur during this scheduling season, requiring schedule adjustments for affected routes and airports. True if DST transitions occur within the season period.
attributes.references: ICAO Annex 2 - Rules of the Air

attributes.name: duration_days
attributes.description: Total number of calendar days in the scheduling season, calculated from start_date to end_date inclusive. Typically ranges from 180 to 185 days.

attributes.name: end_date
attributes.description: The last date of the IATA scheduling season when the seasonal schedule expires. Typically the Saturday before the next season starts.

attributes.name: historical_use_it_or_lose_it_threshold_percent
attributes.description: The minimum slot utilization percentage required during this season to retain grandfather rights for the next equivalent season. Typically 80% per IATA WSG, but may vary by jurisdiction (e.g., EU Regulation 95/93). Expressed as a percentage (e.g., 80.00 for 80%).
attributes.references: IATA Worldwide Slot Guidelines (WSG), EU Regulation 95/93

attributes.name: iata_schedules_conference_end_date
attributes.business_glossary_term: International Air Transport Association (IATA) Schedules Conference End Date
attributes.description: The end date of the biannual IATA Schedules Conference. Conferences typically last 3-5 days and occur twice per year (spring for winter season, fall for summer season).

attributes.name: iata_schedules_conference_location
attributes.business_glossary_term: International Air Transport Association (IATA) Schedules Conference Location
attributes.description: The city and country where the IATA Schedules Conference for this season is held (e.g., 'Geneva, Switzerland', 'Singapore').

attributes.name: iata_schedules_conference_start_date
attributes.business_glossary_term: International Air Transport Association (IATA) Schedules Conference Start Date
attributes.description: The start date of the biannual IATA Schedules Conference where airlines, airports, and slot coordinators meet to coordinate seasonal schedules, negotiate slots, and finalize bilateral agreements.

attributes.name: iata_season_year
attributes.business_glossary_term: International Air Transport Association (IATA) Season Year
attributes.description: The calendar year in which the season primarily falls or begins, used for grouping and filtering seasons by year (e.g., 2025 for S25 or W25/26).

attributes.name: initial_schedule_submission_deadline
attributes.description: The deadline by which airlines must submit their initial seasonal schedule requests to slot coordinators and Global Distribution Systems (GDS). Typically occurs several months before season start per IATA Schedules Information Standards (SIS).

attributes.name: last_modified_timestamp
attributes.description: The timestamp when this schedule season record was last updated. Supports change tracking and audit compliance.

attributes.name: northern_hemisphere_dst_end_date
attributes.business_glossary_term: Northern Hemisphere Daylight Saving Time (DST) End Date
attributes.description: The date when daylight saving time ends in the northern hemisphere during this season (typically first Sunday in November for North America, last Sunday in October for Europe). Null if not applicable to this season.
attributes.references: ICAO Annex 2 - Rules of the Air

attributes.name: northern_hemisphere_dst_start_date
attributes.business_glossary_term: Northern Hemisphere Daylight Saving Time (DST) Start Date
attributes.description: The date when daylight saving time begins in the northern hemisphere during this season (typically second Sunday in March for North America, last Sunday in March for Europe). Null if not applicable to this season.
attributes.references: ICAO Annex 2 - Rules of the Air

attributes.name: notes
attributes.description: Free-text field for capturing additional information, special circumstances, or operational notes relevant to this scheduling season (e.g., COVID-19 slot relief measures, exceptional slot waiver periods, regulatory changes).

attributes.name: peak_travel_period_flag
attributes.description: Indicates whether this season is considered a peak travel period with higher demand and load factors. Summer seasons are typically peak periods for leisure travel in the northern hemisphere.

attributes.name: schedule_season_status
attributes.description: Current lifecycle status of the scheduling season. Planning: season is being prepared and schedules are being submitted. Active: season is currently in effect. Completed: season has ended but data is still operational. Archived: season is historical and closed for reporting only.

attributes.name: season_code
attributes.business_glossary_term: International Air Transport Association (IATA) Season Code
attributes.description: IATA standard season code identifying the scheduling period. Format: S25 for Summer 2025, W25/26 for Winter 2025/2026. This is the externally-known business identifier for the season.

attributes.name: season_name
attributes.description: Human-readable descriptive name for the scheduling season (e.g., 'Summer 2025', 'Winter 2025/2026').

attributes.name: season_type
attributes.description: Classification of the scheduling season into IATA-defined periods: summer (typically late March to late October) or winter (typically late October to late March).

attributes.name: slot_coordination_cycle
attributes.description: The IATA slot coordination cycle identifier corresponding to this season, used by slot coordinators at Level 2 and Level 3 airports for capacity management and slot allocation.

attributes.name: slot_return_deadline
attributes.description: The final date by which airlines must return unused or unwanted airport slots to the slot coordinator to avoid use-it-or-lose-it penalties. Critical for slot allocation compliance at Level 3 coordinated airports.

attributes.name: southern_hemisphere_dst_end_date
attributes.business_glossary_term: Southern Hemisphere Daylight Saving Time (DST) End Date
attributes.description: The date when daylight saving time ends in the southern hemisphere during this season (typically first Sunday in April for Australia). Null if not applicable to this season.
attributes.references: ICAO Annex 2 - Rules of the Air

attributes.name: southern_hemisphere_dst_start_date
attributes.business_glossary_term: Southern Hemisphere Daylight Saving Time (DST) Start Date
attributes.description: The date when daylight saving time begins in the southern hemisphere during this season (typically first Sunday in October for Australia). Null if not applicable to this season.
attributes.references: ICAO Annex 2 - Rules of the Air

attributes.name: start_date
attributes.description: The first date of the IATA scheduling season when the seasonal schedule becomes effective. Typically the last Sunday of March for summer seasons and last Sunday of October for winter seasons.

attributes.name: supplementary_schedule_submission_deadline
attributes.description: The deadline for airlines to submit supplementary or revised schedule changes after the initial submission. Allows for adjustments closer to the season start date.

products.name: seasonal_schedule
products.description: Operational schedule plan for a specific route during an IATA season, defining the planned service pattern including days of operation (DOW mask), departure and arrival times (local and UTC), frequency per week, cabin configuration, planned aircraft type, block time, and schedule status (planned, filed, approved, active, cancelled). Represents the filed schedule submitted to IATA and slot coordinators. Aligns with Jeppesen Flight Planning System seasonal schedule module.
products.reference: IATA Scheduling Guidelines (SSG)

attributes.name: seasonal_schedule_id
attributes.description: Unique identifier for the seasonal schedule record. Primary key for this entity.

attributes.name: aircraft_type_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to fleet.aircraft_type. Business justification: Seasonal schedules must reference valid aircraft types to enforce fleet availability constraints, validate seat capacity, verify ETOPS certification for route requirements, and support schedule-to-fle

attributes.name: cost_centre_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to finance.cost_centre. Business justification: Seasonal schedules drive seasonal cost allocation for winter/summer network planning. Airlines track operating costs by schedule season and cost centre to analyze seasonal profitability, optimize capa

attributes.name: operating_carrier_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to route.carrier. Business justification: seasonal_schedule has operating_carrier_code as STRING. Normalizing to carrier.carrier_id for the carrier operating the scheduled flight. This creates proper referential integrity for schedule records

attributes.name: origin_station_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to airport.station. Business justification: Seasonal schedules specify origin station for slot coordination, gate allocation planning, ground handler contracting, and operational resource planning. Role prefix 'origin_' distinguishes from desti

attributes.name: route_id
attributes.description: Reference to the route for which this seasonal schedule is defined. Links to the route master data defining the origin-destination city pair.

attributes.name: schedule_planner_employee_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to workforce.employee. Business justification: Seasonal schedules are created by network planning analysts who design frequency patterns, optimize connections, and coordinate with slot coordinators. Clear ownership requirement for schedule quality

attributes.name: schedule_season_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to route.schedule_season. Business justification: Seasonal_schedule currently has iata_season_code (STRING) but should reference schedule_season via FK. Every seasonal schedule operates within a defined IATA season. The schedule_season table is the a

attributes.name: aircraft_configuration_code
attributes.description: Internal code identifying the specific cabin configuration planned for this schedule. References the seat map and cabin class layout (e.g., number of first, business, premium economy, and economy seats). Used for inventory and revenue management.

attributes.name: aircraft_owner
attributes.description: Indicates the ownership/lease arrangement for the aircraft planned for this schedule. Values: owned (airline-owned), wet_lease (leased with crew), dry_lease (leased without crew), acmi (Aircraft Crew Maintenance Insurance lease), charter (chartered from third party).

attributes.name: approved_timestamp
attributes.description: Date and time when this seasonal schedule received final approval from all required authorities (slot coordinators, civil aviation authorities, bilateral agreement partners). Nullable if not yet approved.

attributes.name: arrival_time_local
attributes.description: Scheduled arrival time in local time at the destination airport. Format: HH:MM (24-hour). This is the planned gate arrival time (on-blocks time) in the destination airport local timezone. May show next-day arrival if flight crosses midnight.

attributes.name: arrival_time_utc
attributes.description: Scheduled arrival time in UTC (Coordinated Universal Time). Format: HH:MM (24-hour). Used for operational planning and coordination across time zones.

attributes.name: ask_planned
attributes.description: Planned Available Seat Kilometers for this seasonal schedule. Calculated as total seats multiplied by route distance in kilometers. Key capacity metric for network planning and revenue management.

attributes.name: block_time_minutes
attributes.description: Scheduled block time in minutes. Block time is the total time from gate departure (off-blocks) to gate arrival (on-blocks), including taxi time at both airports. Used for crew duty calculations and operational planning.

attributes.name: codeshare_indicator
attributes.description: Boolean flag indicating whether this seasonal schedule is part of a codeshare agreement. True if the flight is operated by one airline but marketed under multiple airline codes. False for solely-operated flights.

attributes.name: created_timestamp
attributes.description: Date and time when this seasonal schedule record was first created in the system. Audit field for data lineage and change tracking.

attributes.name: day_change_indicator
attributes.description: Indicates the number of days difference between departure and arrival dates. Values: 0 (same day), 1 (next day), 2 (two days later), -1 (previous day for flights crossing international date line westbound). Used to calculate actual arrival date from departure date.

attributes.name: days_of_operation
attributes.description: Seven-character string representing the days of the week this flight operates. Each position represents a day (Monday through Sunday). Values: 1=operates, 0=does not operate. Example: 1111100 means Monday-Friday only. Also known as DOW (Day of Week) mask.

attributes.name: departure_time_local
attributes.description: Scheduled departure time in local time at the origin airport. Format: HH:MM (24-hour). This is the planned gate departure time (off-blocks time) in the origin airport local timezone.

attributes.name: departure_time_utc
attributes.description: Scheduled departure time in UTC (Coordinated Universal Time). Format: HH:MM (24-hour). Used for operational planning and coordination across time zones.

attributes.name: destination_airport_code
attributes.description: Three-letter IATA airport code for the arrival airport. Represents the destination point of this flight leg.

attributes.name: destination_terminal
attributes.description: Terminal identifier at the destination airport where this flight arrives. Used for passenger information and ground operations planning. Format varies by airport (e.g., 1, A, T1, North).

attributes.name: effective_from_date
attributes.description: The first date on which this seasonal schedule becomes effective. Marks the start of the schedule validity period within the IATA season.

attributes.name: effective_to_date
attributes.description: The last date on which this seasonal schedule is effective. Marks the end of the schedule validity period within the IATA season. Nullable for open-ended schedules.

attributes.name: filed_timestamp
attributes.description: Date and time when this seasonal schedule was officially filed with IATA and relevant slot coordinators. Represents the submission timestamp for regulatory and coordination purposes.

attributes.name: flight_number
attributes.description: The airline flight number assigned to this seasonal schedule. Typically consists of airline code followed by numeric identifier (e.g., AA1234). This is the published flight number visible to passengers.

attributes.name: frequency_per_week
attributes.description: The number of times this flight operates per week during the seasonal schedule period. Derived from the days_of_operation mask. Range: 0-7.

attributes.name: last_modified_timestamp
attributes.description: Date and time when this seasonal schedule record was last updated. Audit field for change tracking and data quality monitoring.

attributes.name: marketing_carrier_code
attributes.description: Two-character IATA airline code of the carrier that markets and sells the flight. For codeshare flights, this may differ from the operating carrier. Typically matches the airline prefix in the flight number.

attributes.name: meal_service_code
attributes.description: IATA meal service code indicating the type of meal service planned for this flight. Common values: B=Breakfast, L=Lunch, D=Dinner, S=Snack, M=Meal (unspecified), N=No meal service. Used for catering planning and passenger information.
attributes.references: IATA Passenger Services Conference Resolutions Manual

attributes.name: origin_terminal
attributes.description: Terminal identifier at the origin airport from which this flight departs. Used for passenger information and ground operations planning. Format varies by airport (e.g., 1, A, T1, North).

attributes.name: remarks
attributes.description: Free-text field for additional notes, special instructions, or operational comments related to this seasonal schedule. May include information about seasonal variations, special events, or coordination notes.

attributes.name: schedule_status
attributes.description: Current lifecycle status of the seasonal schedule. Values: planned (initial planning stage), filed (submitted to IATA and slot coordinators), approved (regulatory and slot approval received), active (currently operating), suspended (temporarily not operating), cancelled (permanently removed from schedule).

attributes.name: service_type
attributes.description: IATA service type code indicating the nature of the flight service. Values: J=Passenger Jet, F=Cargo, C=Charter, P=Positioning/Ferry. Passenger scheduled services typically use J.

attributes.name: slot_time_destination
attributes.description: Allocated slot time at the destination airport for landing. At slot-coordinated airports, this is the specific time window allocated by the slot coordinator. Format: HH:MM (24-hour local time). May differ slightly from scheduled arrival time.

attributes.name: slot_time_origin
attributes.description: Allocated slot time at the origin airport for takeoff. At slot-coordinated airports, this is the specific time window allocated by the slot coordinator. Format: HH:MM (24-hour local time). May differ slightly from scheduled departure time.

attributes.name: total_seats
attributes.description: Total number of passenger seats available on the planned aircraft configuration for this seasonal schedule. Used for capacity planning and ASK (Available Seat Kilometer) calculations.

attributes.name: traffic_restriction_code
attributes.description: IATA traffic restriction code indicating any limitations on passenger carriage. Examples: G=Government approval required, X=Technical stop (no traffic rights), T=Technical stop with traffic rights. Blank if no restrictions apply.

products.name: route_slot_allocation
products.description: Airport slot allocation record for a specific route and season at a slot-coordinated (Level 2 or Level 3) airport. Captures slot coordinator reference number, allocated departure or arrival time, slot type (historical grandfather, new entrant, pool), slot series (full season or partial), days of operation, aircraft type restriction, slot status (requested, allocated, confirmed, returned, swapped), and IATA slot coordination conference reference. Critical for constrained airports (LHR, JFK, CDG, NRT). Aligns with IATA Worldwide Slot Guidelines (WSG).
products.reference: IATA Worldwide Slot Guidelines (WSG)

attributes.name: route_slot_allocation_id
attributes.description: Unique identifier for the airport slot allocation record. Primary key for the route slot allocation entity.

attributes.name: cost_centre_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to finance.cost_centre. Business justification: Airport slot costs are significant operating expenses at slot-constrained airports (LHR, JFK, NRT). Airlines allocate slot acquisition, holding, and opportunity costs to route cost centres for route p

attributes.name: regulatory_requirement_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to compliance.regulatory_requirement. Business justification: Slot allocations at coordinated airports must comply with IATA WSG guidelines and local coordinator requirements. Slot compliance officers track regulatory obligations. Essential for slot coordination

attributes.name: route_id
attributes.description: Reference to the route for which this slot is allocated. Links to the route master data defining the origin-destination city pair and service characteristics.

attributes.name: schedule_season_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to route.schedule_season. Business justification: Route_slot_allocation currently has slot_season_code (STRING) but should reference schedule_season via FK. Slot allocations are granted for specific IATA seasons. The schedule_season table contains th

attributes.name: slot_coordinator_employee_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to workforce.employee. Business justification: Slot allocations at constrained airports require designated coordinators who negotiate with airport authorities, manage historical rights, and coordinate swaps. Regulatory requirement and operational

attributes.name: station_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to airport.station. Business justification: Slot allocations are station-specific regulatory permissions. Slot utilization tracking, coordinator coordination, historic rights validation, and compliance reporting require direct station link. No

attributes.name: aircraft_size_category
attributes.description: General aircraft size category restriction for the slot. Used when specific type restrictions are not applied but size-based capacity management is in effect.

attributes.name: aircraft_type_restriction
attributes.description: ICAO aircraft type code restriction for this slot allocation (e.g., B738, A320, B77W). Some slots at noise-sensitive or capacity-constrained airports may be restricted to specific aircraft types or size categories. Null if no restriction applies.
attributes.references: ICAO Aircraft Type Designators, IATA Worldwide Slot Guidelines (WSG)

attributes.name: allocated_time
attributes.description: The specific time allocated for the departure or arrival movement in local airport time (HH:MM format, 24-hour clock). This is the coordinated time window the airline must operate within.

attributes.name: bilateral_agreement_reference
attributes.description: Reference to the bilateral air service agreement between countries that governs traffic rights and slot access for this route. Relevant for international routes where slot allocation must comply with bilateral treaty provisions.
attributes.references: ICAO Bilateral Air Service Agreements, IATA Worldwide Slot Guidelines (WSG)

attributes.name: created_timestamp
attributes.description: Timestamp when this slot allocation record was first created in the system. Part of audit trail for slot coordination data lineage.

attributes.name: days_of_operation
attributes.description: Days of the week on which this slot is allocated, represented as a string of digits where 1=Monday, 2=Tuesday, 3=Wednesday, 4=Thursday, 5=Friday, 6=Saturday, 7=Sunday. For example, '1357' means Monday, Wednesday, Friday, Sunday. Empty or '1234567' indicates daily operation.

attributes.name: effective_from_date
attributes.description: The first date on which this slot allocation becomes effective. For full season slots, this is typically the season start date. For partial season slots, this is the first date of the allocated period.

attributes.name: effective_to_date
attributes.description: The last date on which this slot allocation is effective. For full season slots, this is typically the season end date. For partial season slots, this is the last date of the allocated period.

attributes.name: environmental_restriction_flag
attributes.description: Indicates whether this slot is subject to environmental restrictions such as noise abatement procedures, curfew limitations, or emissions-based access rules. True if environmental constraints apply to the slot usage.
attributes.references: ICAO Annex 16 (Environmental Protection), IATA Worldwide Slot Guidelines (WSG)

attributes.name: historical_precedence_flag
attributes.description: Indicates whether this slot carries historical precedence (grandfather rights) for the airline. True if the airline has operated this slot in previous equivalent seasons and is entitled to priority retention under IATA use-it-or-lose-it rules (80% usage threshold).

attributes.name: last_modified_timestamp
attributes.description: Timestamp when this slot allocation record was last updated. Tracks changes to slot status, times, or other allocation parameters throughout the coordination lifecycle.

attributes.name: slot_allocation_timestamp
attributes.description: Date and time when the slot coordinator officially allocated this slot to the airline. Marks the transition from requested to allocated status.

attributes.name: slot_cancellation_reason
attributes.description: Reason for cancellation of the slot allocation by the coordinator or airline. Populated when slot_status is 'cancelled'. May include regulatory changes, airport capacity reductions, or airline non-compliance with usage requirements.

attributes.name: slot_conference_reference
attributes.description: Reference to the IATA slot coordination conference where this slot was discussed or allocated (e.g., IATA Slot Conference Worldwide, Regional Slot Conference). IATA holds biannual slot conferences where airlines and coordinators negotiate slot allocations.

attributes.name: slot_confirmation_timestamp
attributes.description: Date and time when the airline confirmed acceptance and intention to use the allocated slot. Required by IATA WSG to retain slot rights for future seasons.

attributes.name: slot_coordination_level
attributes.description: IATA coordination level of the airport for this slot. Level 1 (non-coordinated): no slot coordination required; Level 2 (schedule-facilitated): voluntary schedule coordination; Level 3 (fully coordinated): mandatory slot allocation by coordinator. Only Level 2 and Level 3 airports issue formal slot allocations.

attributes.name: slot_coordinator_reference_number
attributes.description: Unique reference number assigned by the airport slot coordinator to this slot allocation. Used for official correspondence and slot coordination activities.

attributes.name: slot_movement_type
attributes.description: Indicates whether this slot is for an arrival or departure movement at the coordinated airport.

attributes.name: slot_priority_score
attributes.description: Numeric score assigned by the slot coordinator to prioritize this slot request relative to competing requests. Higher scores indicate higher priority. Factors include historical precedence, new entrant status, network connectivity, and public interest considerations.

attributes.name: slot_request_timestamp
attributes.description: Date and time when the airline submitted the slot request to the coordinator. Used to establish priority in slot allocation processes where multiple carriers request the same time.

attributes.name: slot_return_reason
attributes.description: Business reason for returning the slot to the coordinator pool. Populated when slot_status is 'returned'. Common reasons include route discontinuation, schedule optimization, fleet changes, or commercial underperformance.

attributes.name: slot_series_type
attributes.description: Indicates whether the slot allocation covers the full IATA season, a partial period within the season, or a single date. Full season slots run for the entire summer or winter season; partial season slots cover a subset of dates.

attributes.name: slot_status
attributes.description: Current status of the slot allocation in the coordination lifecycle. Requested: airline has submitted a slot request; Allocated: coordinator has provisionally allocated the slot; Confirmed: airline has confirmed acceptance and usage; Returned: airline has returned the slot to the pool; Swapped: slot has been exchanged with another carrier; Cancelled: slot allocation has been cancelled.

attributes.name: slot_swap_partner_airline_code
attributes.description: IATA airline code of the partner airline involved in a slot swap transaction. Populated only when slot_status is 'swapped'. Slot swaps allow airlines to exchange slots to optimize their network schedules.
attributes.references: IATA Airline Codes, IATA Worldwide Slot Guidelines (WSG)

attributes.name: slot_swap_reference_number
attributes.description: Unique reference number for the slot swap transaction, assigned by the slot coordinator. Links this slot allocation to the corresponding swapped slot record.

attributes.name: slot_tolerance_minutes
attributes.description: Number of minutes before or after the allocated time within which the flight operation is considered compliant with the slot. Typically -5 to +10 minutes for departures and -10 to +5 minutes for arrivals, but varies by airport coordinator policy.

attributes.name: slot_type
attributes.description: Classification of the slot allocation type. Historical grandfather slots are held by airlines with historic precedence; new entrant slots are reserved for new carriers; pool slots are available for general allocation; ad hoc slots are one-time allocations; emergency slots are for irregular operations.

attributes.name: slot_usage_percentage
attributes.description: Percentage of allocated slot times that were actually used by the airline during the season. IATA WSG requires 80% usage to retain historical rights. Calculated as (flights operated within slot tolerance / total allocated slot occurrences) * 100.

attributes.name: terminal_restriction
attributes.description: Specific terminal designation at the airport where this slot must be used (e.g., Terminal 1, Terminal 5, Concourse B). Some airports allocate slots with terminal restrictions due to capacity or operational constraints.

products.name: hub_spoke_topology
products.description: Master record defining the airline's hub-and-spoke network structure and connection bank design. Captures each hub airport with tier classification (primary, secondary, focus city), spoke relationships with thickness indicators (thin, thick, regional), minimum connecting time (MCT) by terminal pair, and connection bank definitions (arrival wave start/end, departure wave start/end, target connection windows). Used in schedule design to maximize connecting passenger flows, minimize misconnect risk, and optimize wave-system timing at hub airports. Aligns with Jeppesen NetLine/Network planning methodology.
products.reference: Hub-and-Spoke Network Design

attributes.name: hub_spoke_topology_id
attributes.description: Unique identifier for the hub-spoke network topology record. Primary key for the hub_spoke_topology data product.

attributes.name: hub_station_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to airport.station. Business justification: Hub/spoke topology defines network structure around hub stations. Connection bank planning, MCT validation, gate sequencing, and wave optimization require direct hub station link. Role prefix 'hub_' d

attributes.name: occurrence_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to safety.occurrence. Business justification: Hub operations have distinct safety profiles (connection pressure, ground congestion, complex taxi routes). Required for hub safety performance analysis and minimum connecting time reviews. Links topo

attributes.name: allocated_slot_time
attributes.description: The specific time slot (HH:MM format) allocated by the airport coordinator for this hub-spoke route at slot-constrained airports. Represents the authorized takeoff or landing time window.

attributes.name: arrival_wave_end_time
attributes.description: Local time (HH:MM format) when the arrival wave ends for this connection bank. Marks the completion of the inbound flight cluster, after which the departure wave begins.

attributes.name: arrival_wave_start_time
attributes.description: Local time (HH:MM format) when the arrival wave begins for this connection bank. Represents the start of the inbound flight cluster arriving at the hub to feed connecting passengers into the departure wave.

attributes.name: bilateral_agreement_reference
attributes.description: Reference to the bilateral air service agreement between countries that governs this hub-spoke route. Bilateral agreements specify traffic rights, frequencies, capacity, and designated carriers for international routes.

attributes.name: codeshare_partner_indicator
attributes.description: Boolean flag indicating whether this hub-spoke route includes codeshare agreements with partner airlines. True if codeshare partners place their flight numbers on this route, false if operated solely under the airline's own code.

attributes.name: connection_bank_number
attributes.description: Sequential identifier for the connection bank (wave) within the daily hub operation. Most hubs operate 3-6 connection banks per day, each consisting of an arrival wave followed by a departure wave to maximize connecting passenger flows.

attributes.name: daily_frequency_count
attributes.description: Number of daily flights operated on this hub-spoke route pair. Used to calculate spoke thickness and assess market density.

attributes.name: departure_wave_end_time
attributes.description: Local time (HH:MM format) when the departure wave ends for this connection bank. Marks the completion of the outbound flight cluster for this connection bank.

attributes.name: departure_wave_start_time
attributes.description: Local time (HH:MM format) when the departure wave begins for this connection bank. Represents the start of the outbound flight cluster departing from the hub, carrying connecting passengers from the arrival wave.

attributes.name: effective_end_date
attributes.description: The date when this hub-spoke topology configuration expires or is superseded by a new configuration. Null for open-ended configurations. Used to maintain historical network topology for analysis.

attributes.name: effective_start_date
attributes.description: The date when this hub-spoke topology configuration becomes effective in the network schedule. Aligns with IATA seasonal schedule changes (typically late March and late October).

attributes.name: hub_tier_classification
attributes.description: Strategic classification of the hub airport within the airline's network hierarchy. Primary hubs are the largest connecting points with the most extensive spoke networks, secondary hubs serve regional markets, focus cities offer limited connecting service, and regional hubs serve specific geographic areas.

attributes.name: last_modified_timestamp
attributes.description: Timestamp when this hub-spoke topology record was last modified. Used for change tracking and audit purposes in network planning systems.

attributes.name: minimum_connecting_time_minutes
attributes.description: The minimum time in minutes required for passengers to make a legal connection between arriving and departing flights at this hub for this specific terminal pair or connection type. MCT varies by domestic-to-domestic, domestic-to-international, international-to-international, and terminal configuration.
attributes.references: IATA MCT Standards, Airport Authority Regulations

attributes.name: misconnect_risk_score
attributes.description: Calculated risk score (0-100) indicating the probability of passenger misconnections on this hub-spoke route based on historical OTP, MCT adequacy, connection bank timing, and operational complexity. Higher scores indicate higher misconnect risk.

attributes.name: network_optimization_priority
attributes.description: Strategic priority level assigned to this hub-spoke route for network optimization initiatives. Critical routes are core to the network and receive highest investment, low priority routes may be candidates for frequency reduction or elimination.

attributes.name: planned_ask_capacity
attributes.description: The planned ASK capacity for this hub-spoke route, calculated as available seats multiplied by route distance in kilometers. Key metric for network capacity planning and resource allocation.

attributes.name: planning_system_source
attributes.description: Identifier of the source planning system that created or manages this hub-spoke topology record (e.g., Jeppesen NetLine/Network, internal network planning tools). Used for data lineage and system integration.

attributes.name: seasonal_pattern
attributes.description: Indicates the seasonal operating pattern for this hub-spoke route. Year-round routes operate continuously, seasonal routes operate only during specific periods (summer leisure markets, winter ski destinations), peak season routes have enhanced frequency during high-demand periods.

attributes.name: slot_constrained_indicator
attributes.description: Boolean flag indicating whether the hub or spoke airport is slot-constrained, requiring allocated takeoff and landing slots. True for Level 3 coordinated airports (e.g., LHR, JFK, HND), false for non-coordinated airports.

attributes.name: spoke_airport_code
attributes.description: Three-letter IATA airport code identifying the spoke (destination) airport connected to the hub. Represents the endpoint of a hub-spoke route segment.

attributes.name: spoke_thickness_indicator
attributes.description: Classification of the spoke route based on frequency and capacity. Thin spokes have 1-2 daily flights, thick spokes have 3+ daily flights with larger aircraft, regional spokes serve nearby markets with high frequency, ultra-thin spokes are seasonal or less-than-daily, and mega spokes are high-density trunk routes with multiple widebody flights.

attributes.name: target_connection_window_minutes
attributes.description: The ideal time window in minutes between arrival and departure for optimal passenger connections within this connection bank. Balances MCT requirements with passenger convenience and operational efficiency. Typically 60-120 minutes for domestic connections, 90-180 minutes for international.

attributes.name: target_load_factor_percentage
attributes.description: The target load factor (percentage of seats filled) for this hub-spoke route, used in network planning and revenue management. Expressed as a percentage (e.g., 82.50 for 82.5%).

attributes.name: target_otp_percentage
attributes.description: The target on-time performance percentage for this hub-spoke route, defined as flights arriving within 15 minutes of scheduled time. Used to set operational performance goals and monitor connection reliability.
attributes.references: DOT On-Time Performance Standards, IATA Standards

attributes.name: topology_status
attributes.description: Current lifecycle status of this hub-spoke topology record. Active topologies are in operation, planned topologies are scheduled for future implementation, suspended topologies are temporarily inactive (e.g., due to IROP or seasonal suspension), discontinued topologies have been permanently removed from the network.

attributes.name: weekly_frequency_count
attributes.description: Total number of flights operated per week on this hub-spoke route pair. Accounts for day-of-week variations in schedule.

products.name: partnership
products.description: Master record for all carrier-to-carrier commercial partnership arrangements at the route level, encompassing codeshare agreements, interline ticketing agreements, special prorate agreements (SPAs), and joint venture arrangements. Captures partner carrier IATA code, agreement type (codeshare free-flow, codeshare block-space, standard interline, SPA, through-check-in, joint venture), applicable routes or O&D pairs, revenue sharing basis (prorate, block-space, revenue-share pool), cabin class availability, baggage through-check eligibility, e-ticket interline capability, effective date, expiry date, and agreement status. Serves as the SSOT for all route-level partnership data enabling multi-carrier itinerary construction, codeshare flight number assignment, and interline revenue settlement.

attributes.name: agreement_number
attributes.description: Externally-known unique business identifier for this partnership agreement, used in contracts and commercial correspondence.

attributes.name: agreement_status
attributes.description: Current lifecycle state of the partnership agreement: draft (under negotiation), pending_approval (awaiting executive sign-off), active (in force), suspended (temporarily inactive), terminated (ended before expiry), or expired (reached natural end date).

attributes.name: agreement_type
attributes.description: Classification of the commercial partnership arrangement: codeshare free-flow (marketing carrier sells seats on operating carrier inventory), codeshare block-space (marketing carrier purchases block of seats), standard interline (ticketing and baggage transfer agreement), special prorate agreement (SPA - negotiated revenue split), through-check-in (baggage handling only), or joint venture (revenue and cost sharing alliance).

attributes.name: antitrust_immunity_granted
attributes.description: Indicates whether the partnership (typically joint venture) has been granted antitrust immunity by regulatory authorities, allowing revenue and capacity coordination.

attributes.name: approval_date

attributes.name: approved_by

attributes.name: auto_renewal_enabled
attributes.description: Indicates whether the partnership agreement automatically renews for an additional term upon expiry unless either party provides notice of termination.

attributes.name: baggage_through_check_eligible
attributes.description: Indicates whether passengers on interline itineraries under this agreement are eligible for baggage through-check (baggage checked to final destination without re-check at transfer point).

attributes.name: block_space_seat_count
attributes.description: Number of seats purchased by the marketing carrier under a block-space codeshare agreement. Null if not a block-space agreement.

attributes.name: cabin_class_availability
attributes.description: Comma-separated list of cabin classes (e.g., F, J, W, Y) for which this partnership agreement applies. Null if applies to all classes.

attributes.name: codeshare_flight_number_range_end
attributes.description: Ending flight number in the range allocated to the marketing carrier for codeshare flights under this agreement. Null if not a codeshare agreement.

attributes.name: codeshare_flight_number_range_start
attributes.description: Starting flight number in the range allocated to the marketing carrier for codeshare flights under this agreement. Null if not a codeshare agreement.

attributes.name: created_timestamp

attributes.name: effective_date
attributes.description: Date on which the partnership agreement becomes active and binding.

attributes.name: eticket_interline_capable
attributes.description: Indicates whether electronic ticketing is supported for interline itineraries under this agreement (both carriers must support e-ticket interline).

attributes.name: expiry_date
attributes.description: Date on which the partnership agreement expires or is scheduled to terminate. Null for open-ended agreements.

attributes.name: frequent_flyer_accrual_eligible
attributes.description: Indicates whether passengers can accrue frequent flyer miles/points on the partner carrier when traveling on codeshare or interline flights under this agreement.

attributes.name: frequent_flyer_redemption_eligible
attributes.description: Indicates whether passengers can redeem frequent flyer miles/points for award travel on the partner carrier under this agreement.

attributes.name: gds_distribution_enabled
attributes.description: Indicates whether codeshare flights under this agreement are distributed through Global Distribution Systems (Amadeus, Sabre, Travelport) for travel agent booking.

attributes.name: last_modified_timestamp
attributes.description: Timestamp when this partnership agreement record was last updated in the system.

attributes.name: minimum_connecting_time_minutes
attributes.description: Minimum time in minutes required for passenger connections between the partner carriers under this agreement, used for interline itinerary construction.

attributes.name: notes
attributes.description: Free-text field for additional comments, special terms, or operational notes related to this partnership agreement.

attributes.name: notice_period_days
attributes.description: Number of days advance notice required by either party to terminate the partnership agreement.

attributes.name: prorate_percentage
attributes.description: Percentage of ticket revenue allocated to the partner carrier under prorate revenue sharing. Null if revenue_sharing_basis is not prorate.

attributes.name: revenue_sharing_basis
attributes.description: Method by which revenue is allocated between partner carriers: prorate (IATA standard prorate formula based on mileage), block_space (fixed payment for seat block), revenue_share_pool (joint venture pooling), cost_plus (cost reimbursement plus margin), or fixed_fee (flat payment per flight or period).

attributes.name: route_scope
attributes.description: Geographic scope of the partnership agreement: specific_od_pair (applies to one origin-destination pair), regional_network (applies to routes within a region), or global_network (applies to all routes between the carriers).

attributes.name: settlement_currency_code
attributes.description: Three-letter ISO 4217 currency code in which revenue settlements between partner carriers are conducted under this agreement.

attributes.name: settlement_frequency
attributes.description: Frequency at which revenue settlements are processed between partner carriers: weekly, biweekly, monthly, or quarterly.

attributes.name: special_service_request_passthrough
attributes.description: Indicates whether Special Service Requests (meal preferences, wheelchair assistance, etc.) are passed through between carriers for interline passengers under this agreement.

attributes.name: termination_date
attributes.description: Actual date on which the partnership agreement was terminated, if terminated before the scheduled expiry_date. Null if not terminated early.

attributes.name: termination_reason
attributes.description: Free-text explanation of why the partnership agreement was terminated early, if applicable.

products.name: interline_agreement
products.description: Master record for interline ticketing and traffic agreements between the airline and partner carriers at the route or network level. Captures partner carrier IATA code, agreement type (standard interline, special prorate agreement, through-check-in), applicable O&D pairs, prorate basis (IATA prorate factor, mileage, negotiated), baggage through-check eligibility, e-ticket interline capability, BSP/ARC settlement basis, effective date, and agreement status. Enables multi-carrier itinerary construction and revenue settlement.

attributes.description: Foreign key linking to finance.cost_centre. Business justification: Interline agreements generate prorate revenue and settlement costs tracked by cost centres. Airlines allocate interline revenue, prorate expenses, and BSP/ARC settlement costs to route cost centres fo

attributes.name: agreement_notes
attributes.description: Free-text field for additional notes, special conditions, restrictions, or operational instructions related to the interline agreement.

attributes.name: agreement_status
attributes.description: Current lifecycle status of the interline agreement indicating whether it is active, suspended, terminated, pending approval, expired, or under negotiation.

attributes.name: agreement_type
attributes.description: Classification of the interline agreement defining the scope and nature of the partnership (standard interline, special prorate agreement, through check-in, codeshare interline, virtual interline, bilateral prorate).

attributes.name: alliance_membership
attributes.description: Indicates whether the interline agreement is facilitated by membership in a global airline alliance (Star Alliance, oneworld, SkyTeam, Value Alliance) or is a standalone bilateral agreement (none).

attributes.name: baggage_through_check_eligible
attributes.description: Boolean flag indicating whether baggage can be checked through to the final destination across both carriers under this interline agreement (True) or must be reclaimed and re-checked (False).

attributes.name: codeshare_eligible
attributes.description: Boolean flag indicating whether this interline agreement permits codeshare flight operations between the airline and partner carrier (True) or is limited to standard interline ticketing (False).

attributes.name: created_timestamp
attributes.description: Timestamp when this interline agreement record was first created in the system.

attributes.name: e_ticket_interline_capable
attributes.description: Boolean flag indicating whether electronic ticketing (e-ticket) is supported for interline itineraries under this agreement (True) or paper tickets are required (False).

attributes.name: effective_date
attributes.description: Date on which the interline agreement becomes binding and operational for ticketing and traffic purposes.

attributes.name: expiration_date
attributes.description: Date on which the interline agreement expires or terminates. Nullable for open-ended agreements subject to notice-based termination.

attributes.name: frequent_flyer_accrual_eligible
attributes.business_glossary_term: Frequent Flyer Program (FFP) Accrual Eligible Flag
attributes.description: Boolean flag indicating whether passengers can accrue frequent flyer miles or points on the partner carrier segments under this interline agreement (True) or not (False).

attributes.name: gds_distribution_enabled
attributes.business_glossary_term: Global Distribution System (GDS) Distribution Enabled Flag
attributes.description: Boolean flag indicating whether interline itineraries under this agreement are available for booking through Global Distribution Systems (GDS) such as Amadeus, Sabre, and Travelport (True) or restricted to direct channels (False).

attributes.name: irop_reprotection_eligible
attributes.description: Boolean flag indicating whether passengers can be reprotected on the partner carrier in case of irregular operations (IROP) such as delays, cancellations, or missed connections (True) or not (False).

attributes.name: last_modified_timestamp
attributes.description: Timestamp when this interline agreement record was last updated or modified in the system.

attributes.name: liability_limit_sdr
attributes.business_glossary_term: Liability Limit in Special Drawing Rights (SDR)
attributes.description: Maximum liability limit per passenger for baggage, delay, or injury claims under the interline agreement, expressed in Special Drawing Rights (SDR) as defined by the Montreal Convention.

attributes.name: minimum_connecting_time_minutes
attributes.description: Minimum connecting time in minutes required at the transfer point for interline connections under this agreement. Ensures operational feasibility of through-ticketing.

attributes.name: modified_by_user
attributes.description: Identifier of the user or system process that last modified this interline agreement record. Supports audit trail and data governance.

attributes.name: prorate_basis
attributes.description: Method used to allocate revenue between carriers for interline journeys: IATA prorate factor, mileage-based calculation, negotiated fixed split, revenue share percentage, or cost-plus model.

attributes.name: prorate_percentage
attributes.description: Negotiated percentage of total fare allocated to the operating carrier or partner carrier under the prorate agreement. Expressed as a percentage (0.00 to 100.00).

attributes.name: route_scope
attributes.description: Defines the geographic or network scope of the interline agreement: network-wide (all routes), specific city pair, regional coverage, hub-and-spoke network, or alliance network.

attributes.name: settlement_basis
attributes.description: Financial settlement mechanism for interline revenue: BSP (Billing and Settlement Plan), ARC (Airlines Reporting Corporation), direct billing between carriers, ICH (IATA Clearing House), or bilateral settlement agreement.
attributes.references: IATA Resolution 728 - Billing and Settlement Plan

attributes.name: special_prorate_agreement_number
attributes.description: Unique identifier for a Special Prorate Agreement (SPA) filed with IATA or negotiated bilaterally, if applicable. Nullable for standard interline agreements.

attributes.name: ssr_handling_agreement
attributes.description: Defines the level of Special Service Request (SSR) data exchange and handling between carriers: full SSR exchange, limited SSR support, or no SSR exchange.

products.name: bilateral_asa
products.description: Master record for bilateral Air Service Agreements (ASAs) between countries that govern the airline's right to operate routes between two nations. Captures agreement name, country pair, agreement type (traditional bilateral, open skies, liberal bilateral), designated carriers, permitted route rights (3rd/4th/5th/7th freedom), capacity entitlements (frequency limits, seat limits, ASK limits), tariff filing requirements, cabotage restrictions, effective date, and regulatory authority references. Serves as the legal foundation for international route authority.
products.reference: ICAO Air Service Agreements

attributes.name: bilateral_asa_id
attributes.description: Unique identifier for the bilateral air service agreement record.
attributes.references: ICAO Doc 9626 Manual on the Regulation of International Air Transport

attributes.name: regulatory_authority_id
