International affairs teams track authority contacts for amendment negotiations. Removes denormalized author

attributes.name: agreement_name
attributes.description: Official name or title of the bilateral air service agreement, typically referencing the two countries involved.
attributes.references: ICAO Doc 9626 Manual on the Regulation of International Air Transport

attributes.name: agreement_number
attributes.description: Official reference number or treaty identifier assigned to the bilateral air service agreement by the governing authorities.
attributes.references: ICAO Doc 9626 Manual on the Regulation of International Air Transport

attributes.name: agreement_status
attributes.description: Current lifecycle status of the bilateral air service agreement indicating whether it is in force, suspended, terminated, awaiting ratification, under negotiation, or expired.
attributes.references: ICAO Doc 9626 Manual on the Regulation of International Air Transport

attributes.name: agreement_type
attributes.description: Classification of the bilateral air service agreement based on the level of liberalization and restrictions. Traditional bilateral agreements have strict capacity and frequency controls; open skies agreements remove most commercial restrictions; liberal bilateral agreements offer significant freedoms with some limitations; restrictive bilateral agreements impose tight controls on operations.
attributes.references: ICAO Doc 9626 Manual on the Regulation of International Air Transport

attributes.name: amendment_count
attributes.description: Number of amendments, protocols, or memoranda of understanding that have been added to the original bilateral air service agreement.
attributes.references: ICAO Doc 9626 Manual on the Regulation of International Air Transport

attributes.name: ask_limit_country_a
attributes.business_glossary_term: Available Seat Kilometer (ASK) Limit Country A
attributes.description: Maximum Available Seat Kilometers permitted per week or month for designated carriers of Country A under the bilateral agreement. Null if unlimited.
attributes.references: ICAO Doc 9626 Manual on the Regulation of International Air Transport

attributes.name: ask_limit_country_b
attributes.business_glossary_term: Available Seat Kilometer (ASK) Limit Country B
attributes.description: Maximum Available Seat Kilometers permitted per week or month for designated carriers of Country B under the bilateral agreement. Null if unlimited.
attributes.references: ICAO Doc 9626 Manual on the Regulation of International Air Transport

attributes.name: cabotage_permitted
attributes.description: Indicates whether the agreement permits cabotage (eighth or ninth freedom rights), allowing an airline of one country to carry passengers or cargo between two points within the other country.
attributes.references: ICAO Doc 9626 Manual on the Regulation of International Air Transport

attributes.name: capacity_entitlement_type
attributes.description: Type of capacity entitlement specified in the agreement. Unlimited allows unrestricted capacity; predetermined sets fixed capacity levels; Bermuda-type links capacity to demand; frequency-limited restricts number of flights; seat-limited restricts number of seats; ASK-limited restricts Available Seat Kilometers.
attributes.references: ICAO Doc 9626 Manual on the Regulation of International Air Transport

attributes.name: change_of_gauge_permitted
attributes.description: Indicates whether the agreement permits change of gauge operations, allowing an airline to change aircraft size at an intermediate point on a route.
attributes.references: ICAO Doc 9626 Manual on the Regulation of International Air Transport

attributes.name: codeshare_permitted
attributes.description: Indicates whether the agreement permits codeshare arrangements between designated carriers and other airlines.
attributes.references: ICAO Doc 9626 Manual on the Regulation of International Air Transport

attributes.name: country_a_code
attributes.description: ISO 3166-1 alpha-3 code for the first country party to the bilateral agreement.

attributes.name: country_b_code
attributes.description: ISO 3166-1 alpha-3 code for the second country party to the bilateral agreement.

attributes.name: created_timestamp
attributes.description: Timestamp when this bilateral air service agreement record was first created in the system.

attributes.name: designated_carriers_country_a
attributes.description: List or description of airlines designated by Country A to operate services under the bilateral air service agreement. May specify airline names, IATA codes, or designation criteria.
attributes.references: ICAO Doc 9626 Manual on the Regulation of International Air Transport

attributes.name: designated_carriers_country_b
attributes.description: List or description of airlines designated by Country B to operate services under the bilateral air service agreement. May specify airline names, IATA codes, or designation criteria.
attributes.references: ICAO Doc 9626 Manual on the Regulation of International Air Transport

attributes.name: dispute_resolution_mechanism
attributes.description: Description of the dispute resolution mechanism specified in the agreement, such as arbitration, consultation, or referral to ICAO.
attributes.references: ICAO Doc 9626 Manual on the Regulation of International Air Transport

attributes.name: effective_date
attributes.description: Date on which the bilateral air service agreement entered into force and became legally binding, typically following ratification by both countries.
attributes.references: ICAO Doc 9626 Manual on the Regulation of International Air Transport

attributes.name: expiration_date
attributes.description: Date on which the bilateral air service agreement is scheduled to expire or terminate, if applicable. Null for agreements with indefinite duration.
attributes.references: ICAO Doc 9626 Manual on the Regulation of International Air Transport

attributes.name: fifth_freedom_rights
attributes.description: Indicates whether the agreement grants fifth freedom rights, allowing an airline of Country A to carry passengers or cargo between Country B and a third country as part of a service originating or terminating in Country A.
attributes.references: ICAO Doc 9626 Manual on the Regulation of International Air Transport

attributes.name: fourth_freedom_rights
attributes.description: Indicates whether the agreement grants fourth freedom rights, allowing an airline of Country A to carry passengers or cargo from Country B to Country A.
attributes.references: ICAO Doc 9626 Manual on the Regulation of International Air Transport

attributes.name: frequency_limit_country_a
attributes.description: Maximum number of weekly or monthly flight frequencies permitted for designated carriers of Country A under the bilateral agreement. Null if unlimited.
attributes.references: ICAO Doc 9626 Manual on the Regulation of International Air Transport

attributes.name: frequency_limit_country_b
attributes.description: Maximum number of weekly or monthly flight frequencies permitted for designated carriers of Country B under the bilateral agreement. Null if unlimited.
attributes.references: ICAO Doc 9626 Manual on the Regulation of International Air Transport

attributes.name: interline_permitted
attributes.description: Indicates whether the agreement permits interline ticketing agreements between designated carriers and other airlines.
attributes.references: ICAO Doc 9626 Manual on the Regulation of International Air Transport

attributes.name: last_amendment_date
attributes.description: Date of the most recent amendment, protocol, or memorandum of understanding to the bilateral air service agreement.
attributes.references: ICAO Doc 9626 Manual on the Regulation of International Air Transport

attributes.name: last_modified_timestamp
attributes.description: Timestamp when this bilateral air service agreement record was last modified in the system.

attributes.name: notes
attributes.description: Additional notes, comments, or special provisions related to the bilateral air service agreement that do not fit into other structured fields.
attributes.references: ICAO Doc 9626 Manual on the Regulation of International Air Transport

attributes.name: route_schedule_annex
attributes.description: Reference to the annex or schedule attached to the bilateral agreement that specifies the authorized routes, intermediate points, and beyond points for designated carriers.
attributes.references: ICAO Doc 9626 Manual on the Regulation of International Air Transport

attributes.name: seat_limit_country_a
attributes.description: Maximum number of seats per week or month permitted for designated carriers of Country A under the bilateral agreement. Null if unlimited.
attributes.references: ICAO Doc 9626 Manual on the Regulation of International Air Transport

attributes.name: seat_limit_country_b
attributes.description: Maximum number of seats per week or month permitted for designated carriers of Country B under the bilateral agreement. Null if unlimited.
attributes.references: ICAO Doc 9626 Manual on the Regulation of International Air Transport

attributes.name: seventh_freedom_rights
attributes.description: Indicates whether the agreement grants seventh freedom rights, allowing an airline of Country A to operate services entirely outside its home country, between Country B and a third country.
attributes.references: ICAO Doc 9626 Manual on the Regulation of International Air Transport

attributes.name: signature_date
attributes.description: Date on which the bilateral air service agreement was officially signed by authorized representatives of both countries.
attributes.references: ICAO Doc 9626 Manual on the Regulation of International Air Transport

attributes.name: tariff_approval_mechanism
attributes.description: Mechanism for tariff approval specified in the agreement. Double approval requires both countries to approve; country of origin allows the airline's home country to approve; double disapproval means tariffs are approved unless both countries disapprove; free pricing allows airlines to set fares without approval; zone pricing establishes fare zones.
attributes.references: ICAO Doc 9626 Manual on the Regulation of International Air Transport

attributes.name: tariff_filing_required
attributes.description: Indicates whether designated carriers are required to file tariffs (fares and rates) with the aeronautical authorities of both countries for approval before implementation.
attributes.references: ICAO Doc 9626 Manual on the Regulation of International Air Transport

attributes.name: termination_date
attributes.description: Actual date on which the bilateral air service agreement was terminated or suspended, if applicable.
attributes.references: ICAO Doc 9626 Manual on the Regulation of International Air Transport

attributes.name: third_freedom_rights
attributes.description: Indicates whether the agreement grants third freedom rights, allowing an airline of Country A to carry passengers or cargo from Country A to Country B.
attributes.references: ICAO Doc 9626 Manual on the Regulation of International Air Transport

attributes.name: plan_notes

attributes.name: plan_status

attributes.name: planned_ask

attributes.name: planned_block_hours

attributes.name: planned_business_class_seats
attributes.description: Number of business class seats planned per flight on this route. Part of the cabin mix configuration.

attributes.name: planned_cask
attributes.business_glossary_term: Planned Cost per Available Seat Kilometer (CASK)
attributes.description: Planned unit cost per Available Seat Kilometer for this route. Used in profitability analysis and route performance evaluation. Business-confidential financial metric.

attributes.name: planned_economy_seats
attributes.description: Number of economy class seats planned per flight on this route. Part of the cabin mix configuration.

attributes.name: planned_first_class_seats
attributes.description: Number of first class seats planned per flight on this route. Part of the cabin mix configuration.

attributes.name: planned_frequency
attributes.description: Number of planned flight departures on this route during the season or planning period. Represents service frequency (e.g., daily, 3x weekly).

attributes.name: planned_premium_economy_seats
attributes.description: Number of premium economy seats planned per flight on this route. Part of the cabin mix configuration.

attributes.name: planned_rask
attributes.business_glossary_term: Planned Revenue per Available Seat Kilometer (RASK)
attributes.description: Planned unit revenue per Available Seat Kilometer for this route. Used in revenue forecasting and route performance evaluation. Business-confidential financial metric.

attributes.name: planned_total_seats
attributes.description: Total number of seats planned per flight on this route, summed across all cabin classes. Represents the aircraft gauge capacity.

attributes.name: planned_yield
attributes.business_glossary_term: Planned Yield (Revenue per Revenue Passenger Kilometer)

attributes.name: planning_period_end_date
attributes.description: End date of the specific planning period within the season (e.g., end of a specific month or week within the season).

attributes.name: planning_period_start_date
attributes.description: Start date of the specific planning period within the season (e.g., start of a specific month or week within the season).

attributes.name: planning_period_type
attributes.description: Granularity of the capacity planning period. Indicates whether this plan represents monthly, weekly, seasonal, or annual capacity deployment.

attributes.name: slot_allocation_status

attributes.name: target_load_factor_percent
attributes.description: Target load factor (percentage of seats filled) planned for this route and season. Used as a performance benchmark for revenue management and network optimization.

products.name: route_performance
products.description: Operational performance record for a route over a defined measurement period (monthly or seasonal), capturing actual vs planned KPIs including OTP (On-Time Performance percentage), load factor (actual passengers / available seats), RPK (Revenue Passenger Kilometers), ASK (Available Seat Kilometers), RASK (Revenue per ASK), CASK (Cost per ASK), yield (revenue per RPK), cancellation rate, diversion rate, and average block time variance. Serves as the route-level operational scorecard. Distinct from flight-level OOOI data owned by the flight domain.
products.reference: IATA Industry Statistics

attributes.name: route_performance_id
attributes.description: Unique identifier for the route performance measurement record. Primary key.

attributes.name: analyst_employee_id

attributes.name: budget_plan_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to finance.budget_plan. Business justification: Route performance variance analysis requires linking actuals to budget. Airlines compare actual route performance metrics (revenue, costs, load factor) against budget plans for variance reporting, for

attributes.name: campaign_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to marketing.campaign. Business justification: Campaign effectiveness analysis requires linking marketing spend to route performance outcomes (load factor, revenue, passenger counts). Post-campaign ROI analysis measures whether route-targeted camp

attributes.name: cost_centre_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to finance.cost_centre. Business justification: Route performance measurement requires cost centre attribution for P&L reporting. Airlines track actual route revenue, costs, and profitability by cost centre for management reporting, route performan

attributes.name: route_id
attributes.description: Reference to the route being measured. Links to the route master data defining the origin-destination pair, flight number pattern, and network topology.

attributes.name: schedule_season_id
attributes.description: Reference to the IATA schedule season during which this performance was measured (e.g., Summer 2024, Winter 2023/24). Links to schedule_season for season boundaries and slot coordination context.

attributes.name: ask
attributes.description: The total number of seat-kilometers available for sale on this route. Calculated as sum of (available seats on each flight * flight distance in km). Fundamental capacity metric.
attributes.references: IATA Traffic Statistics, ICAO Statistical Reporting

attributes.name: available_seats_total
attributes.description: The total number of seats available for sale on all operated flights on this route during the measurement period. Basis for load factor calculation.

attributes.name: average_block_time_minutes
attributes.description: The mean block time (gate-to-gate elapsed time) for all operated flights on this route during the measurement period. Used for schedule planning and crew productivity analysis.

attributes.name: average_delay_minutes
attributes.description: The mean arrival delay in minutes for all operated flights on this route during the measurement period. Negative values indicate early arrivals.

attributes.name: block_time_variance_minutes
attributes.description: The difference between average actual block time and scheduled block time. Positive values indicate flights took longer than scheduled; negative values indicate shorter actual times. Used for schedule buffer optimization.

attributes.name: cancellation_rate_percent
attributes.description: The percentage of scheduled flights that were cancelled. Calculated as (flights cancelled / flights scheduled) * 100. Key operational reliability metric.

attributes.name: cask
attributes.description: Cost per unit of capacity. Calculated as (total cost / ASK). Key unit cost metric for route efficiency analysis. Expressed in cost_currency_code per kilometer.

attributes.name: cost_currency_code
attributes.description: The three-letter ISO 4217 currency code in which total_cost_amount is denominated (e.g., USD, EUR, GBP).

attributes.name: created_timestamp
attributes.description: The date and time when this route performance record was first created in the system. Audit trail for data lineage and compliance.
attributes.references: ISO 8601 Timestamp Format, Internal Data Governance Policy

attributes.name: diversion_rate_percent
attributes.description: The percentage of operated flights that were diverted. Calculated as (flights diverted / flights operated) * 100. Indicator of weather, ATC, or operational disruption impact.

attributes.name: flights_cancelled_count
attributes.description: The total number of scheduled flights that were cancelled on this route during the measurement period.

attributes.name: flights_diverted_count
attributes.description: The total number of flights that were diverted to an alternate airport on this route during the measurement period.

attributes.name: flights_operated_count
attributes.description: The total number of flights that actually departed on this route during the measurement period. Excludes cancelled flights.

attributes.name: flights_scheduled_count
attributes.description: The total number of flights scheduled to operate on this route during the measurement period, as published in the airline schedule.

attributes.name: grade
attributes.description: Overall qualitative assessment of route performance based on composite scoring of OTP, load factor, yield, and RASK against targets. Used for executive dashboards and network optimization prioritization.

attributes.name: last_modified_timestamp
attributes.description: The date and time when this route performance record was most recently updated. Audit trail for data lineage and compliance.
attributes.references: ISO 8601 Timestamp Format, Internal Data Governance Policy

attributes.name: load_factor_percent
attributes.description: The percentage of available seats that were occupied by revenue passengers. Calculated as (passengers carried / available seats) * 100. Core capacity utilization metric.

attributes.name: measurement_period_end_date
attributes.description: The last date of the performance measurement period. Typically the last day of a calendar month or the end of a seasonal period.

attributes.name: measurement_period_start_date
attributes.description: The first date of the performance measurement period. Typically the first day of a calendar month or the start of a seasonal period.

attributes.name: measurement_period_type
attributes.description: The granularity of the performance measurement period. Monthly is most common for operational scorecards; seasonal aligns with IATA schedule seasons; custom supports ad-hoc analysis windows.

attributes.name: notes
attributes.description: Free-text commentary on exceptional performance factors, IROP events, competitive actions, seasonal effects, or other context relevant to interpreting the performance metrics for this period.

attributes.name: otp_percent
attributes.description: The percentage of operated flights that arrived within 15 minutes of scheduled arrival time. Industry-standard KPI for route punctuality. Calculated as (on-time arrivals / flights operated) * 100.
attributes.references: IATA Punctuality Standards, DOT 14 CFR Part 234

attributes.name: passengers_carried_count
attributes.description: The total number of revenue passengers transported on this route during the measurement period. Excludes non-revenue passengers (crew, deadheads, etc.).

attributes.name: rask
attributes.description: Revenue per unit of capacity. Calculated as (total revenue / ASK). Key unit revenue metric for route profitability analysis. Expressed in revenue_currency_code per kilometer.

attributes.name: revenue_currency_code
attributes.description: The three-letter ISO 4217 currency code in which total_revenue_amount is denominated (e.g., USD, EUR, GBP).

attributes.name: rpk
attributes.description: The total number of kilometers flown by revenue passengers on this route. Calculated as sum of (passengers on each flight * flight distance in km). Fundamental traffic volume metric.
attributes.references: IATA Traffic Statistics, ICAO Statistical Reporting

attributes.name: total_cost_amount
attributes.description: The total operating cost allocated to this route during the measurement period, including direct costs (fuel, crew, airport charges) and allocated indirect costs (maintenance, overhead). Used for route profitability analysis.

attributes.name: total_revenue_amount
attributes.description: The total passenger revenue generated on this route during the measurement period, including base fare, fuel surcharges, and ancillary revenue allocated to the route. Excludes cargo revenue.

attributes.name: yield
attributes.description: Revenue per unit of traffic. Calculated as (total revenue / RPK). Measures pricing power and fare realization. Expressed in revenue_currency_code per kilometer.

products.name: market_assessment
products.description: Commercial market assessment record for a route or O&D city pair, capturing demand analysis inputs used in network planning decisions. Captures O&D market size (total passengers), airline market share, competitor capacity (ASKs), competitor frequencies, average market fare, revenue opportunity estimate, traffic type mix (O&D vs connecting), seasonality index, growth trend, and assessment date. Supports new route launch decisions, frequency changes, and route suspension analysis. Distinct from route_performance which tracks actuals.
products.reference: IATA MIDT / OAG Market Data

attributes.name: assessment_date

attributes.name: assessment_notes

attributes.name: assessment_status
attributes.description: Current lifecycle status of the market assessment in the network planning workflow.

attributes.name: assessment_type
attributes.description: Type of network planning decision this assessment supports (e.g., new route launch, frequency change, route suspension, seasonal adjustment, competitive response, network optimization).

attributes.name: average_market_fare_usd
attributes.business_glossary_term: Average Market Fare USD (United States Dollar)
attributes.description: Average one-way fare in USD across all carriers in this O&D market, representing market pricing level for revenue opportunity estimation.
attributes.references: IATA BSP (Billing and Settlement Plan) Fare Data

attributes.name: bilateral_agreement_status
attributes.description: Status of bilateral air service agreement between origin and destination countries (open skies, restricted, pending, not applicable), governing traffic rights and capacity.

attributes.name: business_traffic_percent
attributes.description: Percentage of total market traffic attributed to business travelers, important for cabin mix and fare strategy decisions.

attributes.name: codeshare_opportunity_flag
attributes.description: Boolean flag indicating whether codeshare partnership opportunities exist in this market to enhance network reach without deploying own capacity.

attributes.name: competitor_capacity_ask_annual
attributes.business_glossary_term: Competitor Capacity ASK (Available Seat Kilometer) Annual
attributes.description: Total annual competitor capacity measured in ASK (Available Seat Kilometers) deployed in this market, used for competitive capacity benchmarking.

attributes.name: competitor_weekly_frequencies
attributes.description: Total number of weekly flight frequencies operated by all competitors in this O&D market, indicating competitive service intensity.

attributes.name: connecting_traffic_percent
attributes.description: Percentage of total traffic that is connecting through a hub, complementing O&D traffic to total 100% of market traffic mix.

attributes.name: created_timestamp
attributes.description: Timestamp when this market assessment record was first created in the system.

attributes.name: data_source
attributes.description: Source system or data provider for the market intelligence used in this assessment (e.g., MIDT, IATA statistics, GDS data, internal BI, third-party market research).

attributes.name: destination_airport_code
attributes.description: Three-letter IATA airport code for the destination city in the O&D (Origin-Destination) market pair.

attributes.name: growth_trend_percent_yoy
attributes.description: Year-over-year growth trend percentage for this market, indicating whether demand is growing, stable, or declining. Positive values indicate growth, negative indicate decline.

attributes.name: interline_opportunity_flag
attributes.description: Boolean flag indicating whether interline ticketing agreements with other carriers could support this market without direct service.

attributes.name: last_modified_timestamp
attributes.description: Timestamp when this market assessment record was last modified or updated.

attributes.name: leisure_traffic_percent
attributes.description: Percentage of total market traffic attributed to leisure travelers, complementing business traffic for total passenger segmentation.

attributes.name: market_maturity_stage
attributes.description: Lifecycle stage classification of the market (emerging, growth, mature, declining) used for strategic network planning decisions.

attributes.name: od_traffic_percent
attributes.description: Percentage of total traffic that is true O&D (Origin-Destination) point-to-point demand, as opposed to connecting traffic through a hub.

attributes.name: origin_airport_code
attributes.description: Three-letter IATA airport code for the origin city in the O&D (Origin-Destination) market pair.

attributes.name: peak_season_months
attributes.description: Comma-separated list of month names or numbers representing peak travel demand periods for this market (e.g., 'June,July,August' or 'December').

attributes.name: recommended_aircraft_type
attributes.description: Recommended aircraft type or family (e.g., A320, B737, B787) for operating this route based on demand, range, and economics.

attributes.name: recommended_weekly_frequency
attributes.description: Recommended number of weekly flight frequencies for this route based on the market assessment analysis, supporting schedule planning decisions.

attributes.name: revenue_opportunity_estimate_usd
attributes.business_glossary_term: Revenue Opportunity Estimate USD (United States Dollar)
attributes.description: Estimated annual revenue opportunity in USD for the airline in this market, calculated from market size, target share, and average fare assumptions.

attributes.name: seasonality_index
attributes.description: Seasonality index representing demand variation across the year, where 1.00 is average, >1.00 is peak season, and <1.00 is off-peak season.

attributes.name: slot_availability_destination
attributes.description: Slot availability status at the destination airport (available, constrained, unavailable), critical for slot-constrained airports under IATA WSG (Worldwide Slot Guidelines).

attributes.name: slot_availability_origin
attributes.description: Slot availability status at the origin airport (available, constrained, unavailable), critical for slot-constrained airports under IATA WSG (Worldwide Slot Guidelines).

attributes.name: total_market_passengers_annual
attributes.description: Total annual passenger volume (Pax) in the O&D market across all carriers, representing total market size for demand analysis.

attributes.name: vfr_traffic_percent
attributes.business_glossary_term: VFR (Visiting Friends and Relatives) Traffic Percent
attributes.description: Percentage of total market traffic attributed to VFR (Visiting Friends and Relatives) segment, a key demand driver in ethnic and diaspora markets.

products.name: operational_standard
products.description: Reference master defining operational time standards used in schedule construction and rotation planning for each route and aircraft type combination. Encompasses block time standards (gate-to-gate flight time including taxi, airborne, and seasonal wind adjustments), turnaround time standards (minimum and standard ground time by turnaround type), and component time allocations (cleaning, catering, fueling, boarding). Captures route, airport, aircraft type, direction, applicable season, and last review date. Serves as the single source of truth for all time-based parameters feeding Jeppesen rotation planning, crew duty time calculations, and OTP measurement baselines.

attributes.name: airborne_time_minutes
attributes.description: Standard flight time in minutes from takeoff to landing, including seasonal wind and weather adjustments.

attributes.name: applicable_season_code
attributes.description: IATA season code for which this operational standard is effective (e.g., S23 for Summer 2023, W23 for Winter 2023/2024).

attributes.name: approval_date
attributes.description: Date when this operational standard was formally approved for use in schedule planning and crew duty calculations.

attributes.name: approval_status
attributes.description: Approval status of this operational standard by authorized network planning or operations management personnel.

attributes.name: block_time_minutes
attributes.description: Standard gate-to-gate block time in minutes, including taxi-out, airborne time, taxi-in, and seasonal wind adjustments. Used as baseline for schedule construction and On-Time Performance (OTP) measurement.

attributes.name: boarding_time_minutes
attributes.description: Standard time allocated for passenger boarding, varies by aircraft capacity, load factor, and boarding process efficiency.

attributes.name: cargo_loading_time_minutes

attributes.name: cargo_unloading_time_minutes
attributes.description: Standard time allocated for cargo and baggage unloading upon arrival, varies by cargo volume and ULD count.

attributes.name: catering_time_minutes
attributes.description: Standard time allocated for catering service during turnaround, including galley restocking and waste removal.

attributes.name: cleaning_time_minutes
attributes.description: Standard time allocated for cabin cleaning during turnaround, varies by aircraft size and turnaround type.

attributes.name: confidence_level
attributes.description: Confidence level in the accuracy of this operational standard based on sample size, data quality, and operational stability. High confidence indicates robust historical data; low confidence may indicate new route or limited operational history.

attributes.name: created_timestamp
attributes.description: Timestamp when this operational standard record was first created in the system.

attributes.name: data_source
attributes.description: Source of the time standard data: historical performance analysis from actual flight operations, aircraft manufacturer specifications, industry benchmarks, or internal operational analysis.

attributes.name: deboarding_time_minutes
attributes.description: Standard time allocated for passenger deboarding upon arrival, varies by aircraft capacity and airport gate configuration.

attributes.name: direction
attributes.description: Direction of flight operation: outbound from origin to destination, or inbound from destination back to origin. Accounts for prevailing wind and operational differences.

attributes.name: effective_date
attributes.description: Date from which this operational standard becomes active and applicable for schedule planning and rotation construction.

attributes.name: expiry_date
attributes.description: Date on which this operational standard ceases to be applicable. Null indicates an open-ended standard.

attributes.name: fueling_time_minutes
attributes.description: Standard time allocated for aircraft refueling during turnaround, varies by fuel uplift volume and airport infrastructure.

attributes.name: last_modified_timestamp
attributes.description: Timestamp when this operational standard record was last updated or modified.

attributes.name: last_review_date
attributes.description: Date when this operational standard was last reviewed and validated by network planning or flight operations teams.

attributes.name: minimum_turnaround_time_minutes
attributes.description: Minimum allowable ground time in minutes for this aircraft type and station combination, used for tight connection planning and irregular operations (IROP) recovery.

attributes.name: next_review_date
attributes.description: Scheduled date for the next review of this operational standard to ensure continued accuracy and relevance.

attributes.name: notes
attributes.description: Additional notes, comments, or special considerations related to this operational standard, including operational constraints, seasonal factors, or airport-specific requirements.

attributes.name: sample_size
attributes.description: Number of actual flight operations analyzed to derive this operational standard. Larger sample sizes indicate higher statistical reliability.

attributes.name: seasonal_adjustment_minutes
attributes.description: Time adjustment in minutes applied to block time for seasonal wind patterns, weather conditions, and daylight variations. Can be positive or negative.

attributes.name: standard_status
attributes.description: Current lifecycle status of this operational standard. Active standards are used in production schedule planning; draft and under_review are pending approval; superseded indicates replacement by newer standard; archived for historical reference only.

attributes.name: taxi_in_time_minutes
attributes.description: Standard time in minutes from landing to gate arrival (on-blocks), accounting for airport layout and taxiway congestion.

attributes.name: taxi_out_time_minutes
attributes.description: Standard time in minutes from gate departure (off-blocks) to takeoff, accounting for airport congestion and ATC (Air Traffic Control) procedures.

attributes.name: turnaround_time_minutes
attributes.description: Standard ground time in minutes required between arrival and departure for aircraft servicing, including cleaning, catering, fueling, boarding, and maintenance checks.

attributes.name: turnaround_type
attributes.description: Classification of turnaround based on flight characteristics and service requirements. Determines resource allocation and time standards.

attributes.name: variance_minutes
attributes.description: Statistical variance in minutes observed in historical performance data, indicating operational variability and schedule buffer requirements.

products.name: block_time_standard

Captures route, aircraft type, direction (outbound/inbound), planned block time (minutes), taxi-out time, taxi-in time, airborne time, seasonal adjustment (summer/winter winds), and last review date. Block time standards are the foundation of crew duty time calculations, fuel planning, and OTP measurement.

attributes.name: atc_delay_factor_minutes

attributes.name: block_time_standard_status
attributes.description: Current lifecycle status of the block time standard. Active standards are used for schedule construction; inactive standards are historical; under_review standards are being validated; superseded standards have been replaced by newer versions.

attributes.name: contingency_buffer_minutes
attributes.description: Additional buffer time in minutes added to the planned block time to account for operational variability, ATC delays, weather, and other uncertainties. Used to improve schedule reliability and OTP performance.

attributes.name: crew_duty_time_minutes

attributes.name: data_source

attributes.name: destination_airport_code

attributes.name: direction
attributes.description: Direction of flight relative to the airline's hub or base. Outbound represents flights departing from hub; inbound represents flights arriving at hub. Block times may differ by direction due to prevailing winds and operational patterns.

attributes.name: effective_date

attributes.name: etops_time_adjustment_minutes
attributes.business_glossary_term: Extended-Range Twin-Engine Operational Performance Standards (ETOPS) Time Adjustment (Minutes)
attributes.description: Additional block time in minutes for ETOPS-certified routes requiring extended-range twin-engine operations. Accounts for required routing to remain within diversion distance of suitable alternate airports.

attributes.name: expiry_date

attributes.name: fuel_planning_time_minutes
attributes.description: Block time used for fuel planning calculations, which may differ from scheduled block time to ensure adequate fuel reserves for contingencies, alternate airports, and regulatory requirements.

attributes.name: historical_average_block_time_minutes
attributes.description: Historical average actual block time in minutes based on past flight performance data. Used for benchmarking and validating planned block time standards against operational reality.

attributes.name: last_modified_timestamp
attributes.description: Timestamp when this block time standard record was last modified. Supports change tracking, audit trail, and data governance requirements.

attributes.name: last_review_date
attributes.description: Date when this block time standard was last reviewed and validated against actual flight performance data. Block time standards should be reviewed regularly (typically quarterly or seasonally) to ensure accuracy.

attributes.name: next_review_date
attributes.description: Scheduled date for the next review and validation of this block time standard. Ensures proactive maintenance of block time accuracy and alignment with operational performance.

attributes.name: notes
attributes.description: Free-text notes capturing special considerations, operational constraints, seasonal factors, or other contextual information relevant to this block time standard. May include rationale for adjustments or known anomalies.

attributes.name: origin_airport_code

attributes.name: percentile_85_block_time_minutes
attributes.description: 85th percentile of historical actual block times in minutes. Represents the block time that 85% of flights achieve or beat. Used as a reliability target for schedule planning to balance OTP performance with schedule efficiency.

attributes.name: planned_block_time_minutes
attributes.description: Total planned gate-to-gate block time in minutes, representing the scheduled duration from gate departure (off-blocks) to gate arrival (on-blocks). This is the foundation for schedule construction, crew duty time calculations, and OTP measurement.

attributes.name: sample_size
attributes.description: Number of historical flight records used to calculate this block time standard. Larger sample sizes provide greater statistical confidence in the standard's accuracy and reliability.

attributes.name: seasonal_adjustment_type
attributes.description: Indicates whether this block time standard applies to summer season (typically March-October in Northern Hemisphere), winter season (typically October-March), or year-round. Seasonal variations account for prevailing winds, jet stream patterns, and daylight saving time impacts.

attributes.name: slot_constrained_adjustment_minutes
attributes.description: Additional time in minutes added to block time for slot-constrained airports where departure or arrival slot availability may require schedule padding to ensure slot compliance and reduce IROP risk.

attributes.name: standard_deviation_minutes
attributes.description: Standard deviation of historical block times in minutes, representing the variability and consistency of actual flight performance. Lower standard deviation indicates more predictable block times.

attributes.name: taxi_in_time_minutes
attributes.description: Planned taxi-in time in minutes from landing (wheels-down) to gate arrival (on-blocks). Varies by airport layout, gate assignment, and ground traffic.

attributes.name: taxi_out_time_minutes
attributes.description: Planned taxi-out time in minutes from gate departure (off-blocks) to takeoff (wheels-up). Varies by airport congestion, runway configuration, and time of day.

attributes.name: wind_adjustment_minutes
attributes.description: Adjustment in minutes to account for prevailing wind patterns, jet stream effects, and seasonal wind variations. Positive values indicate headwind penalties; negative values indicate tailwind benefits.

products.name: route_promotion
products.description: This association product represents the inclusion of specific routes in loyalty promotional campaigns. It captures the many-to-many relationship between loyalty promotions and routes, where a single promotion can target multiple routes (e.g., Triple miles on all Asia-Pacific routes) and a single route can be included in multiple concurrent promotions (seasonal campaign + new route launch + competitive response). Each record links one loyalty_promotion to one route with route-specific promotion parameters, performance tracking, and date overrides that exist only in the context of this relationship.. Existence Justification: Airlines routinely design loyalty promotions that target multiple specific routes simultaneously (e.g., Triple miles on all Asia-Pacific routes, Bonus miles on new European routes), and each route can be included in multiple concurrent promotions (seasonal campaign + new route launch + competitive response). Marketing teams actively manage these route-promotion associations as operational entities, tracking route-specific performance metrics (booking uptake, incremental revenue, competitive impact) and configuring route-level parameters (bonus multipliers, date overrides, priority ranks) that differ from promotion-level defaults.
products.reference: Internal - M:N Association

Captures occurrence classification (accident/serious incident/incident/occurrence), ICAO occurrence category (CICTT taxonomy), occurrence subtype with subtype-specific extended attributes, date/time/location, aircraft registration, flight phase, injury severity, damage level, narrative description, initial causal factors, reporting source, and regulatory notification status. Subtype-specific fields accommodate wildlife strike details (species, aircraft part struck, ingestion), runway incursion details (runway designator, severity category A-D), airspace deviation details (cleared vs actual values), and dangerous goods details (UN number, DG class, packaging failure). SSOT for all safety occurrence data across the airline.

Tracks the evolution of risk ratings over time as controls are applied. Aligns with ICAO Annex 19 risk management requirements.

attributes.description: Reference to the hazard being assessed. Links this risk assessment to the identified hazard in the SMS hazard register.

attributes.description: The formal risk assessment technique or framework applied (e.g., ICAO 5×5 Matrix, Bow-Tie Analysis, FMEA, HAZOP, Preliminary Hazard Analysis). Documents the analytical approach for audit and repeatability.

attributes.references: ICAO Annex 19 SMS Framework, Emergency Response Plan (ERP) Standards

attributes.name: duration_minutes
attributes.description: Total elapsed time of the drill exercise in minutes, from start to end.

attributes.name: erp_version_reference
attributes.description: Version identifier of the Emergency Response Plan (ERP) document that was being tested and validated by this drill.
attributes.references: ICAO Annex 19 SMS Framework, Emergency Response Plan (ERP) Standards

attributes.name: exercise_controller_name
attributes.description: Full name of the individual responsible for directing and controlling the drill exercise, typically a senior safety or emergency response manager.

attributes.name: external_agencies_involved
attributes.description: Comma-separated list of external organizations and agencies that participated in the drill (e.g., Airport Fire Rescue, Local Police, Emergency Medical Services, Hospital, Red Cross, Airport Authority).

attributes.name: improvement_action_count
attributes.description: Total number of improvement actions identified from the drill debrief that require follow-up and implementation.

attributes.name: improvement_actions_identified
attributes.description: Detailed list of corrective and preventive actions identified from the drill to enhance emergency response procedures, training, resources, or coordination. Each action should include description and responsible party.
attributes.references: ICAO Annex 19 SMS Framework, Safety Management System (SMS) Corrective Action Process

attributes.name: last_modified_timestamp
attributes.description: Timestamp when this emergency drill record was last updated or modified in the safety management system.

attributes.name: next_drill_due_date
attributes.description: Scheduled date for the next emergency drill of this type or at this station, based on regulatory requirements and internal safety management system (SMS) schedules.
attributes.references: ICAO Annex 19 SMS Framework, FAA Regulations, EASA Requirements

attributes.name: objectives_defined
attributes.description: Detailed list of specific learning and performance objectives established for the drill, aligned with Emergency Response Plan (ERP) competencies and regulatory requirements.
attributes.references: ICAO Annex 19 SMS Framework, Emergency Response Plan (ERP) Standards

attributes.name: objectives_met_count
attributes.description: Number of drill objectives that were successfully achieved during the exercise, as assessed by observers and the exercise controller.

attributes.name: objectives_not_met_count
attributes.description: Number of drill objectives that were not achieved or only partially achieved during the exercise.

attributes.name: observer_list
attributes.description: Comma-separated list of names and roles of individuals assigned to observe and evaluate the drill performance, including regulatory observers if present.

attributes.name: overall_performance_rating
attributes.description: Summary assessment of the drill performance across all objectives and participants. Reflects readiness and effectiveness of emergency response capabilities.

attributes.name: participant_count
attributes.description: Total number of personnel actively participating in the drill exercise, including airline staff, contractors, and external agency responders.

attributes.name: participating_departments
attributes.description: Comma-separated list of airline departments and external agencies participating in the drill (e.g., Flight Operations, Ground Ops, Maintenance, Airport Authority, Fire Rescue, Medical Services, Local Police).

attributes.name: participating_stations
attributes.description: Comma-separated list of IATA station codes for all airports and facilities participating in the drill, including remote coordination centers.

attributes.name: primary_station_code
attributes.description: Three-letter IATA airport code of the primary station where the drill is conducted. The lead location for the exercise.

attributes.name: regulatory_compliance_status
attributes.description: Assessment of whether the drill met regulatory requirements for emergency preparedness and response as mandated by applicable aviation authorities.
attributes.references: FAA Regulations, EASA Requirements, ICAO Annex 19

attributes.name: regulatory_observer_agency
attributes.description: Name of the regulatory authority or agency whose representative observed the drill (e.g., FAA, EASA, Transport Canada, national Civil Aviation Authority).
attributes.references: FAA Regulations, EASA Requirements, ICAO Annex 19

attributes.name: regulatory_observer_present
attributes.description: Indicates whether a representative from a regulatory authority (FAA, EASA, national CAA) was present to observe the drill.
attributes.references: FAA Regulations, EASA Requirements, ICAO Annex 19

attributes.name: report_completed_date
attributes.description: Date on which the formal drill report was completed and submitted to management and regulatory authorities as required.

attributes.name: report_submitted_to
attributes.description: Comma-separated list of internal departments and external agencies to whom the drill report was submitted (e.g., Safety Department, Executive Management, FAA, EASA, Airport Authority).
attributes.references: ICAO Annex 19 SMS Framework, FAA Regulations, EASA Requirements

attributes.name: scenario_category
attributes.description: High-level classification of the emergency scenario type being exercised. Aligns with Emergency Response Plan (ERP) scenario taxonomy.
attributes.references: ICAO Annex 19 SMS Framework, Emergency Response Plan (ERP) Standards

attributes.name: scenario_description
attributes.description: Detailed narrative of the emergency scenario being simulated in the drill, including incident type, location, scale, and key conditions (e.g., aircraft fire on gate, medical emergency in-flight, security threat, hazmat spill).
attributes.references: ICAO Annex 19 SMS Framework, Emergency Response Plan (ERP) Standards

attributes.name: sop_references
attributes.description: Comma-separated list of Standard Operating Procedure (SOP) document identifiers and version numbers that were exercised during the drill.
attributes.references: ICAO Annex 19 SMS Framework, Standard Operating Procedure (SOP) Version Control

products.name: performance_indicator
products.description: Safety Performance Indicator (SPI) and Safety Performance Target (SPT) master definitions used to monitor SMS effectiveness as required by ICAO Annex 19. Captures indicator code, indicator name, description, indicator category (lagging/leading), measurement unit, data source, calculation method, target value, alert threshold, warning threshold, measurement frequency, responsible department, and regulatory framework alignment (ICAO/FAA/EASA). Defines the KPI framework — actual measured values are stored in spi_measurement.
products.reference: ICAO Annex 19 SMS Safety Performance Indicator

attributes.name: performance_indicator_id
attributes.description: Unique identifier for the safety performance indicator definition. Primary key.

attributes.name: aggregation_method
attributes.description: The statistical method used to aggregate raw data into the indicator value (e.g., sum, average, count, rate, percentage, maximum, minimum). [ENUM-REF-CANDIDATE: sum|average|count|rate|percentage|maximum|minimum — 7 candidates stripped; promote to reference product]

attributes.name: alert_threshold
attributes.description: The threshold value at which an alert is triggered, indicating that the indicator has reached a critical level requiring immediate management attention and corrective action.

attributes.name: approval_authority
attributes.description: The role, position, or individual who approved this indicator definition for use in the SMS (e.g., Director of Safety, Accountable Executive, Safety Review Board).

attributes.name: approval_date
attributes.description: The date on which this indicator definition was formally approved for use in safety performance monitoring.

attributes.name: benchmark_source
attributes.description: Identifies the external benchmark or industry standard used for comparison (e.g., IATA Safety Report, peer airline group average, regional safety statistics). Null if no external benchmark is used.
attributes.references: IATA Safety Report, ICAO Safety Report

attributes.name: calculation_method
attributes.description: Detailed description or formula defining how the indicator value is calculated from source data. Includes numerator, denominator, and any normalization factors (e.g., incidents per 100,000 flight hours = (total incidents / total flight hours) * 100,000).

attributes.name: created_timestamp
attributes.description: Timestamp when this indicator definition record was first created in the system.

attributes.name: data_source
attributes.description: Identifies the operational system or data source from which the indicator data is collected (e.g., AMOS for maintenance events, Flight Operations Control for OOOI data, SMS database for occurrence reports).

attributes.name: easa_alignment_flag
attributes.business_glossary_term: European Union Aviation Safety Agency (EASA) Alignment Flag
attributes.description: Boolean flag indicating whether this indicator is explicitly aligned with EASA Part-ORO SMS requirements (True) or not (False).

attributes.name: effective_from_date
attributes.description: The date from which this indicator definition becomes effective and is used for safety performance monitoring.

attributes.name: effective_to_date
attributes.description: The date until which this indicator definition remains effective. Null if the indicator is currently active with no planned end date.

attributes.name: faa_alignment_flag
attributes.description: Boolean flag indicating whether this indicator is explicitly aligned with FAA SMS requirements and guidance (True) or not (False).

attributes.name: icao_alignment_flag
attributes.business_glossary_term: International Civil Aviation Organization (ICAO) Alignment Flag
attributes.description: Boolean flag indicating whether this indicator is explicitly aligned with ICAO Annex 19 SMS framework requirements (True) or is an airline-specific custom indicator (False).

attributes.name: indicator_category
attributes.description: Classification of the indicator as either leading (predictive, proactive measures such as safety audits completed or training compliance) or lagging (reactive, outcome-based measures such as accident rate or incidents reported).

attributes.name: indicator_code
attributes.description: Unique alphanumeric code assigned to the safety performance indicator for reference and reporting purposes. Typically follows organizational coding standards (e.g., SFT-001, OPS-1234).

attributes.name: indicator_description
attributes.description: Detailed explanation of what the indicator measures, its purpose within the SMS, and how it contributes to safety oversight and risk management.

attributes.name: indicator_name
attributes.description: Full descriptive name of the safety performance indicator as used in safety management reporting and dashboards.

attributes.name: indicator_status
attributes.description: Current lifecycle status of the indicator definition. Active indicators are in use for monitoring; inactive indicators are temporarily suspended; under_review indicators are being evaluated for changes; retired indicators are no longer used.

attributes.name: last_modified_timestamp
attributes.description: Timestamp when this indicator definition record was last modified or updated.

attributes.name: last_review_date
attributes.description: The date on which this indicator definition was last reviewed by the responsible authority or safety committee.

attributes.name: measurement_frequency
attributes.description: The frequency at which the indicator is measured and reported (e.g., daily, weekly, monthly, quarterly, annually, or real-time for continuous monitoring).

attributes.name: measurement_unit
attributes.description: Unit of measure for the indicator value (e.g., count, percentage, rate per 100,000 flight hours, days, hours). Defines how the indicator is quantified.

attributes.name: next_review_date
attributes.description: The date on which this indicator definition is scheduled for its next formal review.

attributes.name: notes
attributes.description: Free-text field for additional notes, clarifications, or context regarding the indicator definition, calculation nuances, or historical changes.

attributes.name: regulatory_framework
attributes.description: Identifies the regulatory framework(s) or standard(s) to which this indicator aligns, such as ICAO Annex 19, FAA SMS requirements, EASA Part-ORO, or national civil aviation authority mandates. May list multiple frameworks separated by semicolons.
attributes.references: ICAO Annex 19 SMS Framework, FAA SMS, EASA Part-ORO

attributes.name: reporting_level
attributes.description: Classification of the organizational level at which this indicator is primarily reported and monitored (operational for front-line teams, tactical for department managers, strategic for senior leadership, executive for board and accountable executive).

attributes.name: responsible_department
attributes.description: The department, division, or organizational unit responsible for monitoring this indicator, collecting data, and taking corrective action when thresholds are breached (e.g., Safety Department, Flight Operations, Maintenance).

attributes.name: review_frequency
attributes.description: The frequency at which this indicator definition is reviewed for continued relevance, accuracy, and alignment with safety objectives (e.g., quarterly, annually).

attributes.name: target_value
attributes.description: The target or goal value set for this indicator as part of the Safety Performance Target (SPT) framework. Represents the desired performance level the organization aims to achieve.

attributes.name: trend_analysis_enabled
attributes.description: Boolean flag indicating whether trend analysis and statistical process control are enabled for this indicator (True) or if it is monitored as a point-in-time value only (False).

attributes.name: version_number
attributes.description: Version number of the indicator definition, used to track changes to calculation methods, thresholds, or other parameters over time. Follows semantic versioning (e.g., 1.0, 1.1, 2.0).

attributes.name: warning_threshold
attributes.description: The threshold value at which a warning is issued, indicating that the indicator is approaching an unacceptable level and requires monitoring and potential intervention.

products.name: spi_measurement
products.description: Periodic measurement records for Safety Performance Indicators (SPIs) capturing actual measured values against defined targets and thresholds. Captures indicator reference, measurement period (month/quarter), measurement date, actual value, target value, alert threshold breached flag, warning threshold breached flag, trend direction, data quality flag, measurement notes, and responsible analyst. Enables SMS performance monitoring and regulatory reporting to FAA, EASA, and national CAAs.
products.reference: ICAO Annex 19 SMS SPI Measurement

attributes.name: spi_measurement_id
attributes.description: Unique identifier for the SPI measurement record. Primary key.

attributes.name: performance_indicator_id
attributes.description: Reference to the defined SPI being measured. Links to the SPI definition catalog.

attributes.name: primary_spi_employee_id
attributes.description: Reference to the safety analyst or employee responsible for recording and validating this SPI measurement.

attributes.name: actual_value
attributes.description: The actual measured value of the SPI for the measurement period. This is the primary quantitative result of the measurement.

attributes.name: alert_threshold_breached_flag
attributes.description: Boolean flag indicating whether the actual value breached the alert threshold for this measurement period. True indicates breach requiring immediate action.

attributes.name: alert_threshold_value
attributes.description: The alert threshold value for this SPI. When actual value crosses this threshold, it triggers an alert requiring immediate action.

attributes.name: approved_timestamp
attributes.description: The date and time when this SPI measurement was approved for publication or regulatory reporting.

attributes.name: corrective_action_required_flag
attributes.description: Boolean flag indicating whether this measurement result requires corrective action to be initiated. True when thresholds are breached or performance is unacceptable.

attributes.name: created_timestamp
attributes.description: The date and time when this SPI measurement record was first created in the system. Audit trail field.

attributes.name: data_quality_flag
attributes.description: Categorical flag indicating the quality status of the measurement data (verified, provisional, estimated, incomplete, suspect).

attributes.name: data_quality_score
attributes.description: A quality score (0-100) indicating the reliability and completeness of the measurement data. Higher scores indicate higher confidence in the measurement.

attributes.name: data_source_system
attributes.description: The name or identifier of the source system from which the measurement data was extracted (e.g., SMS database, FOQA system, maintenance system).

attributes.name: last_modified_timestamp
attributes.description: The date and time when this SPI measurement record was last modified. Audit trail field.

attributes.name: measurement_date
attributes.description: The date when the SPI measurement was recorded or calculated. Represents the business event timestamp for this measurement.

attributes.name: measurement_method
attributes.description: The method used to collect or calculate this SPI measurement (automated system, manual data entry, hybrid, calculated from other metrics).

attributes.name: measurement_notes
attributes.description: Free-text notes providing additional context, explanations, or observations about this SPI measurement. May include reasons for anomalies or data quality issues.

attributes.name: measurement_period_end_date
attributes.description: The end date of the measurement period covered by this SPI measurement.

attributes.name: measurement_period_start_date
attributes.description: The start date of the measurement period covered by this SPI measurement.

attributes.name: measurement_period_type
attributes.description: The frequency or type of measurement period for this SPI measurement (daily, weekly, monthly, quarterly, annual, ad-hoc).

attributes.name: measurement_status
attributes.description: The current lifecycle status of this SPI measurement record (draft, submitted for review, reviewed, approved, published).

attributes.name: published_timestamp
attributes.description: The date and time when this SPI measurement was published to stakeholders or submitted to regulatory authorities.

attributes.name: regulatory_reporting_required_flag
attributes.description: Boolean flag indicating whether this SPI measurement must be reported to regulatory authorities (FAA, EASA, national CAA).
attributes.references: ICAO Annex 19 SMS Framework, FAA, EASA

attributes.name: reporting_period_month
attributes.description: The calendar month (1-12) of the measurement period. Used for monthly aggregation and trend analysis.

attributes.name: reporting_period_quarter
attributes.description: The calendar quarter (1-4) of the measurement period. Used for quarterly aggregation and trend analysis.

attributes.name: reporting_period_year
attributes.description: The calendar year of the measurement period. Used for annual aggregation and regulatory reporting.

attributes.name: responsible_department
attributes.description: The department or organizational unit responsible for this SPI measurement (e.g., Flight Safety, Ground Safety, Maintenance Safety).

attributes.name: sample_size
attributes.description: The number of observations or data points used to calculate this SPI measurement. Relevant for rate-based or statistical SPIs.

attributes.name: target_met_flag
attributes.description: Boolean flag indicating whether the actual value met or exceeded the target value for this measurement period.

attributes.name: target_value
attributes.description: The target or goal value defined for this SPI during the measurement period. Used to assess performance against objectives.

attributes.name: trend_direction
attributes.description: The trend direction of the SPI compared to previous measurement periods (improving, stable, deteriorating, insufficient data).

attributes.name: unit_of_measure
attributes.description: The unit of measure for the SPI values (e.g., count, percentage, rate per 1000 flights, hours, incidents per million departures).

attributes.name: variance_from_target
attributes.description: The calculated variance between actual value and target value. Positive indicates performance above target, negative indicates below target.

attributes.name: variance_percentage
attributes.description: The variance from target expressed as a percentage. Calculated as ((actual - target) / target) * 100.

attributes.name: warning_threshold_breached_flag
attributes.description: Boolean flag indicating whether the actual value breached the warning threshold for this measurement period. True indicates breach requiring attention.

attributes.name: warning_threshold_value
attributes.description: The warning threshold value for this SPI. When actual value crosses this threshold, it triggers a warning requiring attention.

products.name: wildlife_strike
products.description: Wildlife strike occurrence records capturing bird and wildlife strikes as required by FAA Wildlife Strike Database reporting and ICAO circular 107. Captures strike date, airport ICAO code, flight phase (approach/takeoff/en-route/taxi), species identified, species quantity, aircraft part struck (engine/windshield/radome/wing/fuselage), damage level (none/minor/substantial/destroyed), effect on flight (none/aborted takeoff/precautionary landing/engine shutdown), ingestion flag, and FAA/ICAO report submission reference.
products.reference: FAA Wildlife Strike Database / ICAO Circular 107

attributes.name: wildlife_strike_id
attributes.description: Unique identifier for the wildlife strike occurrence record. Primary key.

attributes.name: aircraft_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to fleet.aircraft. Business justification: Wildlife strike damage assessment, repair tracking, and airworthiness restoration require linkage to specific aircraft. Enables analysis of aircraft vulnerability patterns (e.g., radome strikes on spe

attributes.name: destination_content_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to marketing.destination_content. Business justification: Wildlife strike patterns at specific airports inform destination content warnings or operational communications. Real business process: destination safety information for route planning and passenger

attributes.name: flight_leg_id
attributes.description: Reference to the specific flight leg during which the wildlife strike occurred.

attributes.name: general_ledger_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to finance.general_ledger. Business justification: Wildlife strikes generate repair costs, insurance claims, and AOG costs posted to GL. cost_estimate_usd and repair_hours fields require GL linkage for financial impact tracking and insurance claim rec

attributes.name: occurrence_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to safety.occurrence. Business justification: Wildlife strikes are a specific type of occurrence. Adding wildlife_strike.occurrence_id → occurrence.occurrence_id links wildlife strike records to their master occurrence record. Removes redundant o

attributes.name: occurrence_report_id
attributes.description: Reference to the parent safety occurrence report if this strike is part of a broader safety event investigation.

attributes.name: regulatory_requirement_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to compliance.regulatory_requirement. Business justification: Wildlife strikes have specific FAA/ICAO reporting requirements (FAA Form 5200-7). Links strike records to regulatory reporting obligations, ensuring timely submission and compliance with wildlife haza

attributes.name: repair_order_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to procurement.repair_order. Business justification: Wildlife strikes cause aircraft damage requiring vendor repairs. Linking strikes to repair orders supports cost tracking, insurance claims, regulatory reporting to FAA/ICAO, and analysis of repair tur

attributes.name: aircraft_out_of_service_hours
attributes.description: The total number of hours the aircraft was out of service due to the wildlife strike, including inspection, repair, and testing time.

attributes.name: aircraft_part_struck
attributes.description: The specific part or component of the aircraft that was struck by the wildlife. [ENUM-REF-CANDIDATE: engine|windshield|radome|nose|wing|fuselage|landing_gear|tail|propeller|rotor|other|unknown — 12 candidates stripped; promote to reference product]

attributes.name: altitude_feet
attributes.description: The altitude of the aircraft in feet above ground level (AGL) or mean sea level (MSL) at the time of the wildlife strike.

attributes.name: corrective_action_required_flag
attributes.description: Indicates whether corrective actions are required as a result of this wildlife strike. True if actions required, False otherwise.

attributes.name: cost_estimate_usd
attributes.business_glossary_term: Cost Estimate in United States Dollars (USD)
attributes.description: The estimated total cost of the wildlife strike including aircraft repair, operational disruption, and other direct costs, expressed in USD.

attributes.name: created_timestamp
attributes.description: The timestamp when this wildlife strike record was first created in the system, in yyyy-MM-ddTHH:mm:ss.SSSXXX format.

attributes.name: damage_level
attributes.description: The severity level of damage sustained by the aircraft as a result of the wildlife strike, following FAA damage classification standards.

attributes.name: effect_on_flight
attributes.description: The operational impact of the wildlife strike on the flight, including any immediate actions taken by the crew.

attributes.name: engine_ingestion_flag
attributes.description: Indicates whether the wildlife was ingested into one or more aircraft engines. True if ingestion occurred, False otherwise.

attributes.name: faa_report_number
attributes.description: The unique report number assigned by the FAA Wildlife Strike Database upon submission of the strike report.

attributes.name: icao_report_reference

attributes.description: The reference number or identifier for the wildlife strike report submitted to ICAO under Circular 107 reporting requirements.

attributes.name: indicated_airspeed_knots
attributes.description: The indicated airspeed of the aircraft in knots at the time of the wildlife strike.

attributes.name: investigation_status
attributes.description: The current status of any safety investigation triggered by this wildlife strike occurrence.

attributes.name: last_modified_timestamp
attributes.description: The timestamp when this wildlife strike record was most recently updated or modified, in yyyy-MM-ddTHH:mm:ss.SSSXXX format.

attributes.name: pilot_warned_flag
attributes.description: Indicates whether the pilot was warned of wildlife presence prior to the strike. True if warning was issued, False otherwise.

attributes.name: precipitation
attributes.description: The type of precipitation present at the time of the wildlife strike, if any.

attributes.name: regulatory_reportable_flag
attributes.description: Indicates whether this wildlife strike meets the threshold for mandatory regulatory reporting to FAA or other civil aviation authorities. True if reportable, False otherwise.

attributes.name: remains_collected_flag
attributes.description: Indicates whether wildlife remains were collected for species identification or analysis. True if collected, False otherwise.
